summary: KEP-3498 proposes extending the Kubernetes metrics stability framework with two new stability classes, `beta` and `internal`, and narrows the meaning of `alpha` to the nascent stage of a KEP-proposed feature. The KEP is at implementable status, stage beta.
rationale: The existing framework only distinguishes `stable` and `alpha` metrics, so feature metrics at intermediate stages get no guarantees or full stability. The KEP adds classes that mirror feature release stages and separates internal low-level metrics from feature metrics. The readme ties this to PRR requirements for production readiness metrics.
alternatives: Doing nothing — The readme calls it a viable alternative but says it leaves feature metrics with no guarantees or fully stable, which it presents as an odd position.

Forced upgrades of metrics stability classes in the alpha version — The readme defers this to the beta version of the KEP, so the alpha version only adds the classes without changing existing metrics.

evidence.quote: This KEP intends to propose additional stability classes to extend on the existing metrics stability framework, such that we can achieve parity with the various stages of the feature release cycle.
Introduce two more metric classes: `beta`, corresponding to the `beta` stage of feature release, and `internal` which corresponds to internal development related metrics.
We also propose amending the semantic meaning of an `Alpha` metric such that it represents the nascent stage of a KEP-proposed feature

For the alpha version of this KEP, we will implement the necessary changes to Kubernetes metrics framework, such that it supports the additional classes of metrics, without making changes to any existing metrics or their stability levels.

The KEP was withdrawn at alpha stage in v1.33 after the containerd changes did not work out and the requesting users found other solutions.

The maintainer later said the containerd changes never worked as intended and the users asking for this had found alternatives, so the KEP was deprecated.

summary: KEP-3515 proposed switching kubectl explain's data source from OpenAPI v2 to OpenAPI v3 and replacing the hand-written printer with a go/template implementation, with a fallback to the v2 implementation. The KEP is now implemented at stage beta.

summary: KEP-3521 adds a `.spec.schedulingGates` field to Pod so integrators can mark a Pod as not yet ready for scheduling; the scheduler parks gated Pods until all gates are removed. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Pods are considered schedulable once created, so Pods waiting on missing resources or external criteria keep churning the scheduler and downstream tools such as Cluster Autoscaler. The gates field lets users and controllers hold Pods out of scheduling until ready, without marking them Unschedulable. Discussion then focused on how gates interact with spec.nodeName, the format of the field, and downgrade behavior.
alternatives: Boolean `.spec.schedulingPaused` field — The readme says it "cannot support multiple independent controllers to control specific aspect a Pod's scheduling readiness."

Blocking spec.nodeName while scheduling is paused — Commenters raised that a human admin or client may intentionally set nodeName to force placement, and that unaware schedulers need predictable behavior; the discussion did not settle on a hard block.

Keep gates as a flag rather than a list (readiness-gate style) — The thread moved toward a list-based format, with one option similar to finalizers and another similar to readinessGates; the sources do not show a final choice beyond the readme's `.spec.schedulingGates` list.

summary: KEP-3541 proposes a new `Recreate` update strategy for StatefulSets, mirroring Deployments' Recreate strategy: delete all pods, wait for full termination, then create new pods according to podManagementPolicy. The KEP is at implementable status, stage alpha.
rationale: With RollingUpdate, a pod that never reaches Ready (bad config, resource limits) halts the update, and the controller does not replace it even after a corrected config is applied, forcing manual deletion. The Recreate strategy gives a simple, predictable way to recover stuck pods for workloads that can tolerate downtime. It is opt-in and explicitly leaves the default update behavior unchanged.
alternatives: Keep RollingUpdate and rely on maxUnavailable or Parallel podManagementPolicy — The readme says that with maxUnavailable the controller still requires each pod to reach Ready, and with Parallel 'stuck pods remain and are not automatically replaced.'
Add timeout-based progressive failure detection — The KEP lists it as a non-goal: 'Add timeout-based progressive failure detection (use Recreate for simplicity)'.

summary: KEP-3545 adds a kubelet option (topology-manager-policy-options, prefer-closest-numa-nodes) so the TopologyManager favors NUMA node sets with shorter distances when comparing equal-sized sets. It was implemented and graduated to stable, with status marked implemented from 2025-02-03.

summary: KEP-3573 Device Plugins (sig-node) added a vendor-independent mechanism for kubelet to discover, health-check, and allocate vendor devices (e.g. GPUs) via gRPC device plugins. Its status is implemented, stage stable, with Device Manager graduated to stable in v1.26.

summary: KEP-3619 proposes a new SupplementalGroupsPolicy API field so users can control which supplemental groups (including those from /etc/group in the image) are attached to the first container process, instead of changing the existing default behavior. The KEP is recorded as implemented and stable.
rationale: Container runtimes (containerd, CRI-O) merge groups from the image's /etc/group into the first process, which is not OCI-compliant and lets image authors bypass supplemental group policy. The sources show the design discussion and approval; they do not show the implementation rollout details beyond the status history.

summary: KEP-3633 adds MatchLabelKeys and MismatchLabelKeys to PodAffinityTerm so users can scope which Pods are evaluated for required and preferred Pod (anti-)affinity, typically during rolling upgrades. The KEP has reached stable and is marked implemented.
rationale: During rolling upgrades, old and new Pod versions co-exist, and the scheduler cannot tell them apart, so PodAffinity and PodAntiAffinity can block new Pods in a full cluster or filter out valid Nodes in an idle one. The KEP lets users scope affinity evaluation using label keys whose values are set by other systems. Per the discussion, kube-apiserver folds these fields into LabelSelector, so kube-scheduler needs no new logic.
alternatives: Add new operators (ExistsWithSameValue, ExistsWithDifferentValue) to the podAffinityTerm label selector — Proposed by huang-wei in review; the sources do not record it being rejected explicitly, but the design moved on to matchLabelKeys plus notMatchLabelKeys, aligned with PodTopologySpread.

Keep matchLabelKeys and add notMatchLabelKeys alongside matchLabelSelectors — Chosen direction: sanposhiho preferred it because the API field is similar to PodTopologySpread and easier for users to understand. The sources do not say the alternative was rejected in a formal vote.

Gate the scheduler on the feature flag by reading MatchLabelSelectors directly — Not chosen: sanposhiho said kube-apiserver generates LabelSelector from MatchLabelSelectors, so kube-scheduler computes affinity as before and does not depend on the feature gate.

evidence.quote: This enables users to finely control the scope where Pods are expected to co-exist (PodAffinity) or not (PodAntiAffinity), on top of the existing `LabelSelector`.
makes both easier for users to understand instead of making a difference (matchLabelKeys vs matchLabelSelectors) between them to specify a similar thing.
The kube-apiserver generates `LabelSelector` from `MatchLabelSelectors` and kube-scheduler computes PodAffinity/PodAntiAffinity as it does now.

Given that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, once all the work is completed (including removing feature gates), could you please update the KEP status in `kep.yaml` from `implementable` to `implemented`

summary: KEP-3638 lets kubectl fall back to external plugins (kubectl-<cmd>-<sub>) when a built-in subcommand does not exist, instead of returning an "unknown command" error. It is gated behind the KUBECTL_ENABLE_CMD_SHADOW environment variable; current status is implementable at stage beta.
rationale: SIG CLI receives many requests to add subcommands to built-in commands such as kubectl create for new resources, including CRs, but adding them statically increases binary size and maintenance burden. The proposal lets plugins fill that gap for subcommands that do not exist, and reviewers limited shadowing to avoid overriding built-ins. The sources also record a concern that a future built-in could shadow an existing plugin, which the design answers with an env-var-based force escape hatch.
alternatives: A new --use-plugin flag to explicitly invoke a plugin, allowing shadowing of existing subcommands — The KEP judges it hurts usability without gain: users must pass the flag every time, the flag cannot be passed to plugins, and there is no clear use case for shadowing existing subcommands.

Using both a flag and an env var for enablement and the force-plugin escape hatch — Reviewer soltysh preferred keeping only an environment variable for alpha and beta, since the env var is more appropriate for these cases than a flag.

Warning users when a newly added built-in shadows an existing plugin name — Ardaguclu noted it would require checking for external plugins on every command, which is a downside; the sources do not record it being adopted.

I'd suggest not using flag and env variable, but only keep the env var for alpha and beta.
Once this mechanism is fully stable, it'll be fully acceptable to shadow some sub-commands, but not all.

summary: KEP-3659 proposes a second, independent alpha of kubectl apply --prune based on a low-level "ApplySet" grouping specification (labels and annotations on a parent object), replacing the existing alpha prune implementation. Its status is implementable at stage alpha, from 2023-02-09.
rationale: The current --prune flag has design flaws: it cannot reliably identify previously applied objects and is slow and surprising. The KEP stores the set membership metadata on a parent object so pruning can be driven by a stable set rather than by re-deriving it from the manifests. Reviewers pushed back on scope and on storing deletion state in cluster objects, but the KEP's stated primary goal is a correct and efficient prune, with ecosystem interoperability as secondary.
alternatives: Minimal fix to kubectl apply --prune, without a plumbing layer — Reviewer seans3 argued for minimizing scope to the minimum a user needs; the KEP instead kept the plumbing/porcelain specification, and the discussion records justinsb saying ecosystem goals are secondary to correct prune.

Local prune-list kept outside the cluster — Raised by liggitt; justinsb replied that users have not shown interest in that model and would need extra tooling to track the list, so cluster-stored state was kept.
Full GKNN listing with UID (no retrieval of previously applied objects) — seans3 noted this would perform better than the KEP approach, but the sources do not say it was adopted or rejected.

Server-side resource for the ApplySet — johnbelamaric suggested making it not client-side only; soltysh indicated the SIG was preparing to create a server-side resource, but the sources do not record a decision to implement one in this KEP.

evidence.quote: The new implementation is based on a low-level concept called "ApplySet" that other, higher-level ecosystem tooling can build on top of
MUST use a pruning set identification algorithm that remains accurate regardless of what has changed between the previous and current sets
The applyset object is not expected to be stored in the manifests. For kubectl, it is specified via a flag
I think a lot of the complexity comes in because we're trying to avoid creating a new server side resource.

summary: KEP-3668 proposes subdividing the NodePort service port range into a reserved block for static port assignment and a dynamic block, so users can create NodePort Services with static ports with less risk of conflict. The KEP is implemented and stable.
rationale: Users need well-known, predefined NodePort numbers, but dynamic allocation can already have taken a port before a static NodePort Service is created. The design splits the NodePort range so static and dynamic allocations do not collide, modeled on KEP-3070 for Cluster IPs. The stated goal is to allow a static NodePort with less risk of port conflict, and the non-goals exclude changing the allocator implementation or adding new configuration flags.
alternatives: Keep a single shared NodePort range for static and dynamic allocation — The summary notes that without a split, there is no way to know before creating a static NodePort Service whether another dynamic NodePort has already taken the port.
Change the allocator implementation (bitmaps, etc.) — Listed as a non-goal of the KEP.
Add new configuration options or flags — Listed as a non-goal of the KEP.

evidence.quote: The NodePort Service port range can be logically subdivided to avoid the risk of conflict between NodePort that use static and dynamic port allocation.

The idea is mostly the same with [Reserve Service IP Ranges (KEP-3070)](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/3070-reserved-service-ip-range#release-signoff-checklist) did.
Currently, there is no possibility, before creating a NodePort Service with a static port, to know if the port has been chosen already by any other NodePort using dynamic allocation.
- allow to create a Service with a static NodePort with less risk of port conflict.

## Non-Goals
- changing the allocators implementation (bitmaps, ...). - add new configuration options or flags.

summary: KEP-3673 adds a node-level kubelet limit, maxParallelImagePulls, capping the number of image pulls in flight at once, with defaulting and validation rules tied to the existing serialize-image-pulls setting. Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Kubelet pulled images serially by default, and there was no node-level cap when parallel pulls were enabled. The KEP adds maxParallelImagePulls so operators can allow parallel pulls while bounding node disk and network load. Reviewers noted the limit counts images, not layers, and that runtimes such as containerd and CRI-O limit layers per image separately. Later comments reduced the proposed default from 5 to 2 for parallel pulls, which the sources show as a planned change rather than confirmed final behavior.
alternatives: Leave parallel image pull limits to the container runtime (e.g., per-registry limits or containerd MaxConcurrentDownloads) — Reviewers raised this (tzneal) but the KEP author replied that limiting on kubelet 'can address the problem without runtime support', and containerd's MaxConcurrentDownloads limits layers per image, not overall pulls.

Default parallel pulls to unbounded (no limit) when serialize-image-pulls=false — wojtek-t said 'unbounded' is bad and that switching to MaxImagePulls=2 when unset seemed helpful, though the sources say that change would need a second beta.

Change the default from serialized to parallel pulls at GA — wojtek-t argued changing the default behavior affects administrators unaware of image pulls, and said the mitigation is for admins to configure parallel pulls themselves.

evidence.quote: A new integer field `maxParallelImagePulls` will be added to Kubelet Configuration. `maxParallelImagePulls` is the maximum number of inflight image pulls.
Paco is right. This limit will only limit the number of images, not layers. This is because kubelet does not have any visibility over layers.
Limiting the image pulls on kubelet can address the problem without runtime support.
I agree that "unbounded" is bad and switching to MaxImagePulls=2 in such case (if someone didn't set it explicitly) seems helpful.
So disabling serial pulls and making defaul parallel pulls to 2 sounds good.

summary: KEP-3685 moves the EndpointSlice reconciler and its dependencies from pkg/controller/endpointslice into staging/src/k8s.io/endpointslice so out-of-tree controllers can import it as a Go module, with public NewReconciler/Reconcile, a configurable managedBy label, and split diff-computation from diff-application. Status: implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Custom EndpointSlice controllers struggle to implement the fan-out reconciling correctly, and forked or rewritten copies of the reconciler are hard to support. Sharing a maintained library also eases migration from Endpoints to EndpointSlices for custom controllers. The KEP accepts added maintenance burden from splitting code across pkg/controller and staging as the cost.
alternatives: Externalize the entire EndpointSlice controller and use alternate data sources (informers) to customize behavior. — The readme lists this only as an alternative and gives no stated reason for rejecting it.
A generic solution for reconciling fan-out style resources. — Listed as a non-goal; the readme does not give a reason beyond scoping it out.
Letting a Service opt out of the in-tree EndpointSlice controller. — The readme says this was considered and determined to be out of scope, without further reasoning.

summary: KEP-3695 extends the kubelet PodResources API so that node monitoring agents can see resources allocated to pods by Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). The KEP is recorded as implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Node monitoring agents had no way to learn which DRA-allocated resources pods on a node hold. The KEP extends the PodResources API from 2043 and 2403 to expose that data. It explicitly excludes changing GetAllocatableResources(), because DRA has no standard way to report capacity. Reviewers also asked for the Get() behavior on non-running pods to be specified, and the author agreed to add that in a follow-up.
alternatives: Change GetAllocatableResources() to account for DRA-managed resources — Excluded as a non-goal: "With DRA there is no standard way to get the capacity, for example."

Delay the KEP until DRA reaches beta — Klueska argued that "I don't want to block this work on DRA reaching beta, because these APIs are needed for an important use-case of DRA". The feature gate was instead chained to the DRA gate.

Have Get() return an error for terminated but non-deleted pods — Proposed by ffromani as one option for the semantics; the sources do not record a final choice between the two options, and the discussion closed with a request to document one of them.

evidence.quote: To enhance the GetAllocatableResources() call in the PodResources API to account for resources managed by DRA. With DRA there is no standard way to get the capacity, for example.
I don’t want to block this work on DRA reaching beta, because these APIs are needed for an important use-case of DRA and are therefore useful in their own right

summary: KEP-3705 extends kubelet --node-ip so that clusters using an external cloud provider can specify dual-stack node IPs (including IPv4/IPv6 family selectors), and defines how kubelet passes that intent to the cloud provider via the provided-node-ip annotation. Status is implemented, stage stable.

The KEP limits the change to --node-ip values that older kubelets would have rejected, leaving default behavior unchanged. summary: KEP-3715 allows spec.completions of an Indexed Job to be mutated, but only when the new value equals spec.parallelism and both fields change together. The KEP reached implemented status and stable stage.
rationale: Indexed Jobs need a stable index range for workloads like MPI, Ray, and PyTorch that autoscale, but spec.completions was immutable. The KEP treats completions and parallelism as one scalable unit for these workloads, so completions can change only in tandem with parallelism. Failure counting is kept for scaled-down jobs, and the Job API is preferred over StatefulSet for its batch features.
alternatives: Model the workload as a StatefulSet — The KEP says the Job API is a better fit because it offers batch-specific features such as running indexes to completion and pod and container failure handling.
Make spec.completions mutable for NonIndexed jobs as well — NonIndexed mode behavior is an explicit non-goal and is not changed by this KEP.

there is no distinction between the concept of "how many completed indexes do I need" (i.e., `spec.completions`) and the concept of "how many pods do I want running at a time"
While such workloads could be modeled as a StatefulSet, the Job API is a better fit because it offers batch-specific features
Failures will always count. If `spec.completions` was scaled down, then previous pod failures outside the new range will still count against the job's backoffLimit.

summary: KEP-3716 adds "match conditions" (CEL expressions) to admission webhook configurations, extending `rules` so a webhook is only called when every expression evaluates to true; otherwise the request is implicitly allowed. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Admission webhooks are a reliability and latency problem: webhooks sit in the critical request path even when they do no work, and existing scoping (rules, namespace selectors) is insufficient for some cases such as excluding managed components. Match conditions narrow which requests reach a webhook, and the KEP keeps them consistent with ValidatingAdmissionPolicy's CEL model. Reviewers agreed the feature is an optimization, with the core business logic remaining in the webhook backend.
alternatives: An `exclusions:` field with inverted CEL expressions — Reviewers said "We should _not_ use `exclusions`" because it "inverts the meaning of the CEL expressions in a way that makes them more confusing"; the author chose matchConditions instead.

Rely on namespace selectors or existing scoping mechanisms — The KEP states the existing criteria "are insufficient for many use cases", and a reviewer noted namespace scoping only partly covers the need ("With careful use of namespace, I would expect this to be possible today").

Use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy for these cases — The KEP says ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "is intentionally not attempting to cover every possible use case", and this proposal "aims to improve the situation for those webhooks that cannot be migrated."

Cross-webhook match conditions applied globally — The author made this out of scope: "I decided to make this out-of-scope for this KEP, since I think it expands the scope quite a bit", and it was listed as future work.

evidence.quote: A `matchCondition` is a [CEL](https://github.com/google/cel-spec) expression that must evaluate to true for the admission request to be sent to the webhook.
If a `matchCondition` evaluates to false, the webhook is skipped for that request (implicitly allowed).
Yes. We should _not_ use `exclusions`; we should (I propose) list it as an alternative that we rejected, and explain why.
I decided to make this out-of-scope for this KEP, since I think it expands the scope quite a bit, but we should definitely discuss it in the future.
Since this feature is intended as an optimization, if the matchCondition is not run (e.g. on old clusters that don't support the field) the behavior is expected to be equivalent

summary: KEP-3720 proposes freezing the old k8s.gcr.io image registry so that no new digests or tags are pushed after the 1.27 release, with all new images published exclusively to registry.k8s.io. The status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Running public image registries is very expensive and consumes a significant part of the project's infrastructure budget. The project is exceeding its budget because end users will take a long time to upgrade to v1.25, so freezing the old registry by 1.27 is meant to push users to registry.k8s.io sooner. Registry.k8s.io is GA and community-controlled, and the redirect from k8s.gcr.io did not work out.
alternatives: Redirect k8s.gcr.io to registry.k8s.io — The readme says a plan to redirect k8s.gcr.io to registry.k8s.io 'didn't work out', so the project backported the new registry defaults to 1.24, 1.23 and 1.22 instead.
Keep pushing new images to the old registry — The readme lists this as the alternative, but the project is exceeding its infrastructure budget, so the freeze is proposed instead.

evidence.quote: Running public image registries is very expensive and eats up a significant chunk of the project's Infrastructure budget.
we want to incentivise our end users to move to the new registry as fast as possible by freezing the registry by 1.27.
Freeze the `k8s.gcr.io` image by not pushing any new digests or tags after 1.27 release.
There was a plan to redirect `k8s.gcr.io` to `registry.k8s.io` but it didn't [work out]

summary: KEP-3721 adds the ability to populate a container's environment variables from a file, initially restricted to files in an emptyDir volume read by kubelet. Its status is implementable, targeting stable.
rationale: Existing ConfigMap and Secret env mechanisms need extra API calls when an initContainer produces configuration, and vendor images need env vars from files. The KEP lets kubelet read an env file from an emptyDir and instantiate the variables without mounting the file in the consuming container. Reviewers raised concerns about precedence, security of arbitrary volumes, and scope, which shaped the emptyDir-only design.
alternatives: Populate env vars from a ConfigMap or Secret resource — The readme says this proposal 'allows populating environment variables from a file in container filesystem and thus reducing the need of an API call or extra permissions to kube-apiserver.'

Read all variables from a file without naming them (EnvFromSource-style) — This is listed as a non-goal: 'We do not intend to support instantiating all variables from an env file ... without knowing their names a priori.'

Allow any volume type rather than only emptyDir — Sergey Kanzhelev said emptyDir was picked because 'it doesn't have any secrets', and the thread records that expanding beyond emptyDir was not agreed for the current scope. Later proposals (ephemeral volumes) were still under discussion, not adopted.

Restrict the volume source on the producer side only — thockin argued 'A volume is a volume. We shouldn't add new restrictions on mounting it,' and suggested restricting on the consumer side instead, which the discussion accepted as making sense.

evidence.quote: Support instantiating a container's environment variables from a file. This file must be in emptyDir volume.
this proposal allows populating environment variables from a file in container filesystem and thus reducing the need of an API call or extra permissions to kube-apiserver.
Adding the "only emptyDir" restriction on the CONSUMER side makes sense.

This is why emptyDir was picked - it doesn't have any secrets. If you would to expand emptyDir, do you have some suggestions on how this can be limited to some more useful, but still secure set of supported types?
The file will be read by kubelet at container startup time. It will be re-read if the container restarts.

summary: KEP-3726 rephrases the Service port appProtocol field description and declares standard kubernetes.io-prefixed protocol names (e.g. kubernetes.io/h2c) for common protocols that are not IANA service names. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: The appProtocol field only pointed to IANA service names or domain-prefixed names, so implementations gave the same value different meanings (HTTP2 means TLS in GKE but h2c in Istio). The proposal fixes this by defining well-known kubernetes.io-prefixed names for common protocols. The sources state the goals of building consensus and helping implementations interoperate, but do not give further reasons for the chosen approach.
alternatives: Keep IANA service names or domain-prefixed names only — The motivation says this loose definition led implementations to do different things for common protocols, such as HTTP2 in GKE versus Istio.
Support multiple appProtocol values for the same port — It is listed as a non-goal, suggested as follow-up work.

summary: KEP-3744 proposes a process for updating supported Kubernetes release-1.x branches to build and release with new minor versions of Go, so patch releases use a supported Go version while preserving their stability and compatibility. Status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Kubernetes release branches historically stayed on one Go minor version, so the last months of each minor version's 14-month support window could lack Go security fixes. Go changes that break behavior made backporting risky, and the KEP's answer is a staged process: land prerequisite changes on the development branch, backport low-risk ones to release branches, and only then move release branches to the new Go minor version once conditions are met.
alternatives: Request the go team backport security fixes to more than two minor versions — The percentage of patch releases containing security-related content has risen in recent years, so "security fixes only" would not necessarily mean fewer patch releases on older minor versions; not all security fixes can be cleanly backported.

Maintain a custom patched version of older go minor versions with security fix backports — It is not clear that all changes with security implications would be consistently noticed and backported, and staffing a fork would be an ongoing cost; a custom distribution also loses benefits of the standard widely tested distribution and could confuse security scanners.

evidence.quote: Because of this inconsistency, Kubernetes release branches historically remained on a single go minor version, and risked being unable to pick up go security fixes
Update release-1.x branches to build/release using go 1.N once all of these conditions are satisfied
Prioritize making the prereq changes as minimal and low-risk as possible. Merge those changes to the default Kubernetes development branch *prior* to updating to go 1.N.
go 1.N has been released at least 3 months
The primary drawback is risk of a user-facing regression in a patch release due to a go version change.

summary: KEP-3751 proposes a VolumeAttributesClass API so users can change volume performance attributes (IOPS, throughput) on existing volumes online via a PVC reference, without using cloud provider APIs directly. Its status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Kubernetes had no API to change volume IO attributes after provisioning; only capacity could be expanded, and StorageClass parameters are immutable. The KEP adds a VolumeAttributesClass object whose name can be changed on a PVC, letting parameters be updated after creation. The discussion shows many open design questions (quota during modification, driver capability reporting, default VAC behavior) that were raised during review, and the sources do not record how each was finally resolved.
alternatives: Keep using StorageClass parameters and provider APIs directly — Kubernetes does not handle updates of volume attributes other than capacity, so users must call the cloud provider API directly; the readme calls this a friction the KEP aims to remove.

Make StorageClass parameters mutable — A commenter notes it is difficult to make the StorageClass parameters field mutable and impossible to make the PVC storageClassName mutable, so a new object was introduced.

Add a catch-all map[string]string attributes field only — Raised in review by ameade as a question of the value of first-class fields; the sources do not record a final decision beyond the KEP adding first-class fields for throughput and iops and an optional attributes field discussed in comments.

evidence.quote: Kubernetes has no API which allows changing them. Only capacity can be changed through the volume expansion API.

summary: KEP-3756 reverses the kubelet startup order so VolumeManager first reconstructs the actual state of world (ASW) from the host OS and /var/lib/kubelet/pods, then completes it with API server data. It was gated behind feature gate NewVolumeManagerReconstruction and split out of KEP-1710 so it could graduate separately. Status is implemented, stable.

The KEP reconstructs all found volumes from the OS without requiring the API server, so the ASW records real mount details such as mount options, which KEP-1710 needs. It also aims to fix #105536 (volumes not unmounted after restart) and make volume cleanup more robust.
alternatives: Keep reconstruction inside KEP-1710 as one feature — The readme says the work 'can be useful outside of SELinux relabeling and could graduate separately', so it was split out with its own feature and gate.

Ship directly without a feature gate — The readme says 'it changes large parts of kubelet, and we'd like to have it behind a feature gate to provide users a way to get to the old implementations in case of problems.'
Graduate through alpha first — The owner stated 'We're going directly to beta', since the alpha phase already happened under KEP-1710.

evidence.quote: we'd like to have a separate feature + feature gate to be able to graduate VolumeManager reconstruction faster
We propose to reverse the kubelet startup process. 1. Quickly reconstruct ASW from the OS and add **all** found volumes to ASW when kubelet starts as *uncertain*.

summary: KEP-3762 adds a PersistentVolumeStatus field holding the timestamp of when a PersistentVolume last transitioned to a different phase. The API server strategy code sets it on each phase change. Status is implemented, stage stable.

summary: KEP-3836 proposes that kube-proxy fail its healthz (and the cloud load balancer health check) for terminating Nodes, signalled by the ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler taint, so load balancers can drain connections; it also adds a /livez path that keeps the old healthz semantics. The KEP is implemented and stable.
rationale: For externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster services, kube-proxy's healthz only reports whether data-plane programming is stale, so a terminating Node keeps receiving load-balancer traffic and in-flight connections are cut off. The KEP makes kube-proxy report unhealthy when the Node is being deleted, using the cluster autoscaler taint as the signal because .spec.unschedulable would break ingress for cordoned clusters. A separate /livez endpoint lets vendors keep a liveness probe that is unaffected by node termination.
alternatives: Use .spec.unschedulable as the termination signal — Users can cordon all nodes at a given moment, which would cause ingress traffic for all eTP:Cluster services to break.
Align cloud provider health checks for eTP:Cluster services — Non-goal: cloud providers have valid reasons to implement health checks differently; the KEP instead proposes a guidance document.
Include healthz state in eTP:Local health check answers — Treated as a bug to fix directly rather than through the KEP cycle, per the non-goals section.

evidence.quote: Given that the CA taints the Node which is to be downscaled and deleted, with the taint: `ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler` it would seem most appropriate to use that here.
Using `.spec.unschedulable` as this signal would cause ingress traffic for all `eTP:Cluster` services to break.
adds a `/livez` path to its health check server (`proxier_health.go`) corresponding to the old healthz semantics
if we modify `/healthz` to fail when this taint gets added on the Node, then the `livenessProbe` will fail, causing the Kubelet to restart the Pod until the Node is deleted.

summary: KEP-3838 proposes relaxing Pod node selector and node affinity immutability so that gated pods (blocked on a scheduling readiness gate) can have their scheduling directives further constrained. Status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: External resource controllers need to influence where a pod lands while leaving pod-to-node binding to kube-scheduler. Node affinity and selector were immutable, so the KEP allows changes only for pods still blocked by a scheduling gate and only when the change further constrains placement. Reviewers narrowed the rule to appending to existing matchExpressions/fieldExpressions and to new preferred terms, and required nodeName/schedulingGates validation to be unconditional.
alternatives: Allow mutating node affinity/selector of pods unconditionally — Listed as a non-goal; the KEP restricts the change to pods blocked on a scheduling readiness gate.

Restrict adding tolerations on scheduling gates — Non-goal: tolerations are already allowed unconditionally, so restricting them to gated pods would not be backward compatible.

summary: KEP-3850 extends Indexed Jobs so the backoff limit applies per index rather than shared across the Job, letting the Job continue when some indexes fail. It also adds a FailIndex action to PodFailurePolicy to fail an index early. Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: With a single shared backoff limit, one failing index causes the whole Indexed Job to be marked failed and its unfinished indexes cleaned up. This breaks embarrassingly parallel workloads, such as integration test suites where each index is independent. The KEP proposes a per-index backoff policy and a FailIndex action so failed indexes stop retrying while others keep running.
alternatives: Keep a single shared backoff limit for all indexes — The readme says the current shared limit marks the entire job as failed and cleans up unfinished indexes, which does not fit independent indexes.
Support per-index retry control when restartPolicy=OnFailure — This is listed as a Non-Goal and is handled in a separate section of the KEP.

evidence.quote: When the job reaches this shared backoff limit, the job controller marks the entire job as failed, and the resources are cleaned up, including indexes that have yet to run to completion.
We propose a new policy for running Indexed Jobs in which the backoff limit controls the number of retries per index.
called FailIndex, to short-circuit failing of the index before the backoff limit per index is reached.
Other popular batch services like AWS Batch use a separate backoff limit for each index, showing that this is a common use case that should be supported by Kubernetes.

summary: KEP-3857 proposed making read-only volumes recursively read-only (RRO) via the OCI "rro" bind mount option, which calls mount_setattr(2) with MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY and AT_RECURSIVE, requiring kernel >= 5.12 and runc >= 1.1 or crun >= 1.4. The KEP is recorded as implemented and stable.
rationale: A readOnly volume's submounts (e.g. /mnt/usbstorage under /mnt) remain writable, which can compromise data. The design uses the OCI rro option so that read-only bind mounts become recursively read-only, and the reviewers stressed that the default behavior must not change silently because that would break existing workloads. The status is implemented at stable, so the sources support the approach being adopted, though the excerpt does not show the final API shape.

Silently convert readOnly into RRO when possible, with a warning when not possible — A reviewer wrote that this would make an app work on one day and fail the next after a node upgrade, and that 'our tolerance for silently breaking people ... is approximately zero'.

Use a tri-state readOnlyMode or recursivelyReadOnly enum (Disabled/IfPossible/Required) instead of a boolean — Discussion went back and forth on this. The thread notes that 'status is mostly needed because there is no guarantee that it will be applied' and that an IfPossible option would need status reporting. The thread concluded with a simpler proposal: keep readOnly as a bool and add an RRO enum field that is set only when readOnly is true.

evidence.quote: The "rro" bind mount options is implemented by calling [`mount_setattr(2)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mount_setattr.2.html) with `MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY` and `AT_RECURSIVE`
We can't make "Maybe" be the default because RRO is a user-visible behavior change, which could break workloads. The default HAS TO BE the historical behavior, codified.
1) leave `readOnly` as (non-pointer) bool 2) add RRO as enum-string with default value when `readOnly` is true
we can't change RO to mean RRO because that would break someone who deopends on the current behavior.

summary: KEP-3866 proposes a new, officially supported nftables-based backend for kube-proxy on Linux, alongside the existing iptables and ipvs backends. Its status is implemented, stage stable.

summary: KEP-3895 added an interactive flag (--interactive / -i) to kubectl delete. It previews the resources to be deleted and asks the user to confirm with y before deleting. The KEP is marked implemented and stable.

summary: KEP-3926 proposes a way to identify resources that fail decryption or decoding, and adds a new delete option that lets a client delete such a resource through the Kubernetes API without direct etcd access. Its status is implementable at stage beta.
rationale: If one object of a resource type cannot be decrypted, listing that type under a prefix containing it always fails, and today only direct etcd manipulation can remove it. summary: KEP-3935 extends the supported node-to-control-plane version skew from n-2 to n-3, so kubelet and kube-proxy from the oldest supported minor version work with control plane components from the newest. summary: KEP-3939 adds an opt-in Job spec field so replacement Pods are created only after previous Pods fully terminate, instead of as soon as they are terminating, and adds a Job status field counting terminating Pods.
rationale: Jobs currently start replacement Pods once existing Pods have a deletionTimestamp or phase=Failed, and terminating Pods are counted as failed. This causes replacements to fail to start for frameworks like TensorFlow and JAX that need unique Pods per index, and can trigger unwanted scale-ups or resource contention. The KEP makes the waiting behavior opt-in and exposes terminating Pods in status so users and queueing controllers like Kueue can see them.
alternatives: Put the behavior under PodFailurePolicy — The KEP says "We discussed having this under the PodFailurePolicy but this is a more general idea than the PodFailurePolicy."

Keep the existing behavior with no change — The sources do not record a direct rejection; the motivation describes problems with immediate replacement such as replacement pods that "immediately fail to start".

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes a new field for the Job API that allows for users to specify if they want replacement Pods as soon as the previous Pods are terminating (existing behavior) or only once the existing pods are fully terminated (new behavior).
Currently, if a pod enters a terminating state (due to preemption, eviction or other external factors), a replacement pod is created and immediately fail to start.
As an opt-in behavior, the job controller can use the active and terminating pods to determine whether replacement Pods are needed.
2. A new field in Status for tracking the number of terminating pods.

summary: KEP-3960 adds a built-in sleep action to the PreStop lifecycle hook, letting a container pause for a set duration before termination. The KEP reached stage stable and is marked implemented.

Allow a zero-second sleep value — Raised in comment 2209320166 as a possible extension requiring a feature gate and a short KEP. The sources do not show it was adopted.

summary: KEP-3962 proposes mutating admission policies declared in CEL, as an alternative to mutating admission webhooks, building on the validating admission policy work in KEP-3488. The KEP is recorded as implemented and at stable stage, with implementable status from 2024-02-08 and implemented status from 2026-05-21.

summary: KEP-3973 proposes adding a new status field, status.terminatingReplicas, to both Deployments and ReplicaSets so that the number of managed terminating pods is visible. It is observability only; scaling and rollout behavior are explicitly out of scope. The KEP is currently implementable at stage beta.
