summary: KEP-3998 extends the Job API so an Indexed Job can be declared succeeded under a declared success policy, either when a set of specified indexes succeed or when a count of indexes succeed. When a policy is met, a new SuccessCriteriaMet condition is added and lingering pods are terminated. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Indexed Jobs are currently marked Completed only when all indexes succeed, which does not fit workloads such as MPI and PyTorch where only leader indexes determine success. The readme cites third-party frameworks (Kubeflow Training Operator, Flux Operator, JobSet) that already implemented their own success policies. The KEP adds a success policy to the Job API to address this, at the cost of more complexity in deciding when a Job terminates.
alternatives: Support SuccessPolicy for NonIndexed Jobs — Listed as a non-goal: "Support SuccessPolicy for the job with `NonIndexed` mode" was excluded from the first iteration because there are no effective use cases for NonIndexed jobs.

Keep current behavior where an Indexed Job completes only if all indexes succeed — The motivation states this is "currently not possible" for workloads that only care about leader indexes, so the existing behavior does not meet the need.

evidence.quote: This KEP extends the Job API to allow setting conditions under which an Indexed Job can be declared as succeeded.
This is currently not possible because the indexed job is marked as Completed only if all indexes succeeded.
we don't work on the job with `NonIndexed` mode in the first iteration since there aren't any effective use cases for the NonIndexed job.
Then, when the job meets one of the success policies, a new condition, `SuccessCriteriaMet,` is added.

summary: KEP-4004 deprecates the status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion field of v1.Node and has kubelet stop setting it (set to empty string instead), protected by a feature gate. Status is implemented with the feature gate disabled by default.
rationale: The field is inaccurate because kubelet sets it but does not know the kube-proxy version or whether kube-proxy runs. The KEP marks it deprecated and has kubelet write an empty string, using a feature gate until other components stop depending on it. Default-enabling was delayed because the field is in a stable API, so the removal period from the 1.29 announcement had to pass (liggitt's comment).
alternatives: Have kube-proxy itself set status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion — Listed as a non-goal; components should not infer Service features from the kube-proxy version because some clusters run alternative service proxies.
Change v1.Node validation to require the field be unset — Listed as a non-goal in the KEP.

Promote to beta and default-enable in 1.31 — liggitt noted that clearing a stable API field requires a minimum one-year period from the 1.29 announcement, so 1.33 was the earliest default-on; the 1.31 enablement was reverted.

evidence.quote: The proposal is to deprecate the `kubeProxyVersion` field of `NodeStatus`, and to have kubelet set it to an empty string, rather than the kubelet version, in the future.
Thus, we will use a feature gate to protect it until all components are fixed.
because this is clearing population of a stable API field, the minimum period from announcement (in 1.29) is 1 year, so 1.33 is the earliest this can default to clearing.
I think it would stay as-is for 1.32 and default-enable in 1.33
the Feature Gates status has already been updated in PR https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/50783

summary: KEP-4006 moves kubectl exec, attach, cp and port-forward streaming from SPDY/3.1 to WebSockets, first for the kubectl-to-API-server leg, with the API server translating or tunneling to SPDY upstream. Status is implementable, stage beta.
rationale: SPDY is deprecated and many proxies, gateways and load balancers no longer support it, which blocks clients behind those intermediaries. WebSockets is a standardized protocol, and HTTP/2 was rejected because it does not support streaming Upgrade requests. The API server translates WebSocket to SPDY so kubelet and runtimes need no change in the first phase, and the Kubelet leg was moved to Pre-GA after reviewer request.
alternatives: Use HTTP/2.0 for streaming — The KEP says HTTP/2.0 specifically does not support Upgrade requests to create a streamable connection, so it was not adopted.

Negotiate the protocol within a single request using X-Stream-Protocol-Version headers — The reviewer (jpbetz) suggested it, but the author said the extra round trip was justified; the server's ability to handle both upgrades was accepted as fine for clients to make two round trips.

Ship port-forward in the same release as exec, attach and cp — The author excluded port-forward from the first release to reduce scope; maintainers agreed to incremental delivery, with port-forward added later.
Route all WebSocket traffic through the new StreamTranslatorProxy — The author proposed delegating only the v5.channel.k8s.io RemoteCommand requests, so other WebSocket and SPDY users are unaffected.

evidence.quote: The SPDY streaming protocol has been deprecated since 2015, and by now many proxies, gateways, and load-balancers do not support SPDY.
Finally, WebSockets is preferrable to HTTP/2.0 because the updated HTTP standard does not support streaming well.
In this way, the cluster components upstream from the API Server will not initially need to be changed.
I have modified the KEP to schedule extending WebSocket to the Kubelet from `Post-GA` to `Pre-GA`.
we are excluding `port-forward` from this release in order to reduce the scope of our effort and finally make some tangible progress.

summary: KEP-4008 proposes a CRDValidationRatcheting feature gate that lets updates to custom resources succeed when validation errors fall only on unchanged keypaths, so CRD authors and Kubernetes can widen or tighten value validations without breaking existing objects. The KEP is implementable and at stable stage.
rationale: Tightening a CRD value validation today makes any update to an existing object fail, even when the invalid field was not changed, which discourages adding validation. The proposal ratchets validation so only errors on changed keypaths block writes. Reviewers asked for a restricted scope: leaf value validations are ratcheted while anyOf/allOf/oneOf/not and transition rules are not, because the general case is hard to make correct and performant.
alternatives: Ratchet validation by mapping field paths from string error paths back to old and new objects — alexzielenski moved away from this: "I've moved the original plan to use string field path based approach to alternatives." The new plan evaluates old and new pairwise during traversal.

Ratchet all nested value validations (anyOf, allOf, oneOf, not) and transition rules — sttts recommended restricting ratcheting to leaf validations, noting that nested validations "are not common, and they usually don't overlap". jpbetz and benluddy agreed transition rules are not practical to ratchet, since they would need the resource two states back.

Offline one-off process to convert existing etcd resources to pass new validation — alexzielenski argued it "wouldn't solve the main goal of the KEP" because authors and users would both need to track which changes need manual repair.

Opt-in ratcheting via CRD extension or cluster-level flag — The KEP authors leaned toward applying it to all CRDs; the discussion says "open to making it opt-in" but does not record a final choice on opt-in.

evidence.quote: When enabled, this flag allows updates to custom resources that fail validation to succeed if the validation errors were on unchanged keypaths.
My gut feeling is that to make this whole KEP feasible we should heavily restrict the OpenAPI validation constructs we can ratchet.
I'm in favor of not providing ratcheting for transition rules.
Hence, we will move those cases out of the feature gate that we are comfortable with.
This does change the current behavior which would block an update containing an unchanged field that now fails validation. I think it is worth the tradeoff.

summary: KEP-4009 adds an optional CDI device ID field to the Device Plugin API's ContainerAllocateResponse so device plugins can pass fully-qualified CDI device names through the kubelet to CRI runtimes. The KEP status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Device plugins had no explicit way to request CDI devices, so vendors relied on workarounds such as container annotations. The new field lets the CRI field added in #3731 carry device IDs to runtimes without requiring users to adopt DRA. Reviewers debated whether the field needed its own feature gate; the thread records the team's position that the change is an optional field on a stable API, with a gate added later in alpha at reviewers' request.
alternatives: Pass CDI devices from the kubelet to the runtime using container annotations — The discussion says the intent is to use the new CRI field so device IDs stay opaque and the kubelet need not know the runtime version or configuration; annotations were raised as an alternative but not adopted. The thread also notes that for containerd, CDI and CDI annotations must be enabled, which the field approach shifts to device plugin vendors.

Ship the field with no feature gate, as with the cpu_ids addition to PodResources (KEP-1884) — Reviewers (enj, johnbelamaric) objected that a new field needs a feature gate. The authors then updated the KEP to add an alpha feature gate, though the thread says the field itself cannot be gated in protobuf.

Go directly to beta with the feature gate enabled by default — Raised by elezar as an option, referencing a precedent KEP. The thread does not record it being adopted; the KEP was changed to alpha on 2023-06-15.

evidence.quote: adding a field to specify Container Device Interface (CDI) device IDs in the `AllocateResponse`. This supplements the existing fields such as annotations

This keeps these devices IDs opague and does not require any interaction by the Kubelet. At present the Kubelet (at least in my cursory inspection of the code) doesn't perform any other such processing
I have updated the KEP to add this as an alpha feature.
@bart0sh please ensure then that this CRI fields does not depend in an alpha feature https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3731
Does it make sense to close this issue now that it has reached GA, or should we wait until the feature gate has been removed?

summary: KEP-4017 proposes setting the pod index as a label on pods created by StatefulSet controllers (apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index) and by Indexed Job controllers (batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index). The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: The pod index was only available as a StatefulSet pod name suffix, which requires parsing, or as a Job annotation, which the downward API can expose but which cannot be used for selection, metrics/log filtering, or traffic routing. Making the index a label allows selectors and the downward API to use it. The stated goal is that adding the label should not disrupt existing workloads.
alternatives: Keep parsing the StatefulSet pod name to learn the ordinal — The readme calls pod-name parsing a hacky solution and notes the index cannot be used by the downward API or for filtering and routing.
Keep the Indexed Job completion index only as an annotation — The readme says annotations cannot easily be used for selecting pods or filtering metrics/logs, which is the gap the KEP addresses.

evidence.quote: Indexed Jobs set the pod index as an annotation, which means it can be utilized by the downward API, however, it cannot easily be used for selecting pods based on their index
we propose to set the pod index as a **label** on pods for both StatefulSets and Indexed Jobs
Adding the label should not be disruptive to existing workloads.
StatefulSet pod label: `apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index` - IndexedJob pod label: `batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index` (same as existing annotation)

summary: KEP-4020 (Unknown Version Interoperability Proxy, later called Mixed Version Proxy) proposes that during upgrades or downgrades an apiserver proxies requests for built-in resources it does not serve to a peer apiserver that can, and merges aggregated discovery across peers. Its status is implementable, stage beta, with implementable from 2023-06-14.
rationale: During version skew, clients can get 404s for resources that exist elsewhere in the cluster, and incomplete discovery can cause controllers to act wrongly, such as blocking namespace deletion or garbage collecting objects by mistake. The design routes requests to a capable peer and returns 503 when the peer is unreachable, and it merges discovery so that it matches what the cluster can serve. The sources do not give a separate rationale for the move to beta; the status history only records the implementable date.
alternatives: Serve 503s without proxying, or merge discovery without proxying — The readme says merely serving 503s does not solve the problem, and proxying without merged discovery also does not fix it completely; both are needed.

Store peer IP info in the APIServerIdentity lease object — Discussion notes that users could then edit this info unless a webhook blocks them; the masterlease reconciler was preferred as safer, though the final decision was to write to both masterleases and v1.Lease objects.

Add a new discovery endpoint for peer-aggregated discovery — The readme says all discovery changes are implemented at the existing aggregated discovery endpoint /apis, with no new discovery endpoints introduced.

Enforce that the feature requires --peer-ca-file to be set — A reviewer argued the feature should be enabled even without apiserver networking, where the only difference is 503 instead of 404; the sources do not record a final resolution beyond the flag being required per the 2023-06-06 comment.

evidence.quote: ensures that: 1. Client requests for a specific built-in resource are proxied to an API server capable of serving it, avoiding 404 Not Found errors
Likewise proxying but not merging the discovery document, or merging the discovery document but serving 503s instead of proxying, doesn't fix the problem completely.
You are not guaranteed that apiservers will be able to talk to each other in the first place (i.e. firewall rules), so falling back to 503 (instead of 404ing) seems reasonable to me.
I think this would work well and I think the security profile on it is ok since cluster-admins will be able to specify an egress dialer.

summary: KEP-4026 adds a batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp annotation to Jobs created by a CronJob, recording the original expected scheduled time. The KEP reached implemented status and stable stage.
rationale: There was no supported way to get the original or expected scheduled timestamp for a Job created from a CronJob. The CronJob controller sets this value as a Job annotation. The design chose this approach so that adding the annotation would not disrupt existing workloads.
alternatives: Add a label instead of an annotation — Labels are unnecessary because the data is not used with search or to satisfy conditions.

Add a status field — The object's CreationTimestamp would be overridden with the time the CronJob starts, so the original scheduled time would be lost; the new annotation is meant to carry that original/expected value.

evidence.quote: Currently, there is no supported way to get the original/expected initial scheduled timestamp for the job created from a cronjob.
Adding the annotation should not be disruptive to existing workloads.
Labels are unnecessary as we need to pass data that won't be used with search or satisfy certain conditions.
The object already has the `CreationTimestamp` field, but it will get overridden with the time the CronJob will start.

summary: KEP-4033 lets the container runtime tell the kubelet which cgroup driver (cgroupfs or systemd) to use over CRI, so the kubelet no longer needs its own cgroupDriver setting. The status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Kubelet and the container runtime each had a cgroup driver setting, and mismatches caused hard-to-diagnose container creation failures and inconsistent resource allocation. SIG Node chose to make the CRI implementation the source of truth for this low-level choice. Discussion settled on a feature gate (KubeletCgroupDriverFromCRI), with kubelet falling back to its own setting when the runtime does not support the feature, and deprecating the kubelet setting later.
alternatives: Make kubelet the configuration point and have the CRI implementation guess the driver from the CgroupParent path in RunPodSandboxRequest — SIG Node decided the CRI implementation should be the source of truth for low-level choices like this, so this approach was not chosen.

Ship the change straight to beta with the feature gate enabled by default — John Belamaric would not approve going straight to beta and asked for an alpha phase, so the KEP was retargeted to alpha. The source does not describe the later stage transitions beyond the status.

Add a manual opt-out so the kubelet setting can override the runtime — Maintainers argued that the settings must match, so any override is misconfiguration. Haircommander said we should not provide an opt-out.
Remove the kubelet cgroup driver flag right away — Removing it would break users on older runtimes that do not support the new field, so the flag is kept as a fallback and marked deprecated.

evidence.quote: This removes the need for specifying cgroup driver in the kubelet configuration and eliminates the possibility of misaligned cgroup driver configuration between the kubelet and the runtime.
However, SIG Node has decided that the CRI implementation should begin to be the source of truth for low-level choices like this, and thus this approach was chosen.
I've updated the enhancement to target to alpha. Thanks for your feedback, PTAL

Changed to proposal to retain fallback behavior in GA, but, mark the the `--cgroup-driver` flag and the CgroupDriver config option as deprecated and eventually drop the according to the Kubernetes deprecation policy.
I don't think the kubelet should update the cgroup driver if the cri changes without a kubelet restart.

summary: KEP-4049 proposes extending the VolumeBinding scheduler plugin's node scoring to account for dynamic provisioning, based on free/allocatable storage capacity, with a global VolumeBindingArgs option to prefer nodes with least or maximum allocatable capacity (default: maximum). Current status is implementable, stage beta.
rationale: Scoring of nodes for PV provisioning only considered static (pre-created) PVs, so dynamic provisioning ignored free capacity; for local storage, admins want room for volume expansion or tighter packing. Reviewers raised concerns that summing static and dynamic scores could cancel out, so the design moved to scoring dynamic provisioning separately when static PVs are absent. Discussion also led to the feature gate being checked so that disabling it restores static-only scoring.
alternatives: Separate scores for static and dynamic provisioning (method A) — Discussed as more precise, but the author judged adding another scheduler plugin for dynamic-provisioned volumes to be going too far; a compromise implementation was chosen instead.

Weighted sum of static and dynamic scores (method B) — Reviewers (xing-yang) noted it gives the same weighted score regardless of individual scores; the author moved away from it toward method A-style separation.
Summing pre-created PV and dynamic provisioning scores — msau42 warned the scores could cancel each other out and lead to suboptimal placement and fragmentation for both configurations.

evidence.quote: Node scores based on available space can be taken into account when performing dynamic provisioning.
The default setting is to prefer a node with the maximum allocatable.
If we add the two scores together, then the two scores cancel each other out and it becomes a suboptimal choice for both configurations.
the current design separates the scores for static and dynamic provisioning to avoid
The lgtm label has been added. Could you please approve it if there are no issues?

summary: KEP-4080 proposes factoring kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager onto one or more new staging repositories (suggested k/generic-controlplane) that consume k/apiserver and carry a reusable subset of their generic functionality, excluding workload-specific resources. The KEP is in provisional status at stage alpha.
rationale: Kubernetes control planes bundle generic resources and controllers with container orchestration, which makes the generic parts hard to reuse. The proposal factors the generic parts into a library-style staging repo with a sample binary, moving code progressively without user-visible changes. Reviewers agreed the exact repo split would be decided during implementation, and the repo creation was deferred until the package structure is clear.
outcome_reason: Status is provisional, so the KEP has not been finalized or implemented. The sources do not explain the alpha stage choice beyond the reviewer note that the typical alpha/beta/GA process does not fully apply because the moved code is already GA.
alternatives: Split into separate generic-apiserver and generic-controller-manager repos — Raised by jpbetz as a possible split; sttts agreed it could be done and said it is to be discussed, so it was not settled in the sources.

Include a combined one-binary goal for apiserver and controller-manager — deads2k argued separate binaries have aged well and combining looks like a mistake; sttts disagreed, saying the goal does not force a topology and it belongs in the KEP. The disagreement was not resolved in the sources.
Create the staging repos now — sttts said the repos should wait until the code moves are done and the final package structure is clear.

evidence.quote: The factoring will be progressive: we will start with new repo(s) adding nothing to `k/apiserver`, refactor in-place and then progressively move generic functionality
yes, we wait. I put a sentence that we will decide when the final package structure through in-place moves is clear.
I think I'm OK with figuring out the exact split as we go, but I don't want sign off on just a single staging repo in the KEP
This appears to capture our goal of splitting out a "batteries included" generic apiserver.
State here that there will be no changes to system behavior and that the typical alpha/beta/GA doesn't entirely apply to this feature because the code being moved it all GA already?

summary: KEP-4153 proposed declaring Kubernetes native API validation rules via IDL tags (e.g. +minimum, +maximum, +validationRule) in types.go, with validation run against versioned types and published to OpenAPI. The KEP was accepted for alpha in October 2023 and later marked replaced (from 2025-02-13).
rationale: Hand-written validation is hard for users to access, review, maintain, and test, and is spread across roughly 15k lines of code. Declarative IDL tags aim to make rules inspectable, enable shift-left linting, and allow features like ratcheting to be implemented once. Reviewers accepted alpha on the condition of iterating, with several concerns raised about CEL readability and migration safety.
outcome_reason: The sources do not say why the KEP was replaced. The status history records only "replaced from 2025-02-13" with no successor KEP named.
alternatives: Validate the unstructured JSON/YAML instead of the deserialized Go struct — Discussion noted that defaulting happens on the typed object and that CEL has() semantics differ for empty fields, so validating unstructured would cause breaking changes that are hard to predict.

Keep validation hand-written in Go only — The motivation section states hand-written rules are hard to access, review, maintain, and test, and the goal is for 95%+ of them to be replaced with declarative validation.

Use a separate +validation annotation per rule instead of one map-shaped rule — Discussion settled on a list of rule maps, where multiple rules are ANDed together, so multiple annotations are already supported in that form.

evidence.quote: Kubernetes API validation rules are currently written by hand, which makes them difficult for users to access directly, review, maintain, and test.
I think this meets the bar for alpha. Do any reviewers have objections with us merging and iterating?
I agree this does not block alpha. I think it should prevent beta (on by default).
Alpha: Runs both systems, logs differences, admits based off of native validation

summary: KEP-4176 proposes a new CPUManager static policy option, `distribute-cpus-across-cores`, that prefers allocating CPUs from different physical cores on the same socket. The KEP status is implementable at stage alpha.
rationale: Workloads that get two hyperthreads of one physical core can suffer cache and noisy-neighbor effects, so the option spreads allocations across cores while still using the L2 cache on one socket. Reviewers agreed the change is small and self-contained, and the option was approved after the KEP freeze deadline was missed due to reviewer bandwidth. Reviewers required that the option's interaction with existing options (notably full-pcpus-only and distribute-cpus-across-numa) be documented before alpha.
alternatives: Add a new CPU manager policy instead of a policy option — A reviewer stated that it should be a policy option instead of a new one, and later clarified it is a new option, so existing feature gates are good enough.

Use NRI resource policy (Balloons, preferSpreadOnPhysicalCores) instead of changing the kubelet — Maintainers said the NRI plugins do not replicate the static policy 1:1 and the approach differs from the static policy; the reviewer said either approach could move forward, but they were in favor of changing cpumanager.

Make the option error out or implicitly switch behavior when combined with full-pcpus-only — A reviewer preferred treating the combination as a misconfiguration (error) for predictability, but the sources do not record a final decision on this; interaction was left as an open item.

evidence.quote: We propose to add a new `CPUManager` policy option called `distribute-cpus-across-cores` to the static CPUManager policy.
@klueska I accepted the change and I think that's makes it more clear.
It will move from being a `CPUManagerPolicyAlphaOption` to a `CPUManagerPolicyBetaOption` to not having a feature gate protecting it at all.
Please file an exception request for this feature, as per the insructions here
For alpha, we may just call it incompatible with everything else (but it will be much much nicer to have it elaborated), but past alpha we need a proper exploration here.

summary: KEP-4188 proposes a new read-only Kubelet gRPC API, served over a local UNIX socket restricted to local admin users, that returns local Pod information (initially Pod readiness/conditions) from the Kubelet's cache so node-local workloads can avoid depending on kube-apiserver. The KEP is at stage beta with status implementable.
rationale: Node-local consumers (e.g. networking components) need Pod state even when the control plane is unreachable, and polling kube-apiserver adds load and a control-plane dependency. The reviewers accepted that Pod readiness is safe to expose to same-node workloads, since the existing PodResources socket already works similarly, while sig-auth concerns about broader exposure led the authors to narrow the scope to readiness conditions. The status is implementable, and sig-node approvers signed off on the KEP.
alternatives: Add pod readiness endpoints to the existing PodResources API — The authors wanted to keep the API free of kube-apiserver authorization and avoid mixing it with allocated-resource data; a reviewer asked for pros/cons. Quote: "because our goal with this API is to reduce the Control Plane dependency we didn't wanted to add this to already existing API."
Use a REST API instead of gRPC — Listed as an option in the design tables, but the discussion does not record a reason it was rejected; the KEP stayed with gRPC.

Serve only data acknowledged by the control plane — Raised by a reviewer to avoid split-brain; the response was that the API will not override control-plane decisions and exists so nodes can work when the control plane is unavailable. Quote: "the proposed API won't be used to override any decision made by the control plane."

evidence.quote: The full PodSpec may contain sensitive information, so access to this API is secured by restricting the UNIX socket to local admin users only.
We already have a Pod resources API in Kubelet that is exposed in a similar way (via socket and therefore only accessible to other workloads on the same Node).
1) Read-only 2) throttling 3) limited to small set of information initially, for example, pod condition.
I updated the doc and changed all those places to point out that we want to expose readiness information.
Basically the proposed API won't be used to override any decision made by the control plane.

summary: KEP-4191 enhances kubelet to be aware that a container runtime may split the image filesystem from the container writable layer, so that image/container garbage collection and disk usage reporting keep working. The KEP is at implementable status for stage beta.
rationale: Separating image layers (read-only) from the container writable layer onto different disks would break kubelet garbage collection and statistics, which assume one image filesystem. The KEP adds kubelet support so these operations work when the runtime splits the filesystems. Reviewers focused on the scope of the first iteration and on runtime support, and the beta promotion was tied to passing e2e tests.
alternatives: Add separate ContainerFsStats and ContainerFsDevice fields instead of a shared containerfs field — Raised as a suggestion by ruiwen-zhao, considering future support for containerFs, imageFs and nodeFs on separate disks. The sources do not record a final decision to adopt it; the KEP instead added a containerfs field in NodeStats.

Have kubelet error and exit when the runtime does not return ImageFsInfo or container filesystem data — kannon92 said ImageFsInfo is implemented in both CRI-O and containerd, and that failing would break many regression tests. The chosen approach was to assume ImageFs=ContainerFs when the runtime does not report a separate container filesystem.
Move the stats from ImageService to RuntimeService — kannon92 replied that stats are already pulled from the image service in the stats providers, and the sources do not record a move.

evidence.quote: This KEP is about enhancing kubelet to be aware if a container runtime splits the image filesystem.
I will guard against that case. I'll mention that if the container runtime does not support this, then we will assume ImageFs=ContainerFs.
from our convo at WG meeting, isn't this in scope for alpha now?
my main concern with beta promotion is that e2e tests are not merged. I think promoting to beta should be contingent on these working.
we are adding a containerfs field in NodeStats

summary: KEP-4192 moves the Storage Version Migrator (SVM) controller in-tree into kube-controller-manager and moves its REST APIs in-tree under a new API group. Automatic migration is deferred to the user: the Migration resource is created manually rather than triggered automatically.
rationale: Rewriting stored data via no-op updates (kubectl get | kubectl replace) is impractical at scale, especially for large resources like secrets, and needs automation. The KEP keeps scope small by moving the existing out-of-tree controller in-tree and leaving automatic triggering to future work. Reviewers agreed on paginated lists for alpha, with the OOM/memory risk of watch-list or pagination to be resolved before beta.
alternatives: Use streaming watch (watch-list) for SVM's list operations in alpha — Reviewers noted watch-list does not support pagination/continue tokens and the approach was unproven; wojtek-t later said the plan of record is to not use it even after alpha.
Trigger migrations automatically from StorageVersion API hash changes — Explicitly deferred: 'For Alpha, we will not trigger automatic storage version migration, and it will be deferred to the user.'
Support continue tokens for resuming watch-list — wojtek-t and logicalhan objected that resuming a watch-list with a continue token has subtly different semantics and gives users foot guns.

evidence.quote: Move the existing SVM controller logic in-tree into KCM from its [original source](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-storage-version-migrator).
Automatic storage version migration will be deferred to the user.
How about we stick with paginated list for alpha and add a beta graduation criteria line item like
Okay, I think this answers my question. Can we make it super clear in the KEP that there will be no automatic triggering
PRR looks good, but I think we agree that "on by default" (beta), requires resolving the "this may cause kube-apiserver OOMs and cascading failure even for pagination values due to memory explosion".

summary: KEP-4193 adds a `node` claim (name and UID) to service account tokens issued by TokenRequest, and lets tokens be bound directly to a Node object. The KEP is now implemented and stable.
rationale: Verifying a projected Pod token's Node association required fetching the Pod object and cross-checking spec.nodeName, which is a gap for external verifiers wanting to prevent token replay across Nodes. Embedding the immutable Node name and UID in the signed JWT closes that gap. The sources record the design and the graduation path through beta to stable, with the enhancements team asking the owner to mark it implemented once feature gates are removed.
alternatives: Server without the feature gate ignores the node binding and validates only signature and SA existence — The discussion called this making tokens less secure when the gate is disabled, and the owner said "I don't like this option".

Server without the feature gate rejects node-bound tokens — The sources list it as an option requiring node-bound tokens not to be relied on until the upgrade is complete. The owner's leaning was toward option 3, not this one.

Server without the feature gate refuses to issue node-bound tokens but still accepts and validates them, using the node informer — This is the option the owner leaned toward ("I'd lean toward 3 or 3a"), so it is not rejected. The sources do not say it was the final choice.

Gate issuance and acceptance of node-scoped tokens separately, graduating validation before issuance (3a) — The owner mentioned this as a finer-grained variant but did not choose it. The sources do not say why it was not adopted.

evidence.quote: This will be implemented as an additional `node` entry in the private claims embedded into each JWT returned by the TokenRequest API
we will also add the ability to bind a token/JWT to a Node object directly, similar to how a token can be bound to a Pod or Secret resource today.
3. Server without feature gate does not allow creation of explicitly node-bound tokens but continues to accept/validate them if presented. Requires running the node informer.
Given that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, is all the work completed (including removing feature gates)?

summary: KEP-4205 proposes having the kubelet read cgroupv2 Pressure Stall Information (CPU, memory, IO) exposed via cAdvisor and runc, and expose pod-level PSI in the Summary API. The KEP is recorded as implemented and stable.
rationale: Node pressure conditions today are capacity-based (memory and disk) and there is no CPU or IO pressure condition, so PSI is proposed as an earlier signal of resource contention. The design says it "makes it possible to read PSI metric without installing additional dependencies". Discussion centered on phased rollout, per-slice reporting, and whether PSI should be gated separately; the maintainers settled on default-on without a separate feature gate for the stats reporting. The runc dependency was resolved by runc 1.2.0, which the source says is no longer a concern.
alternatives: Two feature gates, one for reporting PSI in status and one for turning it into node conditions — Suggested by tzneal; dropped because ndixita argued stats reporting wouldn't impact anything, and tzneal agreed: "That works for me as well and eliminates the need for a separate feature gate."

Add a kubelet config knob to disable PSI metrics to reduce metric cost — Reviewers said the cost can be handled by Prometheus metric filtering and future CRI stats granularity; haircommander said "if they don't want the metrics, don't enable PSI."
Ship the feature in an earlier release before the runc dependency landed — Deferred in June 2024 because "the runc dependency is not in yet"; the KEP was later pushed to a later release.

evidence.quote: This enhancement now makes it possible to read PSI metric without installing additional dependencies
Ah, I didn't realize you were planning on having them on by default without a feature gate. That works for me as well and eliminates the need for a separate feature gate.
Yes, since the runc dependency is not in yet. Please defer this KEP to next release.
If customers want to enable PSI, they get these metrics. if they don't want the metrics, don't enable PSI.

summary: KEP-4210 adds an optional Kubelet setting, ImageMaximumGCAge, plus a feature gate, so that images unused for a set time are garbage collected regardless of disk usage. Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Kubelet image GC only runs when disk usage crosses a threshold, so images from an old release (e.g. after an automatic upgrade) can sit on disk until then. The KEP adds an age-based trigger, defaulting to 0 (disabled), and the sources say it is opt-in and best-effort. Maintainers also raised reliability concerns, and sergeykanzhelev asked that the setting be explicitly documented as best effort; the sources do not record how those were resolved beyond the implemented status.
alternatives: Add a Kubelet garbage collection plugin system — Too complicated, probably won't be needed.
Delegate image GC responsibility down to CRI — Would cause code duplication between CRI implementations, out of scope for this.

Make ImageMinimumGCAge independent of the disk usage threshold — ImageGCMinimumAge is only relevant under disk pressure, and ImageMaximumGCAge seeks to qualify otherwise unqualified images; the authors found the distinction clear, and the backwards compatibility issues were judged not worth the config size savings.
Skip the alpha phase and go directly to beta — Raised by kannon92 as a question; the sources do not record a decision on it beyond the KEP being added with a feature gate.

evidence.quote: An additional approach is to define a way for an admin to request images are cleaned up after they're unused for a certain period of time.
To begin, this option will be set to 0, which will be interpreted as "disabled". In the future, a more reasonable default may be chosen.
afaict we still require a feature gate, even for optional fields like this one.
we should clearly state the best effort nature of this setting than - it will simplify the design.
One direction to go is to allow more granular configuration on what falls under this policy and what is not.

summary: KEP-4214 proposes that kubeadm stop binding the admin.conf credential to system:masters. Instead, admin.conf gets a regular cluster-admin credential via a new kubeadm:cluster-admins group, and a separate super-admin.conf holds the break-glass credential bound to system:masters. The KEP is in status implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: The system:masters group bypasses RBAC, so its permissions cannot be removed, and Kubernetes lacks certificate revocation. The only way to revoke such a credential is a CA rotation. Splitting the credential lets admin.conf be revoked with RBAC while a break-glass super-admin.conf remains for disruptive cases.
alternatives: Keep admin.conf bound to system:masters — The readme states that a credential bound to system:masters can bypass RBAC and that its permissions cannot be removed, so a compromised admin.conf can only be revoked by CA rotation.

Use the existing system:masters or kubeadm:cluster-admins groups for additional users — The proposal says using the existing system:masters or kubeadm:cluster-admins Groups will not be recommended; new users should get their own ClusterRoleBinding per User or Group.

evidence.quote: Binding an admin credential to the`system:masters` group means it can [bypass RBAC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubeadm/issues/2414#issue-836108390) - i.e. its permissions cannot be removed.
A general purpose `admin.conf` must be created that does not bind to `system:masters`. This credential can be shared by kubeadm deployed control plane nodes.
A separate "break-glass", super-user credential can be managed in `super-admin.conf`. This credential can be used to restore the cluster to a normal state in case of disruptive admin user activity.
To preserve the existing behavior where `admin.conf` has full cluster access, a new ClusterRoleBinding will be created called `kubeadm:cluster-admins`.

summary: KEP-4216 proposes identifying container images by a (imageName/imageDigest, runtimeClass) tuple in CRI, kubelet and related tooling, so that the same image reference can resolve to different manifests from an image index per runtime class. Its status is implementable at alpha, as of 2023-10-05.
rationale: The Windows platform matcher requires an exact host/guest OS version match, which breaks Hyper-V isolated containers whose UVM OS version differs from the host. Keying image pulls by runtime class lets the runtime select the manifest matching that runtime's guest platform. Scope was narrowed to kubelet and CRI changes, with container runtime implementation left to each runtime. The sources record no explicit reason beyond SIG Node approval for the alpha status.
alternatives: Pass only an OS version string (e.g. OSVersion) in the pod spec or runtime class — kiashok said passing osversion alone is not generic enough, and jsturtevant said version alone cannot distinguish process-isolated from Hyper-V runtimes.

Keep containerd-specific implementation details in the KEP — Reviewers (aravindhp, haircommander) said the containerd-specific changes are not as relevant, so they were removed and left to the runtimes.

Use a triplet of (image reference/digest, runtime class, OCI platform struct) as mikebrow suggested — The sources note mikebrow said either tuple or triplet works, and the KEP kept the tuple form; no source records a decision against the triplet.

evidence.quote: This problem can be fixed if container runtimes, CRI, and kubelet refer to images as a tuple of (imageName/imageDigest, runtimeClass) instead of the imageName/imageDigest.
Version isn't enough as we also would want to specify difference between process isolated and hyper-v runtimes.
We want this to be more generic for all platforms. For windows, this would be OSVersion but linux does not use OSVersion
I agree with @aravindhp that the containerd specific changes aren't as relevant. I think this should cover kubelet + cri changes

summary: KEP-4222 proposes CBOR as an alternative wire format for Kubernetes API clients and servers, and as the storage serialization for custom resources in apiextensions-apiserver, replacing JSON there. Its status is implementable at stage beta.
rationale: Custom resources cannot use Protobuf, which needs code generation and compile-time schemas, so high-volume custom resources pay JSON codec costs on every request hop. The readme cites benchmarks of up to roughly 8x faster custom resource encode/decode and 2x faster dynamic client decode, from CBOR as a self-describing binary format. The stated goal is to cut CPU and heap churn where Protobuf cannot be used, while not replacing Protobuf or all JSON/YAML.
alternatives: Keep JSON as the only serialization for custom resources — The readme says custom resources are at a serious efficiency disadvantage versus native resources, and benchmarks suggest CBOR reduces that cost. The sources do not record a reason this option was rejected.

Use a Kubernetes-specific length-prefixed CBOR framing scheme — A reviewer (benluddy) said it would be preferable to adopt the standardized CBOR Sequences scheme rather than a Kubernetes-specific framing, though length-prefixed framing may perform better. The sources do not show a final framing decision.

Two separate feature gates, one for storage and one for serving — Suggested by sftim. jpbetz preferred a single gate that stops storing and serving CBOR but still reads it from storage, so turning it off is safe. The sources do not show a final decision.

evidence.quote: It will supersede JSON in apiextensions-apiserver for storage serialization of custom resources.
Benchmarks suggest that custom resource and dynamic client encode and decode operations can be made up to approximately 8x and 2x faster
Replace existing usage of Protobuf. - Substantially reduce the size of encoded objects (a modest size reduction is anticipated).
it would be preferable to adopt that scheme vs. defining a CBOR framing scheme that is Kubernetes-specific.
I'm onboard with a single feature gate where we stop storing an serving CBOR, but continue to support reading it from storage.

summary: KEP-4247 introduces QueueingHint, a per-plugin callback that lets the scheduling queue decide whether a rejected Pod should be requeued after a cluster event, and whether to skip backoff. The KEP is now implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Plugins' EventsToRegister retried Pods on broad events, such as any Node add or update, even when those events could not make the Pod schedulable. Per-event callbacks filter these retries more finely, and letting DRA skip backoff avoids waiting for device-driver updates. The status is implemented, stage stable, which the sources confirm only in the enhancements lead's request to mark it implemented.
alternatives: Requeue by walking all unschedulable plugins' hints until all return Queue (kerthcet's proposal) — Sanposhiho showed a scenario (issue 109437) where NodeAffinity returns QueueSkip and NodeTaint returns Queue, so the Pod is never moved to activeQ; the sources reject this as a complete approach.

Return a Pending or Wait status from the plugin and let the hint decide, decoupled from framework status — The thread left this open; sanposhiho argued that tying backoff skipping to the returned status keeps the decision coupled to the past scheduling cycle, and that a clear rule and guardrail are needed to prevent misuse by custom plugins.

Let custom plugins return QueueImmediately from the hint even when they return Unschedulable — Sanposhiho objected that this needs a clear rule and guardrail, since all plugins gather in the scheduler and must work together without incorrect skip-backoff usage.

Keep returning Queue for all cross-node and non-Node events, as today — Sanposhiho noted that cross-node plugins would then have to return Queue for any non-Node event they register, which is not a real answer to the PodTopologySpread and custom-plugin cases.

evidence.quote: By introducing the callback function to filter out events more finely, the scheduler can retry scheduling of Pods which is only likely to be scheduled in the next scheduling cycle.
We want to improve the performance there by giving ability to plugins to skip backoff in selected cases.
Given that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, if all the work is completed, could you please update the KEP status in `kep.yaml` to `implemented`, and then close this issue?
since the feature was disabled, please update the KEP with notes on what criteria needs to be fulfilled to re-enable the feature.

summary: KEP-4265 adds a `procMount` field to the Pod/container security context so a user can opt out of the container runtime masking and read-only-setting certain /proc paths (value `Unmasked`), with `Default` as the default. The KEP is currently at implementable status, stage stable.
rationale: Some users want unprivileged containers nested inside a Kubernetes container using user namespaces, and the default /proc masking blocks this. The proposal lets the kubelet pass an empty masked-path list to the CRI when Unmasked is set, and restricts the option to the privileged Pod Security Admission level because an unmasked /proc can expose host /proc to root in the container. Reviewers pushed for the KEP to be retargeted at alpha and tied to user namespaces, which is why the status shows that the work depends on user namespaces rather than being a standalone graduation.
alternatives: Add an explicit Masked ProcMountType option — Maintainer haircommander was less inclined, calling it syntactic sugar since default already means masked and PSS can enforce default.
Use --oci-worker-no-process-sandbox like BuildKit — Not broadly supported with other container runtimes or builders.
Ask the kernel to allow mounting a new procfs with masks — Proposed in 2018 but denied in the kernel; no known effort to allow it since.
Give all hostUsers:false pods access to unmasked mounts by default — Opens an argument that user-namespaced pods are less secure, so weakening boundaries should be opt-in.

evidence.quote: having an Unmasked ProcMountType is a privileged operation, and thus is part of the [privileged]
When the kubelet is presented with a pod that has a ProcMountType as Unmasked, it will edit the default list of masked paths it passes down to the CRI
if this ends up impractical in practice a unit test showing the field stripping will be sufficient along with a manual test of disablement.
deferring to 1.35, as user namespaces is not going GA in 1.34
pushing this to beta is a bit early when the only safe way to use it is with user namespaces, which are still alpha

summary: KEP-4292 adds a `custom` flag to `kubectl debug` that takes a JSON (later YAML) file with a partial corev1.Container spec, which is strategic-merge-patched onto the container spec generated by the predefined profiles. It graduated to stable and was marked implemented for 1.33.
rationale: Users need to customize debug containers (env vars, volume mounts, security contexts, labels, image pull secrets) but adding a flag per field would make the command unmaintainable. The proposal therefore accepts a partial container spec and patches it over the predefined profile, with custom values overriding profile values on conflict. It limits scope to container spec because container is the largest common type across pod, node, and ephemeral container debugging.
alternatives: Add a dedicated kubectl debug flag for each field — The readme says adding a new flag for every field puts the debug command at risk of an unmanageable and unmaintainable state.

Make the custom profile JSON a full corev1.Container spec instead of a partial one — Reviewers raised this as an alternative in PR #4293 discussion; the source does not record a reason it was rejected beyond the partial-spec design that was adopted.

Extend customization to pod spec fields as well — The readme states this feature focuses only on container spec customization; pod spec changes can be handled by a few flags such as annotations and labels.

evidence.quote: Adding a new flag for every field puts a debug command at risk of unmanageable and unmaintainable state from not only maintainers point of view but also users.

custom profile json is patched onto the latest version of container spec generated by predefined profiles. As a result, custom profiles always suppress the properties inside predefined profiles in cases of conflicts.
This feature focuses only on container spec customization and has no attempt to change the other fields in pod spec.
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5057 marks the KEP as implemented. I think, we can close this issue as done.

summary: KEP-4317 proposes a PodCertificateRequest API type and a PodCertificate projected volume source so the kubelet can deliver X.509 certificates to pods without bearer tokens. The KEP's status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Issuing X.509 certificates through certificates.k8s.io does not by itself get certificates to workloads. The KEP adds a narrowly scoped PodCertificateRequest type and a PodCertificate projected volume so kubelet provisions keys and chains for pods, with no bearer tokens at any step. Discussion shows the design was narrowed during API review: the request type replaced a CSR-extension approach, and certificate lifetime is bounded through maxExpirationSeconds rather than a fixed rule.
alternatives: Encode pod coordinates in CertificateSigningRequest objects (labels, spec fields, or embedded in spec.request) — The discussion says none of the options met all goals, and a dedicated type for kubelet to request a pod certificate was preferred: "As painful as it is, option 4 seems to meet the goals the best."

Encode pod identity as Subject RDNs instead of a PodIdentity critical extension — The KEP records that this was considered and the extension was chosen, citing that the ability to mark it critical might matter; a reviewer noted RDNs would be simpler to maintain across languages.

Subresource on ServiceAccounts that issues certificates, or HTTP Message Signatures, or HMAC one-time tokens — These are listed as Alternatives in the KEP; the sources give only brief notes on them (HTTP Message Signatures is still a draft, HMAC tokens are not a big improvement over reused bearer tokens) and do not record a full rejection rationale.
HSM or external signing support for private keys in this KEP — Deferred: "After API review, we decided to defer any HSM / external signing support to a future iteration."

evidence.quote: A PodCertificateRequest API type, analogous to CertificateSigningRequest but narrowly scoped to the job of issuing certificates directly to pods.
After API review, we decided to move to use a new PodCertificateRequest type. This significantly cuts down the number of parties that need to care about the X.509 extension
After API review, we decided to defer any HSM / external signing support to a future iteration.
Kube-apiserver will restrict `maxExpirationSeconds` based on a per-signer configuration.
As discussed on slack, we will only set the client cert usages.

summary: KEP-4322 proposes a universal ClusterProfile API as a standard cluster inventory, defining a common status-reporting interface that multiple multi-cluster management implementations can support. The KEP is currently provisional at alpha stage.
rationale: There is no standard way to access a cluster inventory, even though most multi-cluster management solutions include one. Consumers such as schedulers, GitOps tools, and operators must currently learn each project's own cluster APIs. The KEP proposes a shared interface for discovering clusters, their properties, and status, while allowing multiple implementations. The status is provisional, so the design is still a proposal and not yet an accepted decision.
alternatives: Each multi-cluster project keeps its own cluster API and consumers adapt to each one — The readme says consumers 'either need to build the cluster concept by themselves or understand APIs representing a cluster from each cluster management project', which the proposed common API is meant to avoid.
Provide a standard reference implementation of the cluster inventory — This is listed as a non-goal: 'Provide a standard reference implementation.'
Define the Consumer registration API as part of this KEP — This is listed as a non-goal: 'Define the Consumer registration API'.

evidence.quote: there is not a standard way to access such an inventory; as we see more and more users embrace the cloud-native approach
The objective is to establish a shared interface for cluster inventory, defining a standard for status reporting while allowing for multiple implementations.
GitOps tools (ArgoCD, flux etc) are having the requirement to deploy workload to multiple clusters.
Non-Goals * Provide a standard reference implementation. * Define specific implementation details beyond general API behavior.

summary: KEP-4326 proposes an etcd storage version (SV) persisted in the etcd DB file to make etcd data upgrades and downgrades safe, plus an etcdutl migrate command to avoid starting and stopping every intermediate server version on multi-minor upgrades. The KEP is in provisional status.
rationale: Etcd data is not versioned, so upgrades cannot be reverted and downgrades are essentially unsupported, forcing users to rely on backup-before-upgrade. The proposal introduces a storage version to record data compatibility and a migrate command to simplify upgrades. The status is provisional, and the only recorded reason in the sources is that a reviewer pushed it back to provisional because the PRR was not filled in and reviewed.
outcome_reason: The sources say the KEP was pushed back to provisional because the Production Readiness Review (PRR) was not filled in and reviewed, so it could not pass improved validation.
alternatives: Alternative approach to etcd data versioning from the original etcd Downgrades Design document — The readme names this alternative but gives no reasoning for rejecting it; the excerpt does not explain why the storage version proposal was preferred.

evidence.quote: pushing back to provisional as PRR was not filled in and reviewed [to pass improved validation]
Introduce etcd storage version (SV) that is stored and persisted within the etcd DB file.
To simplify etcd data upgrade and downgrade process we will also introduce etcdutl migrate command
there is no way to safely downgrade etcd data after it was touched by newer version

summary: KEP-4330 introduces `--emulation-version` to make a binary emulate a prior Kubernetes release's capabilities, and `--min-compatibility-version` to control the minimum version a component stays compatible with for storage versions, validation and skew. The KEP reached implementable at alpha stage; the implementation merge was later deferred to the 1.31 merge window.
rationale: Upgrades of control-plane components are coarse, so a binary upgrade immediately exposes new features and writes N+1 data. Separating binary version from emulation and minimum compatibility version lets administrators take smaller, diagnosable steps and skip binary versions. The later comment says the core implementation needed to integrate with feature gates in composed sub-components, so merging was deferred to reduce risk to the 1.30 release.
outcome_reason: The sources do not say why the status is implementable at alpha beyond the reviewers' agreement. The deferral is stated in the later issue comment: the team decided to defer merging the implementation until the start of the 1.31 merge window, to de-risk the 1.30 release and allow more time for integration with feature gates.
alternatives: Single compatibility-version flag that both sets features and minimum interop version — Reviewers (johnbelamaric, liggitt) argued there are two distinct concepts: the features enabled and the minimum version to interoperate with safely, so the KEP uses two flags.

Allow emulation-version together with alpha features — jpbetz: alpha features are not designed to be upgradable and supporting them would require keeping alpha code around for the n-3 range before deletion, so the KEP makes them a non-goal.

Require a runtime GODEBUG setting matching the emulated Go version — jpbetz said compatibility-version controls only system behavior and does not require GODEBUG values from a different version; Go version changes apply to binary versions only.

evidence.quote: We will introduce a `--emulation-version` flag to emulate the capabiliites (APIs, features, ...) of a prior Kubernetes release version.
Alpha feature are not designed to be upgradable, so we will not allow alpha features to be enabled when `--emulation-version` is set.
We've decided to defer merging the implementation until the start of the 1.31 merge window. This both de-risks the 1.30 release and gives us time to more fully get this ready.
I think there's two distinct concepts, so yes?: 1. the features you want enabled 2. the min version you want to interoperate with safely
Handing it over to you for final consideration.

summary: KEP-4331 proposes two separate etcd probes: a liveness probe that checks the local node is up and running, and a readiness probe that checks the cluster is ready to serve traffic. The existing /health probe stays unchanged except for bug fixes. The KEP remains in provisional status.
rationale: The single /health probe is used for both liveness and readiness, so it cannot tell whether etcd needs a restart or should stop receiving traffic. The KEP adds separate livez/readyz probes to address this. The sources show the status stayed provisional because the PRR (production readiness review) was not filled in and reviewed when the PR was pushed back.
outcome_reason: The KEP was pushed back to provisional because the PRR was not filled in and reviewed, per the reviewer's comments on PR #4338. The sources do not record any later decision.
alternatives: Keep using the single /health probe for both liveness and readiness — The readme says it is not Kubernetes API compliant and 'does not differentiate whether etcd needs to restart or stop taking traffic.'

evidence.quote: The current etcd implementation has a single `/health` probe that is used to determine both the liveness and readiness of a node.
It does not differentiate whether etcd needs to restart or stop taking traffic.
Add two separate probes 1. Liveness: the liveness probe would check that the local individual node is up and running, or else restart the node.
pushing back to provisional as PRR was not filled in and reviewed [to pass improved validation]

summary: KEP-4346 proposes adding client-go informer metrics (reflector, queue, and eventHandler internals) exposed to Prometheus, gated behind a new InformerMetrics feature gate. The KEP is marked implementable at alpha stage.
rationale: Operators cannot tell why an informer stalls without adding debug logs, so the KEP exposes reflector/queue/eventHandler metrics. Reviewers asked for a feature gate because earlier reflector metrics caused a memory leak and were reverted. The status is implementable, with the stage set to alpha.
alternatives: Keep the reflector metrics removed (no re-add) — The readme says the change is needed because the removed reflector metrics were a memory leak, but it proposes reverting that removal behind a gate instead of leaving the metrics out.

Enable the metrics by default without a feature gate — Reviewers said earlier attempts were reverted after causing problems in the field, and the proposal adds the InformerMetrics feature gate; logicalhan later asked that the metrics be disabled by default and enabled only by explicit flag.
Use an environment variable to enable them — Reviewer rcomment:1481837519 notes an environment variable was updated to a feature gate instead.

evidence.quote: Add a feature gate `InformerMetrics` to enable informer/reflector metrics
I would ordinarily say no, but these in particular have been attempted at least once (I think twice) and reverted after causing issues in the field.
This change remove reflector metrics before https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74636. It is essential to fix memory leak issue.
I think these metrics should only be enabled through an explicit flag, and disabled by default. We have been burned by this so many times

summary: KEP-4355 proposes an opt-in Coordinated Leader Election mechanism in which candidates declare candidacy for a lease and an election coordinator claims the lease for the best candidate (lowest version, to respect skew policy), with an end-of-term marker to preempt the current leader. The KEP is at implementable status, stage beta.
rationale: Node-by-node control plane upgrades and rollbacks can run new-version controller managers or schedulers against old apiservers, violating the Kubernetes skew policy, because the leader is chosen by a race for the lease. Coordinated election picks the oldest compatible candidate deterministically and lets the coordinator preempt the leader at term expiry. Reviewers raised concerns about extra write load from per-candidate leases, whether the version-only ordering is too hardcoded, and the need for extensibility, which led to a strategy field and a beta re-evaluation.
alternatives: Let instances race to be the election coordinator and implement selection logic in the instances — Raised by sttts as an alternative during review (rcomment:1546626575); the sources do not record a decision against it beyond the coordinator-in-one-place preference from jefftree (rcomment:1552203565).

Use a generic integer score instead of version ordering — jefftree preferred centralized version-based ordering so clients need not update if the algorithm changes, and found versions more readable than scoring numbers (rcomment:1552203565).

Use a new object type instead of Lease for election coordination — jpbetz noted a new type would diverge from how other parts of the system use leases and make migration more complex (rcomment:1448236988); the design continues to use Lease.

Interactive approach where identity leases acknowledge end-of-term before re-election — jefftree and wojtek-t identified drawbacks: slower transition on leader loss and possible infinite preemption loops with a slow-writing best candidate (rcomment:1484889581, rcomment:1486270644). The sources do not say it was rejected outright.

evidence.quote: Instead of a race by component instances to claim the lease, component instances declare candidacy for a lease and a election coordinator claims the lease for the best available candidate.
For 3 node control plane upgrade, there is about a 25% chance of a new version of the controller running while old versions of the apiserver are active, resulting in a skew violation.
Offer an opt-in leader election mechanism to: - Elect the candidate with the oldest version available.
So yes - can we please add a user-story along those lines and add Beta criteria to reevaluate extensibility?
This field and available strategies will be re-evaluated for beta, but for alpha we will offer only `OldestCompatibilityVersion`

summary: KEP-4358 adds a `selectableFields` list to CustomResourceDefinition versions so that custom resources can be filtered with `--field-selector` on an allow-listed set of fields (e.g. spec.color), instead of putting such data into labels. The KEP is at status implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Extension authors who need to filter on spec or status fields today must copy that data into labels or write it twice, which the KEP wants to avoid. The design keeps the feature narrow: an allow list of fields, string-equality matching, and no arbitrary or nested field selection, to keep apiserver cost close to label selectors. Built-in declarative support and "in"/"not in" operators were moved out of scope so the KEP could focus on CRDs.
alternatives: Support arbitrary field selection on all fields — The KEP lists costs to apiserver of evaluating filters or maintaining indices, and lack of direct etcd filtering support, as reasons this is complicated.

Use CEL expressions as the selection mechanism — A reviewer argued that keeping user-specifiable CEL evaluation to the write path is better, since a list evaluating CEL over many items is poorly bounded. CEL was deferred from this KEP.
Add in/not-in operators to field selectors in this KEP — wojtek-t suggested separating it into its own KEP because it is independent of CRD field selectors, and the author moved it to future work.
Declarative built-in field selector support — The author moved built-in declarative support out of this KEP due to time constraints for 1.30, scoping it to CRD support only.

evidence.quote: Add an allow list of selectable fields to CustomResourceDefinitions. - Performance and resource consumption characteristics are roughtly equivalent to label selectors.
I'm going to prototype this. In the meantime, I'm moving the declarative built-in support to future work. I'm time constrained on what I can get done in 1.30
So I would suggest separating these two and tracking in/not-in as a separate KEP.

Keeping user-specifiable cel evaluations to the write path seems like a better idea to me. A single list having to evaluate a cel expression on poorly bounded quantities of list items doesn't seem great
Now that this KEP has graduated to `stable`, could we update the KEP status in kep.yaml from `implementable` to `implemented`?

summary: KEP-4368 adds a "managedBy" field to the Job spec so an external controller (for example Kueue in MultiKueue) can take over Job synchronization instead of the built-in Job controller. The KEP is implemented and stable.
rationale: MultiKueue runs a mirror Job in a worker cluster while the user's Job lives in the management cluster, so the status must be synchronized by Kueue rather than the main Job controller. The design therefore needs a way to disable the main Job controller for a given Job and delegate sync to an external controller. The "managedBy" field is the lightweight mechanism chosen for this.
alternatives: Passing custom parameters to the external controller — Listed as a non-goal in the readme, so it was explicitly excluded from the design.

evidence.quote: We support the "managedBy" field as a lightweight mechanism to delegate the Job synchronization to an external controller.
In order to support this workflow we need a mechanism to disable the main Job controller, and delegate the status synchronization to the Kueue controller.
The proposal is to support the "managedBy" field in the Job spec to indicate the only controller responsible for the Job object synchronization.

summary: KEP-4369 relaxes Kubernetes environment variable name validation to allow all printable ASCII characters in the range 32-126 except "=", and documents the rules for setting environment variables. The KEP status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Kubernetes restricted env var names to a narrow identifier set even though it cannot know what applications need, and users cannot always choose their own variable names. The main counter-concern raised in review was that third-party consumers treating env var names as safe filenames or flat paths could break. Reviewers judged the change acceptable with reasonable caution, and the proposal was narrowed to the 32-126 range after container runtime testing.
alternatives: Do nothing (leave the existing rule as-is) — The KEP's motivation is that Kubernetes should not restrict env var names it cannot justify restricting; the sources do not record a specific rejection reason beyond this.

Relax the rule with a long beta period, keeping the legacy rule as default until ValidatingAdmissionPolicy is GA — Listed as an alternative by sftim; hirazawaui said it overlaps with the current KEP and the docs for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could be updated after it. The sources do not record a final decision to reject it.
Namespace label or annotation controlling Pod env var validation — Listed as an alternative in the KEP; the sources do not state why it was not chosen.
New PodValidationRule API kind with CEL rules for env var keys and values — Described as the 'more complex' option in the KEP; the sources do not state why it was not chosen.

evidence.quote: Allows all printable ASCII characters except "=" to be set as environment variables, the range of printable ASCII characters is 32-126.
Kubernetes should not restrict which environment variable names can be used, because it has no way of knowing what the application may need
