summary: KEP-4381 defines structured parameters for Dynamic Resource Allocation: DRA drivers publish devices as ResourceSlice objects with named attributes, users express needs in ResourceClaims, and the scheduler allocates devices by comparing attributes. The KEP was reshaped so this base functionality is the core and KEP-3063 becomes an optional extension. Its status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Accelerators and network-attached devices do not fit the node-local, countable device plugin model, and the scheduler needs to evaluate them without knowing the exact request. Reviewers pushed for a structured, strongly typed API instead of opaque RawExtension parameters, which led to the "semantic" then "structured" parameters naming and to dropping support for custom schedulers. The design trades driver flexibility for a model the scheduler and autoscaler can interpret.
alternatives: Opaque parameters as in KEP-3063 — The readme says the structured model is the base and KEP-3063 adds an optional extension; the drawback section notes drivers give up some flexibility in exchange for structure.
RawExtension for numeric capacity models — Reviewer pohly replaced it with strongly-typed fields: "The usage of RawExtension gets replaced with strongly-typed fields in the resource.k8s.io API."

Separate feature-gated models per semantic model (DRANumericParameters, DRACounterNumericModel, DRAModeSwitchModel) — This was a proposal under discussion in the review; the sources do not show it was adopted as the final gating scheme.
Custom schedulers with their own semantic model — Pohly stated: "Custom schedulers are no longer supported, therefore I am closing this conversation."

evidence.quote: With such a claim in place, the scheduler (or Cluster Autoscaler) can evaluate against the `ResourceSlice` of any candidate nodes by comparing attributes, without knowing exactly what is being requested.

The usage of RawExtension gets replaced with strongly-typed fields in the resource.k8s.io API. This adds better validation, but has the downside that now kubelet is tightly coupled with the control plane.
Custom schedulers are no longer supported, therefore I am closing this conversation.
that is a better name because we define some structure for parameters and the associated mechanics, but not the actual semantic.

summary: KEP-4402 proposes adopting Go workspaces (a checked-in go.work file) in k/k to remove reliance on GOPATH for builds, verify/update scripts, and code generators, sequenced across k/k, gengo (moved to gengo/v2), and kube-openapi. Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: The k/k repo's build and tooling depend on GOPATH hacks layered on top of Go modules and staging repos, which the KEP calls a constant source of complexity and friction. Go workspaces were created for this multi-module setup, so the KEP proposes adopting them and retooling gengo, kube-openapi, and the k/k scripts. The sources do not say more about the reasons beyond this, and the status history shows the work reached implemented from 2024-03-01.
alternatives: Do nothing (keep tools and dev-experience semi-broken) — The KEP lists this as an option but the proposal is to fix the tooling; the sources do not record a specific rejection reason beyond the Goals.
Change how we manage our repos (abandon staging) — Listed under Alternatives without a stated reason for rejection; the Non-Goals say the meaning or structure of staging is not to change.
Abandon the mono-repo — Listed under Alternatives without a stated reason for rejection; the Summary says the monorepo benefits are kept.

Put gengo/v2 in a separate internal location (gengo/v2 with README, new k8s.io repo, code-generator subdirectory, or k8s.io/internal) — The KEP says the general feeling was that gengo/v2 is simplest and good enough, so the alternatives for placing gengo/v2 were not chosen.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes that we adopt Go workspaces and bring our tooling up to modern standards.
This KEP proposes to add a `go.work` file (checked in) and fix all the tools that break because of that.
The general feeling was that `gengo/v2` is simplest and "good enough".
The main gengo change has landed (https://github.com/kubernetes/gengo/pull/259).

summary: KEP-4412 lets the kubelet send a projected service account token (PSAT), bound to the pod and its service account with a configured audience, to kubelet credential provider plugins via stdin, so image pulls can be tied to workload identity without long-lived secrets. The KEP is marked implementable at stage beta.
rationale: Today image pulls rely on long-lived image pull secrets stored in the API or on node-wide kubelet credential providers that any pod on the node can use. The proposal adds an optional tokenAttributes field so a provider can receive a per-pod token and selected service account annotations. Reviewers raised concerns about cache keying, annotation exposure, and downgrade safety, which led to a separate apiserver feature gate that must be beta and enabled one release before this KEP reaches beta.
alternatives: Always pass the service account token through to the registry and rely on registry proxies to perform STS exchange — The readme lists this only under Alternatives with no stated reason for rejection, so the sources do not say why it was not chosen.

Pass arbitrary pod annotations to the credential provider — Reviewer liggitt said this 'makes an effectively unlimited surface area', and the design moved to service account annotations listed explicitly in serviceAccountAnnotationKeys.
Let the credential provider look up service account info directly from the Kubernetes API — Raised by liggitt as an alternative in review; the sources do not record a final rejection rationale.

evidence.quote: When it is set, the Kubelet will provision a token with the given audience bound to the current pod and its service account.
Removed pod annotations and added a new service account annotations field in the credential provider config to define the annotations that'll be plumbed to the plugin
Added a new feature gate and updated the beta criteria to include what @enj mentioned.
This feature needs to be beta/enabled by default at least one release before this KEP goes to beta. This is critical to support downgrade use cases.

summary: KEP-4420 proposes that the kube-apiserver automatically retries create requests using generateName when the generated name conflicts with an existing resource, up to 7 attempts, instead of returning HTTP 409 to the client. The KEP is marked implementable at stable stage.
rationale: Generated names use a 5-character suffix, so name collisions become likely as resource counts grow (50% chance before about 5000 names), and most clients do not retry the 409 error. Lengthening the suffix would break the 63-char name limit and downstream "{5}" regexes, so the KEP has the server retry name generation at the storage create step. Reviewers noted the change is in a critical codepath, and the discussion accepted it as the better option than client-side retries.
alternatives: Increase the length of the random generateName suffix — Breaking in two ways: it forces trimming generateName below 58 chars for names over that length and breaks downstream projects that use "{5}" regexes to match the suffix.
Check etcd for the generated name and regenerate on collision — Adds an etcd round-trip to every create request that uses generateName. The KEP's authors cite this cost as the downside.
Add a retry filter to the apiserver filter chain to re-run the whole request — Re-invokes the full admission chain and increases request latency more than the other approaches.

Build automatic retry into the client, by default or opt-in via a query param — The KEP does not state a specific reason; it lists this as an alternative considered but not adopted. Clients not doing retries was the problem being addressed.

evidence.quote: Today a HTTP 409 respose returned to the client if a name conflict happens. It is possible for clients to detect the error and retry, but we've seen that most clients don't realize to do this
If we retry up to 7 times, we can generate up to 1 million names before reaching a 0.1% chance of a collision.
This code is in a critical system codepath, if anything is wrong with it, it could cause severe problems, up to and including data corruption and loss.
Note that the problem is pre-existing. So this KEP doesn't create or encourage it, just tries to deal with it.
This enhancement is now marked as `tracked for code freeze` for the v1.32 Code Freeze!

summary: KEP-4427 relaxes validation of dnsConfig.searches entries so they may contain underscores or be a single dot, behind a RelaxedDNSSearchValidation feature gate (disabled by default). Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Strict RFC-1123 validation rejects search strings such as abc_d.example.com, which legacy SRV-based workloads need, and rejects the single dot used to avoid internal lookups. The KEP limits the relaxation to search strings only, so other names stay strictly validated. Validation distinguishes new resources from updates so that clusters can be downgraded safely.
alternatives: Keep strict RFC-1123 validation and rewrite resolv.conf from inside the pod — The readme says this typically requires running the pod with higher privileges than the workload requires.
Allow any characters in the DNS search string — Listed as a non-goal: the KEP only allows underscore and a single dot, not arbitrary characters.

Always apply relaxed validation, with no feature gate — The proposal introduces a gate disabled by default, and keeps strict validation for new resources when the gate is off, so there is no compatibility change while it is disabled.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes relaxing the checks on DNS search strings only.
Introduce a RelaxedDNSSearchValidation feature gate which is disabled by default.
Allowing underscores in the search string allows integration with legacy workloads without allowing anyone to define these names within Kubernetes.
As long as the gate is disabled, there is no compatibility change, so cluster downgrades are not affected by the feature.
A workaround is to re-write the resolv.conf file from inside the pod. This typically requires running the pod with higher privileges than the actual workload requires, however.

summary: KEP-4438 defers restarting sidecar containers during Pod termination to a separate feature gate, so that the base sidecar containers feature (KEP-753) can progress without the required kubelet Pod lifecycle refactoring. The KEP is in implementable status at alpha stage.
rationale: The feature of restarting sidecars during Pod termination requires fundamental Pod lifecycle changes that the authors judged too risky for a beta enabled by default. The sidecar containers code was already well tested, so the authors split the work into a separate feature gate to let KEP-753 reach GA faster. The KEP is therefore a decision to decouple the two features rather than to ship the termination restart on the original timeline.
alternatives: Introduce KEP-753 together with the restart during Pod termination feature — The readme says this "would have required a significant refactoring of the kubelet and the Pod lifecycle, which would introduce a risk of disruption to users."

Go directly to beta for the termination restart feature — The readme says "such changes cannot be introduced in beta (enabled by default) without risking disruption to users." A reviewer (wojtek-t) also asked for a rationale and risk paragraph before a direct beta target was considered.

evidence.quote: The reason for this KEP is that restarting sidecar containers during Pod termination requires fundamental changes to the Pod lifecycle
we are introducing a separate feature gate for the sidecar containers KEP to decouple the two features and allow users to use sidecar containers without the refactoring
This feature was originally planned for beta release in the initial KEP, but after further analysis, we decided to postpone and introduce a separate feature gate for it.
The alternative would be to introduce KEP-753 with the restart during Pod termination feature. However, this would have required a significant refactoring of the kubelet and the Pod lifecycle

summary: KEP-4443 proposes an optional Name field on PodFailurePolicyRule (defaulting to the rule's index) so that when a rule with action FailJob triggers, the JobFailed condition reason becomes PodFailurePolicy_{ruleName}. This lets higher-level APIs such as JobSet tell apart Job failures caused by different rules.
rationale: Higher-level APIs built on the Job API need to distinguish failure types, but all pod failure policy rules currently share the single JobFailed reason PodFailurePolicy. Appending the rule name as a suffix gives each rule a distinct, machine-set reason without changing how the policy behaves. The KEP is in implementable status at alpha stage, as of 2024-06-11.
alternatives: Add a SetConditionReason field so users can explicitly set the JobFailed reason — The team decided not to let users set the reason to an arbitrary value, since that would be hard to validate and would diverge from the paradigm of machine-set reasons.

evidence.quote: This will allow users to set multiple pod failure policy rules and distinguish which one (if any) triggered a Job failure.
This prevents higher level APIs like JobSet from distinguishing them and being able to take different actions depending on the type of Job failure that occurred.
ultimately it was decided we didn't want to open up the reason field to be explicitly set by the user to any arbitrary value, as this would be tricky to validate

summary: KEP-4444 adds a new Service spec field, trafficDistribution, as a non-binding routing preference (initially PreferClose, preferring same-zone endpoints) that supersedes the service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode annotation and the deprecated topologyKeys field. The KEP reached implemented status and stable stage.
rationale: The existing topology-mode annotation and topologyKeys field (deprecated since Kubernetes 1.21) are the precursors this KEP replaces. The design gives users a hint rather than a strict guarantee, so implementations can apply best-effort routing while strict locality stays with internalTrafficPolicy and externalTrafficPolicy. The status is implemented and stable as recorded.
alternatives: Strict routing guarantees enforced by the field — Listed as a non-goal: the field "will not enforce deterministic routing paths" and serves only as hints and preferences.

Replacing internalTrafficPolicy and externalTrafficPolicy — Non-goal: the new field "is complementary to internalTrafficPolicy and externalTrafficPolicy" and does not substitute their role in enforcing strict locality.
Adding Local (node-local preference) as an initial heuristic — Deferred: the initial implementation focuses on a core set, and Local "could be explored in future refinements" (see KEP-3015).

evidence.quote: It will supersede the functionality currently provided by the `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotation and it’s precursor `topologyKeys` field
The `trafficDistribution` field will not enforce deterministic routing paths. It serves as a mechanism for expressing hints and preferences
The new field is complementary to `internalTrafficPolicy` and `externalTrafficPolicy`. It does not aim to substitute their role in enforcing strict traffic locality.
This field will serve as preference or hint for the underlying implementation to consider while making routing decisions.

summary: KEP-4460 proposes replacing the kube-apiserver's timeout filter with per-request read/write deadlines via the Go ResponseController, behind the alpha feature gate PerHandlerReadWriteTimeout, so the whole handler runs on one goroutine. Status is implementable at alpha.
rationale: The timeout filter has caused many hard-to-debug data races, and it runs the inner handler in a separate goroutine that cannot be killed externally. Removing it and setting request-scoped read/write deadlines equal to the request context deadline keeps timeout behavior close to today for short, non-long-running requests. The reviewers raised concerns about client behavior changes (HTTP/1 connection close, HTTP/2 stream resets) and about how the handler goroutine would be stopped, and the design treats these as open questions to address during alpha.
alternatives: Use net/http.TimeoutHandler — The author states 'we are not going to use net/http.TimeoutHandler', and enj notes it is strictly worse than the existing handler.

Set a short server-wide timeout and extend it for long-running requests — tkashem replied that long-running requests are outside the scope of this proposal, since no deadline is set on their request context today.

Spin up a monitoring goroutine only for requests that time out, or track all in-flight requests globally — Wojtek suggested avoiding global tracking of inflight requests; tkashem said the goroutine-only approach needs a way to be notified when the context expires, and proposed global tracking as an alpha option with a beta criterion to replace it. The sources do not say which was finally chosen.

Panic from the ResponseWriter Write method or from context Value after timeout — The thread notes the context package can call Value from other goroutines, so a panic there could kill the process; the approach is still under investigation, and panic-on-write is described as an option, not a settled decision.

evidence.quote: the `timeout` filter in the kube-apiserver will become redundant, and thus be removed from the server handler chain.
A new feature flag `PerHandlerReadWriteTimeout` will be introduced, when enabled:
The scope of this proposal is the same, short (non long-running) requests only.
With a featuregate, I think we can try removing our special cased timeout handler.
it merged before my PRR review, but this looks fine for Alpha.

summary: KEP-4471 proposes that kubeadm make kubelets on control plane nodes point to the local kube-apiserver during init, join and upgrade, instead of the load-balanced control plane endpoint, behind the ControlPlaneKubeletLocalMode feature gate. The KEP status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: A kubelet bootstrapped through the load-balanced endpoint can reach kube-apiservers of older control plane nodes, which may violate the rule that kubelet must not be newer than kube-apiserver during immutable rolling upgrades. Pointing the kubelet at the local kube-apiserver avoids this. The change requires reordering etcd join ahead of the kubelet bootstrap wait, which is a CLI-breaking change, so it is gated.
alternatives: Keep the kubelet pointing at the load-balanced control plane endpoint — The source says this 'could result in violations of version skew policy' during immutable rolling upgrades, which the KEP aims to avoid.

Keep the existing phase order during kubeadm join — The KEP states that etcd must join before waiting for the kubelet bootstrap, so the reorder is needed for the local-endpoint path; the source says this 'requires reordering some of the operations'.

Apply the reordering without a feature gate — The source says that because reordering 'can be considered a breaking change to the CLI of kubeadm for some users, this should get done behind a feature gate'.

evidence.quote: Currently the kubelet always points to the load balanced control plane endpoint which could result in violations of version skew policy.
When doing a immutable rolling upgrade (as e.g. done when using [Cluster API]) the kubelet's minor Kubernetes version could be newer than the version of kube-apiserver
Use a new feature gate `ControlPlaneKubeletLocalMode` to toggle the feature until graduating to GA.
Because reordering the phases can be considered a breaking change to the CLI of kubeadm for some users, this should get done behind a feature gate

summary: KEP-4540 adds a `strict-cpu-reservation` policy option to the static CPUManager policy so that reservedSystemCPUs are excluded from the default cpuset used by burstable and best-effort containers, reserving them for system daemons and interrupt processing. The KEP is implemented and at stage stable.
rationale: Under the existing static policy, reservedSystemCPUs isolation applies only to guaranteed pods with integer CPU requests. Burstable and best-effort pods can use the reserved capacity because admission compares only CPU requests against allocatable CPUs, which can starve host OS services. The option removes reserved cores from the shared pool so these pods are kept off them, and it is opt-in so existing static-policy behavior is unchanged.
alternatives: Add a minSharedCPUs setting so a minimum shared pool is kept and exposed to the scheduler — The discussion says the option was abandoned: "The minSharedCPUs option is abandoned and left in the KEP for the record."

Add admission checks in kubelet and scheduler forcing a minimal CPU request for best-effort pods — The author argued it works against the scheduler's decision and creates an inconsistent view: "I see the new option (option 2) is an attempt to work against the scheduler's decision (creating new inconsistent view as you correctly pointed out)." The group deferred this and agreed to start with metrics: "we agreed to start with the metrics to assess the actual impact in real deployment".

Extend the eviction manager to remediate starved best-effort pods — Raised as an option but not adopted; the reviewer noted it could create runaway pod creation loops: "this approach would have the potential to create runaway pod creation loops".

Introduce a new schedulable resource for shared CPUs (Shared added to Allocatable) — Raised as a concern about changing the node API: "Not sure I understand what you are suggesting here because Allocatable (Total - reserved) is static during kubelet's lifecycle"; no decision to adopt it is recorded.

evidence.quote: a new `CPUManager` policy option `strict-cpu-reservation` is introduced which ensures that `reservedSystemCPUs` are strictly reserved for system daemons or interrupt processing
Admission is only comparing the cpu requests against the allocatable cpus. Since the cpu limit are higher than the request, it allows burstable and best-effort pods
The minSharedCPUs option is abandoned and left in the KEP for the record. I will update the KEP to make this very clear.
we agreed to start with the metrics to assess the actual impact in real deployment of the concern before to revisit if we need risk mitigation.
I'm fine deferring the BE protection or not as beta requirement, also considering it seems we reached consensus about adding metrics in alpha.

summary: KEP-4563 proposes a new declarative EvictionRequest API (evictionrequest.coordination.k8s.io) and controller so that pods can be evicted cooperatively through a list of interceptors, falling back to API-initiated eviction only when no interceptor is active. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: Current API-initiated eviction and PodDisruptionBudgets cannot handle single-replica apps, HPA-scaled apps, or cases where the application needs time or resources before termination, and they block or are overridden during node drains. The KEP adds a coordination contract where interceptors act on a pod before the controller evicts it. Reviewers raised concerns about complexity and whether incremental PDB/Eviction API changes would suffice, and the author responded that incremental changes could not address the problems.
alternatives: Incremental improvements to PodDisruptionBudgets and the Eviction API — Reviewer soltysh suggested tackling smaller problems first; the author replied: "I do not see how we can incrementally improve the situation for PDBs and eviction API to address the problems at hand."
Pod API (state in the Pod object itself) — The author stated: "We have analyzed the problem and found serious concurrency, obsevability and extensibility issues."
Liens API (in-use protection KEP) — The author stated: "Liens do not offer any reconciliation mechanism, and it is very hard/impossible for an actor to communicate a deletion intention."

Modeling the request as a finalizer on deletionTimestamp (reviewer thockin's suggestion) — The author argued that the deletion either has not happened yet or never will: "The deletion triggers pod termination with TerminationGracePeriodSeconds which is not what some applications desire."

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to add a new declarative EvictionRequest API to manage the eviction of pods.
Use API-initiated Eviction API of pods that support the eviction request process, only if there are no active interceptors.
I would prefer not to have a new API, but at this time, I do not see how we can incrementally improve the situation for PDBs and eviction API to address the problems at hand.
Liens do not offer any reconciliation mechanism, and it is very hard/impossible for an actor to communicate a deletion intention.
The deletion triggers pod termination with `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` which is not what some applications desire.

summary: KEP-4568 proposes mitigations for kube-apiserver and etcd overload during watchcache initialization or reinitialization, including returning 429 for requests that would otherwise be delegated to etcd or hang on an uninitialized watchcache, and gating readiness on builtin-type watchcache initialization via a PostStartHook. Its status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Watchcache initialization is effectively a list from etcd that can take tens of seconds or more, during which hanging watches consume API Priority and Fairness seats and unindexed lists with resourceVersion=0 are sent to etcd, risking control plane outage. The readme states that watches hang until initialization finishes and that a PostStartHook only reports healthy once, so reinitialization would not affect readyz. Sources do not explain the final stable-stage rationale beyond maintainer comments that the resilient initialization is mature and ready for GA.
alternatives: Use a readiness check or PostStartHook alone to gate initialization — The discussion says a PostStartHook is reported healthy once and never reverts to false, so later reinitialization would not be reflected in readyz; requests would instead return 429.

Pass all requests to etcd when watchcache is not initialized — The readme says that for lists with ResourceVersion=0 delegating to etcd is particularly problematic, and passing too many such requests down can bring down the control plane.

Make streaming lists the only allowed lists during initialization — A maintainer replied that streaming lists will never be allowed here because they are served from watchcache, so they cannot be served while it is uninitialized.

Ship the feature directly as beta behind an alpha-free path versus starting at alpha — Reviewer deadads2k initially opposed going directly to beta; the final decision recorded in the discussion was two feature gates both going directly to beta, one disabled by default and one enabled by default.

evidence.quote: For watch requests, unless it's a consistent watch request (setting RV="") - which isn't really used by none of our core components, it is always handled by the watchcache.

it's reported as healthy as soon as it succeeds for the first time: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/hooks.go#L238-L245 [and it never changes back to false later]
No. Streaming lists will never be allowed here as they are served from watchcache - so if the watchcache is not initialized, we will not be able to serve them at all.
two separate feature-gates - both going directly to beta - one of them disabled by default, second enabled by default
ResilientWatchCacheInitialization has been enabled on since 1.31, so it seems mature enough

summary: KEP-4569 moves Kubernetes support for cgroup v1 into maintenance mode: no new features, e2e regression tests kept, best-effort fixes (security prioritized), and migration guidance. It explicitly does not remove cgroup v1 support; removal is deferred to a future KEP.
rationale: The Linux kernel community focuses new cgroup features on v2, and distributions and systemd are phasing out v1, so Kubernetes must follow. The KEP freezes v1 features and keeps e2e coverage while leaving deprecation and removal for later. Discussion shows the "deprecation" wording caused confusion, so sig-node settled on maintenance mode rather than a removal path.
alternatives: Continue full support for cgroup v1 with no change — The KEP says this would prevent users from accessing cgroup v2 improvements and expose them to risks as systemd and RHEL 9 deprecate v1.

Deprecate cgroup v1 with the eventual goal of removing it — The KEP says this could significantly impact users on legacy OS or kernel versions under long-term support. Reviewers also noted the term 'deprecation' caused confusion, so the KEP was narrowed.

Add a feature gate or env variable required to enable cgroup v1 — The discussion says the feedback was not to disrupt existing v1 support, and that a barrier would force users to take extra steps to keep using v1. The gate was dropped from the proposal.

Log a warning on cgroup v1 hosts at kubelet start — A reviewer (bentheelder) suggested an explicit v1 warning, but the discussion records no decision to adopt it; the status history does not mention it.

evidence.quote: Moving cgroup v1 to maintenance mode presents transitional challenges, including: 1. Operational Overhead

Non-Goals
Removing cgroup v1 support. Deprecation and removal will be addressed in a future KEP.
The term "deprecation" has caused confusion and differing interpretations of how actively cgroup v1 features will be maintained.
We are not going to drop the support for cgroup v1. At least, that is not with-in the scope of this KEP.
the feedback on this KEP has been not to disrupt existing cgroup v1 support. If we put any barrier to enable cgroup v1, it will disrupt their workflow

summary: KEP-4578 proposes introducing Kubernetes-style feature gates into etcd so that new features are gated behind a lifecycle-tracked mechanism, letting users turn features on or off and query feature enablement, replacing the ad hoc --experimental flag approach. Status is provisional.
rationale: The current --experimental flag mechanism is hard to track, has no clear graduation path because removing the prefix is a breaking CLI change, and gives clients no way to query feature enablement. Each experimental flag must also be piped through code separately, so some changes can slip past it. The KEP proposes a single feature gate framework to address these issues.
outcome_reason: Status is provisional, so the sources do not record a final outcome or reason beyond the proposal itself.
alternatives: Keep adding features as --experimental flags and graduate by adding a new stable flag — The readme says this is a breaking change at graduation and leads to features getting stuck or forgotten in the experimental phase.
Handle feature gate enablement at the cluster level in this KEP — The readme lists cluster-level enablement as a non-goal that requires a separate KEP.
Use feature gates to fix bugs — The readme lists using feature gates as a bug-fix mechanism as a non-goal.

evidence.quote: We are introducing the Kubernetes style feature gate framework into etcd to gate future feature enhancement behind a sequence of feature lifecyles.
a new stable feature flag identical to the experimental feature flag but without the --experimental prefix is added to replace the old feature flag, which is a breaking change.
no method for clients to query and make decisions based on feature enablement in a cluster.
Handle the feature gate enablement on the cluster level. They require more careful consideration and thus warrants a separate KEP.

summary: KEP-4580 proposed deprecating kubelet RunOnce mode, marking the KubeletConfiguration RunOnce field and --runonce flag as deprecated, and later removing the flag and mode. The KEP stayed provisional at alpha; the author closed the tracking issue in July 2024 and later said the KEP no longer needs updating.

Reviewers asked for a deprecation path that is gradual and feature-gated, and for PRR and risk sections, while the v1.31 code PR missed code freeze due to a merge conflict. The sources do not give a final reason for dropping the KEP beyond the missed freeze and the author's later comment.
outcome_reason: The provisional status is the recorded fact. The issue was closed by the author on 2024-07-24 after the enhancement was removed from v1.31 at code freeze, and the author later said "We don't need to update this KEP anymore." The sources do not explicitly say why the author chose not to continue.
alternatives: Fix RunOnce mode and add e2e and integration tests — Listed as an alternative in the KEP; the KEP does not say why it was not selected.

Make RunOnce mode work in systemd mode and support volumes — Listed as an alternative in the KEP; reviewer sftim noted documenting an alternative is not the same as selecting it. No selection rationale is recorded.

Introduce a Legacy-named feature gate (e.g., LegacyNodeRunOnceMode) instead of a deprecated gate — soltysh said the Legacy name suggests the opposite of the intent; sftim proposed inverting the gate sense instead. No final decision is recorded.

evidence.quote: Deprecate and remove kubelet support for RunOnce mode, and mark the `RunOnce` field in `KubeletConfiguration` and the `--runonce` flag of kubelet as deprecated
It seems to have completely stopped working in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90377, because the cpuManager is not initialized in runonce
the implementation (code related) PR(s) associated with this enhancement is not in the merge-ready state by code-freeze and hence this enhancement is now removed from the v1.31 milestone.
we will close this issue and will not move forward with it.

summary: KEP-4595 proposes a mutually exclusive `expression` field for CRD additionalPrinterColumns, letting users define printer column values as CEL expressions alongside existing JSONPath. The KEP is currently merged in provisional state, not implementable for alpha.
rationale: JSONPath printer columns cannot handle arrays, conditionals, multi-field computation, or duration formatting, and earlier JSONPath extension attempts broke compatibility. CEL is proposed as a richer alternative evaluated at Table request time. Benchmarks showed CEL FindResults roughly 15-50x slower than JSONPath, and reviewers (liggitt) objected because printer columns run per list item, so the KEP was merged only as provisional pending better performance.
outcome_reason: The KEP was merged as provisional rather than implementable because CEL performance was not yet close enough to JSONPath. The 2025-06-18 comment says the documentation "can't be merged as `implementable` in its current state until we get improved benchmark results for CEL (equivalent or at most 2x to the JSONPath cost)". Later, the 2026 comment says the team will target alpha in 1.38 after revising benchmarks.

summary: KEP-4601 proposed extending authorization attributes with field and label selectors from List, Watch, and DeleteCollection so authorizers (webhook, SAR/SSAR, node, CEL) can use them in decisions. Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Per-node workloads need tighter security, and out-of-tree authorizers need selector information to express restrictions. The design exposes selectors as authorization attributes without adding an in-tree selector-managing authorizer or expanding audit and admission surfaces. Reviewers settled that selector requirements are ANDed server-side, so unrecognized operators can be treated safely, and that selector parse failures and unsupported verbs should error rather than silently drop the selector.
alternatives: Add a second, separate parsed-requirements representation alongside the raw selector string in the SAR body — Reviewer luxas objected to the sprawl of two near-identical representations and wanted a canonical codec library instead.

Drop unparseable or unsupported selectors as non-limiting, as the SubjectAccessReview API does — deads2k said leniency makes it hard to discover VAP or binding bugs, so the design errors instead; the author updated the KEP accordingly.

Use a separate optional interface for selector access instead of adding methods to authorizer.Attributes — luxas disliked this option; deads2k accepted breaking implementers of the interface as an explicit way to force the semantic change.

Change selector combination from AND to another semantic — liggitt argued AND lets webhooks short-circuit on known limits and safely ignore unknown operators, so changing it would break future operator expansion.

evidence.quote: The authorization attributes will be extended to include field selectors and label selectors from List, Watch, and DeleteCollection.
Currently every discrete requirement is AND'd when evaluated server-side. I don't see a need to change that behavior.
This seems to make it very difficult to discovery VAP (or binding) bugs. While I can see a case that leniency makes more successes, I'd try to make it easy to discover bugs and error.
I'm ok breaking people that integrated at this level. They should be aware of the semantic change and this is an easy way to force it.

summary: KEP-4603 proposes an alpha-gated change to kubelet CrashLoopBackOff: lower the initial backoff from 10s to 1s and the maximum from 5 minutes to 1 minute, plus a node-level opt-in config for a faster curve. The KEP is in status implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: The fixed exponential backoff (10s, 20s, ... capped at 5 minutes) is considered too conservative, which delays recovery for failing containers and prevents faster restarts for workloads such as gaming and AI/ML. The KEP front-loads the decay curve and lowers the cap, while keeping the API surface small and making node stability risk measurable through benchmarking and observability. Approval was given at the provisional stage on the condition that the remaining topics (rapid restart, node-level opt-in, benchmarking, Job API interaction, kubelet overhead) would be covered in follow-up KEP PRs for 1.32.
alternatives: restartPolicy: Rapid (a new per-container restart policy value) — Moved out of the proposal to Alternatives Considered; reviewers did not like the API enough given its complexity to back out of it, so the 1.32 release was deferred. The source says: "I did decide today with @tallclair to wait for 1.32 to put this in an actual release because we don't like the API I suggested enough for how complicated it might be to back out of it."

Treat Succeeded pods the same as failed pods or give constant/instant backoff for Succeeded pods — Not in the current scope. The KEP says it will NOT change backoff behavior for Pods transitioning from Success differently from Failed, and the early version that addressed the Success case was dropped.
Lower the maximum CrashLoopBackOff duration within this KEP — Split out into KEP-5593: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay.

Make backoff configuration cluster-admin only via feature gates — Feature gates are only temporary, so the reviewer said cluster-wide configuration should be a KubeletConfiguration option. The KEP adopted a per-node kubelet config rather than a flag.

evidence.quote: Provide an alpha-gated change to get feedback and periodic scalability tests on changes to the global initial backoff to 1s and maximum backoff to 1 minute
This design seeks to change the existing initial value for the backoff curve to 1s to stack more retries earlier, and reduce the maximum backoff for a given restart from 5 minutes to 1 minute
The KEP itself documented well the risk mitigation strategies: * Conservative Defaults * Node-Level Opt-in * Alpha Stage and Feature Gates * Extensive Testing
@lauralorenz and @tallclair indicates they are going to be covered in the following KEP PRs for 1.32, which makes this implementable. /approve at the provisional state

summary: KEP-4622 adds a TopologyManager policy option, max-allowable-numa-nodes, so operators can raise the hard-coded limit of 8 NUMA nodes that the TopologyManager supports. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: The hard-coded limit of 8 NUMA nodes was a stop-gap against state explosion in hint generation, which made kubelets with more NUMA nodes crash. The option lets users on high-end CPUs with more than 8 NUMA nodes run the TopologyManager, at the cost of possibly slower pod admission. Reviewers agreed the feature is an escape hatch and that the real fix (reducing state explosion) is out of scope.
alternatives: Adding a new kubelet configuration option — Listed as an alternative in the KEP's Alternatives section; the sources do not say why it was not chosen.

Remaining in alpha until a proper solution reduces state explosion — Raised by jpbetz in review; the discussion moved on to beta with the risk documented, and the sources do not record a decisive reason against it beyond the agreed text update.

Enforcing a minimum value of 8 and failing kubelet startup below it — klueska argued setting a lower value should be no problem and a kubelet crash only occurs if the machine has more NUMA nodes than configured; ffromani said restricting the value is inconsistent with cadvisor reporting and would be a source of confusion.

Adding a gauge metric for the configured value — klueska said a metric is not appropriate because the option is a node property that does not affect running workloads; the config is the right place to check it.

evidence.quote: The current hard-coded value of 8 was added as a stop-gap 4 years ago to mitigate the state explosion that occurs when trying to enumerate the possible NUMA affinities
If your system has, say 9 NUMA nodes, then you will not be able to run kubernetes on it without this feature.
I would say this feature is use-at-your-own-risk until we have a proper solution in place to reduce the state explosion.
the actual *value* of this new setting doesn't impact the latency of pod admission. The latency is *only* influenced by the number of NUMA nodes your physical system has.
I don't think a metric is appropriate. It is not a feature that is used by workloads.

summary: KEP-4633 proposes making the kube-apiserver's --anonymous-auth setting three-state: disabled, enabled for all requests, or enabled only for a configured list of endpoints. Anonymous requests to other endpoints would be rejected. Status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Anonymous auth is on by default, and admins who want to disable it cannot, because health checks (healthz, livez, readyz) from load balancers and kubelet depend on it. Misconfigured RBAC bindings to system:anonymous have led to cluster takeover. The KEP lets admins allow anonymous access only to a named set of paths, keeping health checks working while blocking other endpoints. Reviewers agreed that defaults do not change and that the path list is exact-match and kept small on purpose.
alternatives: Sidecar proxy restricting endpoints — The readme says it would push complexity into all consumers who are not running sidecar proxies today, while the in-tree change is minimal.

Deny authorizer that rejects anonymous requests — The readme says a deny authorizer is a lot more complex to implement, and that having a later subsystem lock down over-granted requests from the first is not ideal.

Restrict creation of problematic role bindings with ValidatingAdmissionPolicy — Raised by sftim as an alternative to explain in the KEP; the sources do not record a decision on it or a reason it was not chosen.

Glob path matching like RBAC — liggitt said globbing was not required for the use cases presented, and the feature intends to constrain anonymous auth to a well-known set of endpoints, so exact paths were chosen.

evidence.quote: We propose that kubernetes should allow users to configure which endpoints can be accessed anonymously and disable anonymous auth for all other endpoints.
In order to allow these health checks a cluster admin has to enable anonymous requests opening the door for misconfigurations.
This KEP does not propose changing any defaults. kubeadm could choose to configure this to add exactly
I want to keep the surface area here as small as possible, globbing wasn't required for the use cases presented so far
this didn't get marked as implementable, so never got a PRR review

summary: KEP-4639 adds a new VolumeSource that mounts OCI images and OCI artifacts as read-only directories inside a pod, so files can be shared among containers without being baked into the main image. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Sharing files between containers currently requires copying them with an init container and a shell, or bundling them into the main image. The KEP scopes the work to directory mounts only, leaves single-file and manifest-list cases out, and leaves runtime-level format handling to the CRI runtimes. Discussion pushed toward kubelet owning the lifecycle with the runtime serving pull and unmount requests, and some reviewers preferred an out-of-tree CSI driver instead.
alternatives: Out-of-tree CSI driver (for example csi-driver-image-populator) — The readme lists it as an alternative to be documented, and reviewers (kfox1111) noted drivers had poor adoption because clusters did not deploy them. The sources do not record a final rejection rationale beyond the decision to implement in-tree.

Shared volumes inside a single pod or an init container copying files — The author (sallyom) said this required packaging a shell in the model image and an init container, which the new VolumeSource is meant to remove.

Extend the CRI PullImage RPC with a target path field — Proposed by haircommander as a way to reduce RPC duplication; mrunalp responded that the kubelet should own lifecycle decisions and the runtime should service requests. The sources do not show it was adopted.

Single-file mounts or manifest-list handling in the first version — The readme's non-goals and the 2024-06-14 meeting summary explicitly leave single-file and manifest-list cases out for now, restricting output to directories and matching architecture.

evidence.quote: The enhancement leaves single file use case out for now and restrict the mount output to directories.
It will be simpler to leave single file use case out for now and restrict the mount output to directories.
Yes, it would be best let kubelet be responsible for lifecycling decisions and let the runtime service the requests.
Most of the in-tree advantages listed here can be done with an external CSI driver.
In order to remove the need for a shell & init container, I propose a new OCI VolumeSource.

summary: KEP-4656 proposes that kubeadm stop setting the CRI socket annotation (kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket) on Node objects and stop writing --container-runtime-endpoint to kubeadm-flags.env. Instead, kubeadm writes a per-node /var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml containing ContainerRuntimeEndpoint, which is merged into the kubelet config during init/join/upgrade. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: The CRI socket annotation on the Node object persists even when the kubelet or the container runtime changes, so it can go stale. Moving the endpoint into a per-node instance config lets kubeadm set ContainerRuntimeEndpoint in the kubelet config directly, which removes the need to store it on each Node. The readme frames this as a way to use the migrated container runtime endpoint flag in instance configuration.
alternatives: Do nothing and keep using /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env — The readme notes that kubelet has deprecated the --container-runtime-endpoint args, so continuing to use the flags file is not viable long term.
Avoid a feature gate and ship compatibility across multiple versions — The readme says it prefers adding a feature gate to improve user awareness, so this option was not chosen.

evidence.quote: Instead of relying on the annotation, this KEP proses creating an instance config per node and overriding the `ContainerRuntimeEndpoint` in the kubelet config when calling kubeadm commands
This annotation is persistent on the Node object, even if the kubelet is updated or the CRI is changed.
This file will be merged with `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` in the process of kubeadm init/join by using the `kubeletconfiguration` patch target.
Do nothing, continue to use the`/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env` file, but kubelet has deprecated the `--container-runtime-endpoint` args.

summary: KEP-4671 proposes gang scheduling in kube-scheduler built on new Workload (policy template) and PodGroup (standalone runtime scheduling unit) APIs in scheduling.k8s.io, with pods referencing their PodGroup via spec.schedulingGroup. Status is implementable, stage beta. kep.yaml records that it replaces KEP-583 Coscheduling and KEP-5832 Decouple PodGroup API.
rationale: Gang-scheduled workloads (AI training, MPI-style jobs) need all pods to start together, and gang scheduling was implemented outside kube-scheduler at least four times. The design decouples the long-lived Workload policy from runtime PodGroup objects to separate concerns, avoid etcd size limits, and avoid read-modify-write contention on a central object. Reviewers accepted the pod-by-pod-with-WaitOnPermit approach for the current release, with a workload-level placement phase and gang-aware preemption deferred to Beta and later work.
alternatives: Embedding PodGroups within the Workload spec (original design) — The readme says it creates architectural challenges: lifecycle coupling, a 1.5MB etcd object size limit for large Workloads, and contention on status updates. The KEP moved to standalone PodGroups for these reasons.

Keeping pods in WaitOnPermit with a SchedulingTimeoutSeconds field exposed in the API — Reviewers argued it was unclear how users should set the value and that it may be a scheduler setting. The timeout was removed from the API struct and left only in alternatives, with a possible follow-up. The readme does not state the final alternative's rationale in full.

Gang-aware preemption inferred from member pod priority — A reviewer warned that inferring gang priority from pods would be a breaking change. The KEP instead proposes a new additive preemptionPolicy later, as a Beta graduation criterion, not in this release.

evidence.quote: kube-scheduler identifies pods that are in a group and waits until all pods reach the same stage of the scheduling/binding cycle before allowing any pods from the group to advance past that point

Extending the Workload object to track runtime status for all PodGroups leads to significant scalability issues: - *Size Limit*: Large Workloads (i.e., large number of PodGroups) may easily hit the 1.5MB etcd object limit.
`Workload` becomes a scheduling policy object that defines scheduling constraints and requirements. - `PodGroupTemplate` provides the blueprint for runtime `PodGroup` creation.
given the overall consensus (@sanposhiho @andreyvelich @macsko myself) about this version, I just went ahead I made this the leading option and moved the original option down to alternatives.
For that part, I added the first Beta graduation criteria - having a high-level design for gang-preemption to ensure that we won't break compatibility with it.

summary: KEP-4680 proposes exposing device health (served by Device Plugin or DRA) in Pod Status and events, so users can see when a Pod uses a failed or unhealthy device. The KEP is currently implementable at stage beta.
rationale: Pods consuming failing devices crash-loop with little information about the cause, so the KEP surfaces device health in Pod Status. The design is intentionally small and keeps the change limited to health, excluding other device or CPU assignment details. Reviewers raised open questions about device identifiers (ResourceID) and a separate gRPC health interface for DRA, which the KEP resolves by keeping health-only reporting. The status is a fact given as implementable, stage beta, and the source confirms it has not GA'd.
alternatives: A Pod Resources-like API exposed by kubelet to query via kubectl or a node port — The readme says it opens a new API surface and it would be impossible to get status for Pods that have already completed.
Exposing DRA status via ResourceClaims — The readme says this leads to a debate on security so kubelet is limited to which statuses it can set; the alternative was not chosen.

Reporting health for CPUs or other resources in this KEP — The readme says the KEP is intentionally scoped small and the Non-Goals exclude other resource assignment; sergeykanzhelev said he wanted to minimize changes in a single KEP.

Using a Conditions list for health — Discussion shows this was questioned (johnbelamaric) and the author said a plain status value is reasonable and copied from NodeCondition-like types; the source does not record a final decision to drop Conditions.

evidence.quote: This KEP will fix this by exposing device health via Pod Status. This KEP is intentionally scoped small, but can be extended later
Exposing unhealthy devices in Pod Status will provide a generic way to understand that the failure is related to the unhealthy device

summary: KEP-4706 proposed deprecating kustomize in kubectl (alpha in v1.31), then disabling it by default and removing it in v1.36. The KEP was rejected after a sig-architecture discussion, and kustomize stays part of kubectl.
rationale: The KEP argued that kubectl should not promote one customization tool over others, that kustomize's release cycle mismatched kubectl's, and that some kustomize dependencies were problematic. Reviewers (liggitt, thockin, and others) objected that removal would break many users and automation, and that the motivations were vague. The KEP's own note says the sig-architecture discussion on Oct 17th, 2024 decided not to pursue the topic further, mainly because of kustomize's widespread adoption.
outcome_reason: The sources state the decision was to not pursue the removal and to keep kustomize as part of kubectl, made at the sig-architecture meeting on Oct 17th, 2024. The status was changed to rejected in PR #4984. Earlier, the enhancement was dropped from v1.31 and deferred.
alternatives: Freeze kustomize-in-kubectl and warn users to use kustomize directly — Discussed by thockin as a middle ground; liggitt said freezing is not viable because dependencies that cannot be updated become unfixable vulnerabilities.

Keep kustomize in kubectl but exec an external kustomize binary (compatibility mode) — Proposed by codablock and koba1t; benthelder said users would still have to install kustomize separately and it would still break a lot of automation.

Embed kustomize binaries with go embed and exec them from a temp directory — koba1t raised it as an experiment; thockin said it has the same security problems with none of the visibility of vendored code and exec is not always available.

Staged deprecation and removal (v1.31 alpha, v1.34 beta disabled by default, v1.36 removal) — This is the KEP's proposed path; it was rejected after the sig-architecture discussion, with the stated reason being widespread community adoption.

evidence.quote: it was decided not to pursue this topic further, and retain kustomize as part of kubectl. The primary reason for this decision was the widespread adoption of the tool by the community.

summary: KEP-4742 proposes a built-in admission plugin, PodTopologyLabels, that copies standard node topology labels (topology.kubernetes.io/zone, topology.kubernetes.io/region, kubernetes.io/hostname) onto pods/binding so Pods can read them via the Downward API. The KEP is currently at implementable status, stage beta.
rationale: Workloads such as AI/ML, CNI plugins and sharded databases need node topology, and today they must use privileged init containers that query the API. The KEP makes the labels available synchronously at binding time, since env vars and downward API values can only be set at pod start. Scope was narrowed to the standard labels to limit exposure of node information to pods.
alternatives: Expose all node labels via the downward API — Proposed alternative in review; the discussion notes it has too many security risks as Nodes are often shared by many tenants, and the non-goal excludes non-standard node labels by default.

Helper controller copying selected node labels to Pods (label or annotation) — Controller was judged not viable due to a race with the scheduler; the reviewer said 'I don't think controller was ever viable due to race with scheduler'.

Sidecar or init container fetching topology from the Kubernetes API, or a published container image writing to emptyDir — Reviewers (sftim) raised these as workarounds; the KEP's Motivation says these workarounds need elevated privileges, and the KEP argues for a more secure, consistent built-in approach.

Kubelet sets the labels on the pod or a controller copies them asynchronously — Thockin: 'We don't really want async copying from node->pod because env vars can only be set at pod start. So we need a synchronous mechanism, which is why @munnerz went with Binding.'

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes a built-in admission plugin to copy standard node topology labels to Pods.
We don't really want async copying from node->pod because env vars can only be set at pod start. So we need a synchronous mechanism
I decided to only include the standard labels for now as it's safer and doing `*.topology.k8s.io/*` doesn't seem that much more extensible

summary: KEP-4743 proposes a standardized etcd-Kubernetes code interface, owned by SIG-etcd, that formalizes the implicit contract between Kubernetes and etcd so it can be tested and reviewed. Its status is provisional.
rationale: The implicit Kubernetes-etcd contract is undocumented, which hurts testability and causes incorrect usage (e.g. issue #110210). The KEP defines an interface in the etcd client adopted by Kubernetes, scoped to the etcd3 store and master leases, with no new behavior beyond what etcd supports. Comments show enhancements tracking was dropped for v1.32 because there is no user-facing change and the process overhead was not justified.
outcome_reason: The sources give a status of provisional, with the KEP opted out of v1.32 tracking and marked Deferred for that cycle. The sources do not say why it was not advanced further after that.
alternatives: Track the KEP through the standard enhancements process for v1.32 alpha — Maintainers opted out: "the overhead of KEP template, PRR and other processes makes it not worth it."
Keep the implicit contract undocumented — The KEP aims to codify the contract so that "we will improve the testability of both Kubernetes and etcd, prevent common errors in their interaction".

evidence.quote: By formalizing this contract, we will improve the testability of both Kubernetes and etcd, prevent common errors in their interaction, and establish a framework for the future evolution of this critical contract.

summary: KEP-4762 proposes a new podSpec field `hostnameOverride` that lets users set an arbitrary FQDN as a pod's hostname, written into the pod's /etc/hosts. When set, it overrides `hostname`, `subdomain`, and `setHostnameAsFQDN`, and once GA the Kubelet always respects it. The KEP is at status implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Traditional applications may depend on the hostname for permissions or service operations, but Kubernetes pod hostnames always carry the cluster suffix, so they cannot match DNS-based expectations during migration. The proposal adds a dedicated override field so the Kubelet can use an arbitrary FQDN without changing the legacy hostname behavior. The design document acknowledges the drawback that this conflicts with the pod's potential DNS records and is not a standard Kubernetes use case.
alternatives: Configure hostnameOverride via kube-apiserver (defaulting/REST logic writes the computed value) — The design says it would require teaching kube-apiserver about the cluster-suffix, and that it is challenging to pass kube-apiserver configuration options through REST or default logic.
Migrate legacy projects or find alternatives — The document lists this as an alternative only; it does not say why it was not chosen beyond repairing or replacing the traditional projects.

Relax hostname validation to accept FQDN strings — The design says doing so would cause the loss of the DNS resolution records for the pod, and it keeps subdomain and setHostnameAsFQDN handling tangled with the hostname.
Custom setHostnameAsFQDN value — setHostnameAsFQDN is currently a boolean, and changing it to a Custom value would be disruptive to the existing API.
Init container running privileged `hostname` command — The document states it can achieve the same goal but does not give a reason for rejecting it; it requires privileged mode.

evidence.quote: introduces a new field `hostnameOverride` for the podSpec, which, if set, once the API is GA will always be respected by the Kubelet
it will inevitably always carry the `cluster-suffix`, which will never be possible for services that expect to use DNS to match the hostname.
it is undoubtedly in conflict with the current pod's potential DNS records, and using it will bring more confusion to users.
However, since `setHostnameAsFQDN` is currently a boolean type, modifying it would be disruptive to the existing API.

summary: KEP-4781 proposes that kubelet restarts no longer reset containers' Started and Ready statuses to False, so pod status is preserved across restarts. It relies on the probe manager's detection results, and gated behind a deprecated feature gate ChangeContainerStatusOnKubeletRestart that lets admins temporarily re-enable the old behavior. Status is provisional, stage deprecated.
rationale: Today a kubelet restart sets Started and Ready to False for all pods on the node, disrupting services that were working. The KEP keeps the existing status on short restarts and lets the prober re-establish the real state, while a prolonged restart with NotReady node still sets Ready to false. Reviewers asked for a deprecation period, and the author said a wait of at least two release cycles is expected before the gate is locked.
alternatives: Earlier approach in KEP-4784 that inherits the Start state from the previous container and waits on startupProbe — The author found the implementation cumbersome with potential edge cases after tracing pod status transitions, and replaced it with the probe manager approach in PR #5493.
Full alpha to beta to GA feature gate lifecycle — The author said that since the change is not significant, a deprecated gate with a shorter lifecycle is enough.

Add a random wait before periodic probing after startup, as suggested by thockin — The author said their proposal does not include this and instead runs the probe after a random delay between 0 and 1 times PeriodSeconds, which the reviewer did not require.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes improving Pod readiness management in the kubelet to ensure that the status of Pods is not unilaterally modified, and is instead preserved during kubelet restarts.
consistently relying on the detection results of the probeManager. This approach simplifies the implementation and helps us avoid certain edge cases.
Deprecated feature gates typically have a shorter life cycle. Since this feature is not a significant change, we do not need it to go through the full life cycle
For a short kubelet restart, we can confidently assume that the container's state has not changed. Therefore, we can retain the container's state
I don't intend to move forward with this feature in v1.37. Deprecated feature gates typically require three releases before they are locked to their default values

summary: KEP-4785 proposes Resource State Metrics, a separate Kubernetes controller that generates metrics for custom resources from a cluster-scoped ResourceMetricsMonitor config, intended to replace Kube State Metrics' Custom Resource State API. Current status is provisional, alpha.
rationale: The Custom Resource State API in Kube State Metrics has limited scalability and its parsing logic is fragile, and its custom-resource behavior can crash Kube State Metrics and disrupt native metrics. The maintainers moved that API to maintenance-only mode and want a separate controller that can be deprecated and dropped from KSM. The KEP is still provisional, so no final decision beyond this proposal is recorded in the sources.
alternatives: Refactoring the Kube State Metrics Custom Resource State API — The readme says this has been done multiple times before and ended up in the same position owing to its limited scalability.
In-house effort tracked in kubernetes/kube-state-metrics#1978 — The readme mentions it only as an effort with similar goals; it gives no reason for not choosing it.

evidence.quote: the maintainers agreed on putting this on a "maintenance-only" mode in favor of a better solution that prioritizes scalability in the long run
Such a "solution" should allow the maintainers to deprecate and drop the Custom Resource State API from Kube State Metrics

summary: KEP-4800 proposes a new CPU Manager static policy option, "prefer-align-cpus-by-uncorecache", that groups CPU allocations by uncore cache (last-level cache) on an opt-in basis. The KEP is at status implementable, stage stable.
rationale: The default CPU Manager is unaware of split uncore cache architectures and can spread a container's CPUs across several uncore caches, causing noisy-neighbor contention and inter-cache latency. The option changes CPU assignment to sort CPUs by uncore cache and allocate to the fewest caches possible, on a best-effort basis. If alignment is not possible the workload is still admitted, and on hardware without split uncore caches the default behavior is unchanged.
alternatives: Delegate uncore cache affinity CPU allocation to the container runtime and plugins — The readme says that with this approach "the topology alignment granted by the Topology Manager within the kubelet is not compatible."

Use the existing static CPU Manager with manual assignment — The readme says this "requires manual assignment and for user to only run guaranteed pods with CPU sizes matching the corresponding uncore cache CPU group of the specific node."

Use a generic kernel-hierarchy-based alignment (hyperthread, core, cluster, die, socket) instead of cache-specific grouping — A reviewer (kad) suggested this as a more vendor-neutral approach, but the sources say teaching cAdvisor and CPU manager about real topology variations would be more complex, and the KEP stays focused on the cache implementation. The sources do not record a final decision on this.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to introduce a new CPU Manager static policy option, "prefer-align-cpus-by-uncorecache", that groups CPU resources by uncore cache where possible.
If the CPU Manager cannot align optimally, it will still admit the workload as before. Uncore cache assignment will be preferred but not a strict requirement for this feature.
If the node CPU topology does not support split uncore caches, enabling this feature will not impact on the default CPU allocation behavior.
If the hardware lack the capability (L3 cache or virtual cores) than the extra requirement is automatically satisfied, because the workload can't be possibly misaligned.
it's fine to drop compatibility with `distribute-cpus-across-numa`. We don't need a separate KEP, we just need to do that small scope change in a separate commit in addition to this one.

summary: KEP-4802 adds Windows graceful node shutdown: kubelet, running as a Windows service, detects a machine shutdown or restart via the service control handler and terminates pods gracefully. The KEP is marked implementable at stage beta, with status history showing implementable from 2024-10-10.
rationale: Pods are not terminated gracefully when a Windows node shuts down, which can break some workloads. The KEP makes kubelet aware of the Windows shutdown event so it can run pod lifecycle termination (including pre-stop hooks) before the machine stops. Reviewers required clarifying that the feature only works when kubelet runs as a native Windows service, not under nssm.exe, and debated whether kubelet should fail to start in that case.
outcome_reason: Per the sources, the 1.36 enhancements team on 2026-02-11 moved the KEP to Deferred, but the stated reason is only that the owner asked for it to be deferred ("Don't worry. I will move this to `Deferred`"). The sources do not give a fuller reason. The status given to me is implementable, stage beta, so I report that and note the later deferral from the issue thread.
alternatives: Run kubelet as a general Windows console application — The KEP says a general Windows application has little control over the shutdown timeout and is not reliable at receiving the shutdown event.
Use the WaitToKillServiceTimeout registry key to set the shutdown timeout — The KEP says Windows does not prefer this key for this purpose because it has a global effect on all services on the host.

Keep kubelet running under nssm.exe and rely on it to forward control signals — Reviewers said nssm.exe does not reliably pass the control signals to apps it runs, so the shutdown event would not reach kubelet.

evidence.quote: Focus on handling shutdown on machines where kubelet itself runs as a Windows service, on machines where kubelet is loaded through other loaders such as nssm.exe
General Windows application does not have much control on seting of the shutdown timeout value, and does not seem reliable to receive the shutdown event.
I don't believe nssm.exe passes the control signals to apps it runs - which is an advantage of sc.exe and needed for this scenario.
Don't worry. I will move this to `Deferred`. /remove-label tracked/yes /label tracked/no /milestone clear

summary: KEP-4815 proposes letting structured-parameters DRA allocate both full devices and fixed-size partitions of them by adding counter sets (SharedCounters) in ResourceSlice, a ConsumesCounters field on devices, and per-device node selection, so drivers can advertise overlapping partitions that the scheduler will never allocate concurrently. The KEP is in implementable status at stage beta.
rationale: DRA's move to structured parameters lost the ability to allocate partitions of a device on demand, and vendors could only advertise pre-partitioned, non-overlapping devices. The KEP keeps the user-facing request mechanism unchanged and adds counters that the scheduler tracks so conflicting overlapping partitions are never allocated together. Reviewers raised concerns about downgrade safety (old clients ignoring fields), which drove the later discussion of separate types and feature-gated failure behavior.
alternatives: Top-level single 'bag' of resources not tied to any device (Option 1) — Rejected because an abstract bag not tied to a device was perceived as non-intuitive, was verbose and error-prone, and did not support nested partitioning or sharing attributes.

Top-level 'DeviceShape' defining common capacities and resources (Option 4) — Rejected because it was not flexible enough for device-specific attributes and did not allow nested partitions or devices combining resources from more than one source.

Separate pool objects owned outside the ResourceSlice (Option 7) — Considered complicated because of lifecycle ownership of shared objects and what happens when they are missing; out of scope for the current KEP and may be considered later.

Adding the new fields directly to the existing BasicDevice type — Pohly noted that extending the API this way breaks downgrades: an old scheduler would ignore consumesCapacityFrom and could allocate mutually exclusive devices, so a new PartitionableDevice type was preferred.

evidence.quote: Instead, the proposed extensions provide the ability for a vendor to advertise "overlapping" partitions, such that the scheduler will never allocate conflicting ones at the same time.
Where it gets really bad (IMHO) is for `ConsumesCapacityFrom`: an old scheduler would ignore that constraint and might allocate two devices which are mutually exclusive.

we can't extend the API in this way because it breaks downgrades. An old scheduler will not recognize the new fields and attempt to allocate a device based solely on the fields that it DOES know about.
"Fail in sensible way" in this case means that the scheduler must ignore devices which depend on partitioning when `DRAPartitionalDevices` is turned off.

summary: KEP-4816 adds a prioritized list to DRA ResourceClaims so a workload can list alternative device requests ranked by preference; the scheduler uses the first satisfiable entry. The KEP is marked implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Workloads that need a GPU may fail to schedule when only a preferred model is available, and packaged workloads want to list alternatives without editing manifests. The design adds a FirstAvailable list (v1beta1, then Exactly/FirstAvailable in v1beta2) and a limited scoring step so nodes that satisfy higher-ranked subrequests are preferred. Reviewers debated the API shape (one-of semantics, backward compatibility with older clients) and whether cluster-autoscaler could support scoring, which was deferred.
alternatives: Sibling RankedDeviceRequests field next to Requests in DeviceClaim — Older clients would see a partial but valid request and not know it was incomplete; the one-of approach was chosen instead, per the discussion (rcomment:1795698383).
Creating multiple ResourceClaims behind an indirection layer — Raised by aojea as an idea (rcomment:1773821253); the sources do not record it being adopted.

Cluster-autoscaler scoring as a non-goal or alpha requirement — Scoring was made a beta criterion; CA integration was judged a major effort and to be evaluated for feasibility rather than committed (rcomment:1793928065, rcomment:1792637408).

evidence.quote: The order listed is considered a priority order, such that the scheduler will only try to use the second item in the list if it is unable to satisfy the first item
Made scoring a beta criteria; for alpha, it would not prefer one node over the other. Maybe we'll try to do that in alpha but for now it's a beta criteria.
To make it a one-of, we would force people to use either regular `Requests` OR `RankedRequests` in a given claim.
It was the ResourceClaim status which was left in beta, in contrast to what we had planned.

summary: KEP-4817 proposes adding a Devices field to ResourceClaim.Status so DRA drivers can report driver-specific status for each allocated device, with a standardized network-interface data shape (interface name, addresses, MAC). Its status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Allocated device characteristics set during configuration are invisible to users, which hinders debugging, verification, and integration with network services. The KEP adds per-device status to the claim, with a standard network data type as a first step. Design discussion centered on the API shape (opaque data vs. typed network data, one-of vs. non-exclusive fields) and on using "Allocated" in the name, and the KEP was approved by the DRA, PRR, and SIG Network reviewers.
alternatives: Separate Conditions and DeviceInfo fields with a one-of DeviceInfo type (Option 5) — Reviewers questioned whether the one-of construction helps; johnbelamaric said 'I am not sure the one-of construction actually helps' and suggested keeping the approach already in the KEP.

Single Data []DeviceData list with one populated sub-option per item — Proposed by johnbelamaric and refined by thockin as a slice variant. It was discussed but not recorded as the final choice; the API shape was deferred to API review.

Reporting status for devices that failed to allocate — pohly argued that if a device cannot be allocated, there is no reason to publish anything about it in the claim, because the same information would have to be copied to every claim that might use it.

evidence.quote: This proposal enhances the `ResourceClaim.Status` by adding a new field `Devices`. The new field allows drivers to report driver-specific device status data for each allocated device in a resource claim.

if a device cannot be allocated for a claim, then there is no reason to publish anything about it in the claim. Otherwise that same information would have to be added to all claims which potentially might have used such a device.
there were no major concerns or objections stated (though there was a soft suggestion that we might want to explore more options on how we handle the status if we have time)
So now @thockin has already approved but left an open question for @danwinship and @aojea so I will approve but leave the LGTM to them.

summary: KEP-4818 allows a zero value for the sleep duration of the PreStop Sleep action, which the parent KEP-3960 validation rejected. It was added behind the PodLifecycleSleepActionAllowZero feature gate and the KEP reached stable; its status is implemented.
rationale: Validation rejected sleep.seconds = 0 ("must be greater than 0"), even though time.After() accepts zero and returns immediately, so a zero sleep is effectively a no-op. Users such as those whose admission webhooks inject a default PreStop sleep need a no-op hook to opt out. The proposal relaxes validation for new resources and updates while keeping existing zero-second resources working during downgrades.
alternatives: Run exec preStop hook like ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 0"] — Requires a sleep binary in the image; the sleep action already exists as a PreStop hook, so allowing zero there is easier.
Support negative values or an infinite sleep as well — Non-goals: negative values have the same effect as zero, and the KEP does not aim to delay pod termination indefinitely.
Add a kubelet-side feature gate check for zero values — Kubelet already accepts zero via time.After(0), so the sreeram-venkitesh comment judged the gate unnecessary at the kubelet level.

evidence.quote: It however doesn’t accept zero as a valid value for the sleep duration seconds. This KEP aims to add support for setting a value of zero with the sleep action of the PreStop hook.

Introduce a `PodLifecycleSleepActionAllowZero` feature gate which is disabled by default. When the feature gate is enabled, the `validateSleepAction` method would allow values greater than or equal to zero
Currently, kubelet accepts `0`. No validation is done at the kubelet level. The feature gate for `PodLifecycleSleepAction` is used inside `runSleepHandler` function
This KEP is for allowing zero value for the sleep duration and this was in alpha in 1.32.
thank you for updating the history as well! Very thoughtful of you! /lgtm /approve

summary: KEP-4827 proposes a /statusz endpoint on all core Kubernetes components that returns standardized, low-overhead data about the component's basic information, health, versioning, build information and compatibility. Current status is implementable, stage beta.
rationale: Operators currently must dig through logs or configuration to learn a component's build and version details, and version mismatches are hard to spot. The KEP adds a z-page-style endpoint served by the component itself, scoped to the primary serving process only.
