summary: KEP-5295 proposes KYAML, a strict subset ("dialect") of YAML, as a new kubectl output format (`-o=kyaml`) and as the preferred format for project documentation and examples. The KEP status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Conventional block-style YAML is whitespace-sensitive and has type-coercion traps (e.g. "NO" parsed as bool, "11:00" as a sexagesimal number), which make hand-editing and templating (e.g. Helm) error-prone, while JSON lacks comments. KYAML uses flow style with always-double-quoted values, unquoted safe keys, and {} and [] delimiters so it is not whitespace-sensitive and remains valid YAML. The KEP states it is not required of users and that existing YAML output is retained.
alternatives: Use JSON (or JSON with comments stripped before submission) — The KEP says JSON lacks comments and is particular about trailing commas and quoted keys, and that most configuration tooling is built around YAML.

Adopt an existing JSON-like format such as HJSON, JSONC, or JSON5 — The KEP says these would require choosing between them, taking new dependencies, and learning new grammars, while KYAML has none of those drawbacks.
Add styling hints to go-yaml instead of implementing the encoder — The KEP says this would require work in go-yaml, which is EOL, so it defers this path until the revival fork is available.

Implement the formatting rules for kubectl without naming the format — A rcomment from lmktfy says they discount this option; the discussion notes that people would call it KYAML regardless and a name helps clarify the pretty-printing.

evidence.quote: This format is a strict subset (aka "dialect") of standard YAML, and so should be parseable by the existing ecosystem.
KYAML is primarily a specification of output. Since KYAML is a subset of YAML, it should always be accepted as input
it's alpha; we can get feedback (including before the release) and revise what we do
nobody is **forced** to use this, the KEP retains support for the existing yaml output and of course decoding remains untouched
Specify a YAML dialect which is 100% compatible with existing parsers and tooling.

summary: KEP-5304 proposes exposing DRA device attributes and other metadata to containers by having the DRA kubelet plugin framework write per-request metadata JSON files and bind-mount them into containers via CDI, so workloads like KubeVirt can read device details (e.g. PCIe address, mdev UUID) without custom controllers. Status is implementable, stage beta.
rationale: Consumers today must chase claim status, then ResourceSlice, to find device attributes, which pushes projects like KubeVirt into fragile custom controllers. The framework-assisted design keeps the scheduler and kubelet unchanged, and drivers opt in through a plugin-level flag or option. Metadata is written per request so containers only see the requests they reference. Discussion moved the design from a shared driver-names directory to driver-owned per-driver directories, and from mutable metadata to a prepare-time model for network drivers.
alternatives: Downward API environment variables populated by kubelet — The readme says the downward API only surfaces one attribute at a time and that the approach would have been more ergonomic, but it was not chosen because drivers would have to populate env vars and the design needed multi-level lookup. Its reasons are only partly stated in the sources; the readme's Drawbacks section compares it directly.

Shared /var/run/dra-device-attributes directory keyed by claim and request, with driver-name files — A reviewer (pohly) argued the shared directory is not portable to Windows or across host OSes and complicates cleanup. The design was revised to keep metadata under each driver's own plugin directory, and a driverNames file was dropped because drivers would race writing it.

Allowlist of attributes exposed to pods — Reviewers (johnbelamaric) said no allowlist is needed because the feature does not expand data beyond what users with read access to ResourceSlice can already obtain; the KEP was to be swept to remove it.
Feature gate for the feature — johnbelamaric stated there is no feature gate because the only upstream changes are to a library used by downstream components, which may do their own feature gating.

evidence.quote: Containers only see metadata for the requests they reference (via `resources.claims[].request`), providing proper isolation when a claim has multiple requests used by different containers.
When the flag is set, the framework enables the metadata code path; when unset, the feature is fully disabled — no CDI specs or metadata files are generated.
I don't see a need to use the same directory for all drivers. These `metadata.json` files are driver-owned files which are accessed through the CDI files.
There's no feature gate because the only upstream changes are to a library used by downstream components, which may or may not have their own way to do feature gating.
The driverNames file proposed to be filled by different drivers will cause issues as each driver will start to write to it and race.

summary: KEP-5307 adds per-container restartRules so kubelet restarts a container on specified exit codes, even when the Pod has restartPolicy=Never. The KEP is at status implementable, stage beta.
rationale: AI/ML training Pods must distinguish retryable failures (restart in place) from hardware failures (reschedule the Pod), which restartPolicy alone cannot express. The design adds a container-level restartRules field, with the Job controller unaffected because kubelet restarts keep the Pod Running. Reviewers pushed for a coherent restart story across pod restartPolicy, container restartPolicy and rules, and the PR was approved as an incremental step.
alternatives: Add a new RestartPolicy enum value such as RuleBased — Reviewer thockin noted RestartPolicy overloads the meaning to include sidecar, and the thread concluded a new enum value could not be added; the restartRules name was kept instead.

Use restartPolicy OnFailure at the Pod level — The readme says OnFailure does not work because hardware failures must produce a Pod failure and rescheduling, and the pod failure policy is not compatible with OnFailure.

Redesign restart semantics first with a new exitCodes-based restartPolicy model — The sources show this was proposed by thockin as a broader design, but the PR was narrowed to restartRules as a targeted per-container addition; the sources do not record a final decision to adopt that model.

evidence.quote: This will allow users to configure special exit codes of the container to be treated as non-failure and restart the container in-place even if the Pod has a restartPolicy=Never.
this PR only introduces `restartRules` as a targeted, per-container override and does not change the existing `restartPolicy`.
API LGTM overall - all my comments are minor and this doesn't have to be final API /approve
I remain some concerns, but those concerns shouldn't block we move forward this alpha feature.
So I accept that I am going to be grumpy. I think we CAN get to a place where container `restartPolicy` is less restricted

summary: KEP-5311 relaxes Service name validation from DNS-1035 label rules (apimachineryvalidation.NameIsDNS1035Label) to DNS label rules (NameIsDNSLabel), so Service names may start with a digit. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
rationale: Service name validation was stricter than for most other Kubernetes resource names. Relaxing it removes the NameIsDNS1035Label check that only Services used, and lets users follow the same naming conventions as their other resources. The stated drawback is that third-party tooling may not be compatible with the new validation.
alternatives: Keep NameIsDNS1035Label for Services — The readme says Service name validation is stricter than most other resource names and the change is meant to bring it in line with them. The Alternatives section is marked N/A, so the sources do not record a rejected alternative.

Remove NameIsDNS1035Label from the whole codebase — This is listed as a non-goal: the KEP does not change validation for other resource types, though the readme mentions removing the function as part of the change.

evidence.quote: Additionally, this change also allows users to name their Services with the same conventions as other of their resources, ie: Service names can now start with a digit.
The proposal is to change this validation to `apimachineryvalidation.NameIsDNSLabel`, allowing Service names to start with a digit.

summary: KEP-5313 proposes a vendor-neutral, namespaced, data-only PlacementDecision API that standardizes the "which clusters" output of multicluster schedulers, so consumers (GitOps engines, orchestrators, rollout controllers, AI/ML pipelines) can read one format from any scheduler. Its status is provisional at alpha stage, since 2025-11-25.
rationale: Each multicluster scheduler publishes its own placement-decision API, so every consumer needs custom integration code per scheduler, which the KEP calls an integration explosion. The KEP scopes the standard to the decision output only: it leaves placement requests and workload deployment vendor-specific, and it requires each cluster reference to map to a ClusterProfile. The status is provisional, and the sources do not describe any review outcome or acceptance beyond that.
alternatives: Status quo: each scheduler ships its own placement API — The KEP says this leads to consumer bloat and vendor lock-in, with each consumer writing separate code for every scheduler.
Extend the Work API to carry scheduling details — The KEP says this overloads a workload syncing API with scheduling details, coupling the where with the what.

evidence.quote: This KEP introduces a vendor neutral `PlacementDecision` API that standardizes the output of multicluster placement calculations.
Example: 10 consumers with 10 schedulers needs 100 separate integrations today, but only 20 integrations with this API
What this API standardizes: The "which clusters" answer (the decision output).
Extending `Work API`: overloads a workload syncner API with scheduling details which couples the where with the what.

summary: KEP-5325 proposes a new HPA field, SelectionStrategy, so HPAs can choose how pods are selected for metric collection: LabelSelector (default, current behavior) or OwnerReference (only pods owned by the target workload). The KEP is in implementable status at alpha stage.
rationale: HPA collects metrics from every pod matching the target's label selector, so unrelated pods such as Jobs or other Deployments that share labels can distort scaling. The KEP adds a selection strategy field to address this while keeping existing configurations working by defaulting to LabelSelector. The source gives the Job-sharing-label example as the motivating case.
alternatives: Keep selecting all pods matching the label selector (current behavior) — This is the behavior that causes incorrect scaling when unrelated pods share labels; the default is kept only for backward compatibility.
Future selection strategies such as Annotations — The source mentions these only as possible future extensions of the enumerated type; they are not part of this proposal.

evidence.quote: it collects metrics from all pods that match the target workload's label selector. This can lead to incorrect scaling decisions when unrelated pods
We propose adding a new field to the HPA specification called `SelectionStrategy` that allows users to specify how pods should be selected for metric collection
If set to `LabelSelector` (default): Uses the current behavior of selecting all pods that match the target workload's label selector.
Maintain backward compatibility with existing HPA configurations

summary: KEP-5328 proposes a Node Declared Features framework: a new field declaredFeatures in node .status, populated by the Kubelet, that the kube-scheduler, admission controllers and the API server use to avoid placing or validating pods on nodes lacking required feature-gated features during version skew. Status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Version skew means nodes may run older Kubelets without a newly enabled feature, so the scheduler may place a pod needing that feature on an incompatible node, leading to runtime or Kubelet admission failures. Declaring features on nodes lets control plane components handle this upfront, leaving the pod Pending with an event explaining the unmet requirement. The design limits declared features to those directly actionable by control plane components to keep the list manageable.
alternatives: Node capabilities/feature lists with long-term or swap-style capabilities — Reviewers (sergeykanzhelev, wojtek-t) objected that capabilities could grow the NodeStatus object indefinitely and be misused for configuration like swap or runtime handlers; scope was narrowed to temporary skew-related capabilities.

Automatic deprecation of capabilities once a feature becomes GA — The author moved automatic deprecation to Alternatives Considered after reviewer concerns about poor code hygiene and scalability; it is not part of the proposal.
SemVer-based filtering in Node Selectors — Raised by pravk03 as a potential alternative for further exploration; the sources do not say why it was not chosen.

Using NFD or swap-specific node status/allocatables instead — Reviewers suggested allocatable resources or other statuses for non-feature-gate indications such as swap or SELinux vs AppArmor; the KEP text does not record a final decision on these.

evidence.quote: This proposal introduces a new field `declaredFeatures` to node's `.status` to expose information which the kube-scheduler, admission controller or the API server would use to make more informed decisions.
A pod without a matching node remains `Pending` with an event that details the unmet feature requirement, providing actionable user feedback
To ensure the number of declared features remains manageable, the design requires that every declared feature be directly actionable by a control plane component.
The KEP can be scoped for temporary capabilities to solve version skew use cases.
we went away from this goal with the concern that the list will ever grow with little value and no option to purge.

summary: KEP-5339 proposed a standardized, pluggable way for controllers to obtain credentials for clusters represented by ClusterProfile CRs, by exec'ing external credential plugins that reuse the Kubeconfig exec protocol. The KEP is now in status "replaced" at alpha stage.
rationale: ClusterProfile inventories lacked a standard way to get credentials for the clusters they describe, and previous attempts had failed. The proposal uses exec'd plugins, so cluster managers can supply credential methods without embedding them in controller code or recompiling. It reuses the Kubeconfig external credential protocol to ease implementation.
outcome_reason: The status history records a move to "replaced" on 2026-06-23, but the provided sources do not say what replaced it or why. No replacing KEP is named in the sources.
alternatives: Alternatives section of the design document — The excerpt names an Alternatives section but gives no content, so the alternatives considered are not stated in the sources.

evidence.quote: This KEP provides a standardized way to obtain credentials for Clusters when using ClusterProfile and makes it pluggable to allow the diverse ecosystem to support the multitude of ways to obtain credentials.
Previous attempts at writing credentials have failed and we believe that a plugin model, also reusing known flows, will help solve the "credentials" need for ClusterProfiles.
Plugins would be exec'ed by the controller so that they don't need be built-in the binary, allowing flexibility into writing their own credential plugins
we propose to reuse the exec approach and protocol used for external credentials in Kubeconfig (but not the configuration part of kubeconfig).

summary: KEP-5365 adds an imageRef field to the pod status for ImageVolumes so the digest of the image used by an ImageVolume is reported, as containerStatuses already does for containers. The KEP is marked implementable at alpha.
rationale: ImageVolume digests are not advertised in pod status, unlike container image digests in containerStatuses, which hurts monitoring, git-ops workflows, and KubeVirt live migration. The KEP adds a status field and leaves the pod spec unchanged. Reviewers pushed for the field to be named imageRef to match CRI, and asked for it to be documented in the CRI field so implementations know what to report.
alternatives: Name the field imageID or ImageDigest — A reviewer objected to imageID as ambiguous and said it had caused issues before; the team settled on imageRef, the same name used for container statuses.

Add API server validation that rejects imageRef for non-ImageVolume volumes — The sources raise this as a question (sergeykanzhelev suggested it so edge cases are avoided) but do not record a decision on it.

Keep the field flat in the volume status — deads2k suggested an intermediary struct for ImageVolume-specific status to match the discriminated union used in the volume spec; haircommander and iholder101 agreed in principle, but the sources do not confirm the final shape.
