summary: KEP-5866 proposes server-side sharded LIST and WATCH in the Kubernetes API server, letting clients request only the events in a hash range via a new selector-style parameter. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: Client-side sharding still delivers the full event stream to every replica, so each replica pays the network and deserialization cost of discarded events. The KEP moves filtering to the API server so each replica receives only its shard, while clients still choose their own hash ranges. Reviewers accepted the alpha scope, and the exact request syntax was deferred to API review.
alternatives: Label-based sharding (client writes shard info into object labels and filters on them) — Reviewers said labels need admission or another controller to set them, leak controller topology into object state, and are hard to reshard. The readme says: "persisting the sharding information into the object state seems like a slippery slope because of admission/controller and also being super difficult to reshard later."

Modulo-based partitioning (hash % ShardingCount == ShardingIndex) — The KEP chose consistent hash ranges so clients can reshard without moving every key. The reviewer said: "fixing the partitioning to be modulo % is also not ideal for controllers wanting reshards to not move every key around".

Extending fieldSelector or using CEL expressions such as fieldSelector=range(...) or selector=0 < hash(...) < 100 — The author argued that extending fieldSelector would push toward CEL and that complex CEL makes parsing and validation harder for normal GET requests. The author said: "Having more complex CEL expressions seems like extra overhead as it would make parsing and validating the field more difficult".

Separate ListOptions fields for sharding (ShardingIndex, ShardingCount, ShardingLabelKey, HashFunc) — Listed in alternatives with the con that it increases the surface area of meta/v1.ListOptions with watch-specific fields and makes future evolution less flexible. The exact grammar was left to API review.

summary: KEP-5882 proposes a new `.spec.podReplacementPolicy` field on Deployments so users can choose whether new pods are created only after terminating pods finish or immediately. The KEP is in implementable status at alpha stage.
rationale: Deployments handle terminating pods inconsistently: Recreate waits for terminating pods, while RollingUpdate and scale-up do not, so pod count can exceed spec.replicas. This causes extra node autoscaling, slower rollouts under contention, and lost visibility into work done by terminating pods. The KEP adds a per-Deployment policy, modeled on the Job field, to let users pick the behavior.
alternatives: Implement the behavior in a separate controller that manages ReplicaSets — The KEP says there is a need for this to be implemented by the Deployment controller, because many existing workloads can benefit from this feature.

summary: KEP-5945 adds an optional flag on ResourceSlice (originally two fields, SkipNodePrepare and SkipNodeUnprepare, later reduced to a single boolean, SkipNodeOperations) so that DRA devices needing no node-side prepare/unprepare can skip those kubelet gRPC calls. Status is implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: Kubelet currently calls NodePrepareResources and NodeUnprepareResources for every claim, and a driver that is gone can leave pods stuck in Terminating during unprepare. Reviewers wanted the skip set on ResourceSlice rather than DeviceClass, since the driver author knows whether a device needs preparation. The split into two fields was dropped because prepare without unprepare was judged to add complexity without a real need, and a single flag was chosen instead. Reviewers also flagged risks (driver mislabeling, slice updates after allocation copying the flag) that the sources do not show as fully resolved.
alternatives: Set the skip fields on DeviceClass — johnbelamaric said DeviceClass is for the cluster administrator, who could easily make a mistake with this being at that level; the driver author should decide, so the field moved to the slice level.

Two separate fields SkipNodePrepare and SkipNodeUnprepare — Reviewers found the true/false combination fragile (driver missing at teardown); johnbelamaric and pohly preferred one flag because prepare-without-unprepare only makes sense with extra cleanup and adds complexity. The KEP was updated to a single boolean.

Put the fields on each Device instead of the ResourceSlice — troychiu said placing them on Device seems repetitive and might inflate the ResourceSlice size; mortent noted devices needing and not needing preparation can be split across multiple slices in the same pool.

Copy device attributes into ResourceClaim status so kubelet can write CDI metadata directly — johnbelamaric said this was discussed for KEP-5304 and rejected: copying all attributes to status would be a huge size increase on the object.

evidence.quote: I updated the KEP to introduce fields in `ResourceSlice`. Placing them on `Device` seems repetitive and might inflate the size of `ResourceSlice` instance.
`DeviceClass` is for the cluster administrator, who could easily make a mistake with this being at that level.
Ok. @troychiu how about we go back to just a single boolean then? Maybe `SkipNodeOperations`?
I prefer to not add functionality and complexity, no matter how small, when there is no real need for it.
Before lgtm it, I need these review comments to be addressed

summary: KEP-5958 proposes letting clients opt out of receiving metadata.managedFields in API responses via an Accept parameter (drop=metadata.managedFields), implemented as a serializer mode with a distinct identifier. Status is implementable, stage alpha, but the sources show it was dropped from the v1.37 release and deferred toward v1.38.
rationale: Clients such as kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler already strip managedFields client-side, yet the API server still serializes them, costing CPU, bandwidth, and client GC. The KEP moves the stripping to encode time via an Accept parameter. Reviewers questioned the performance benefit, the per-client versus per-request configuration, and server-side safety; the maintainers then agreed to drop it from v1.37 due to negative performance implications of the current implementation.
outcome_reason: The sources say the feature will not be completed in v1.37 because of negative performance implications of the current implementation proposal. The maintainers agreed to drop it from the v1.37 release and have a rough idea for v1.38. The KEP status field still reads implementable, stage alpha, and the sources do not say whether it was later re-milestoned.
alternatives: Per-client configuration via rest.Config — Reviewers argued it is the wrong place: it cannot express per-object or per-informer choices, and a single binary watching multiple resources may need different behavior. The KEP later dropped the hard rest.Config commitment and said the client-go surface would be decided at implementation.

ListOptions flag such as excludeManagedFields=true — The KEP's Alternatives section rejected it because Accept parameters are the standard Kubernetes way to control object representation. A reviewer later suggested ListOptions as an alternative for per-informer control.
General-purpose field selection — The KEP lists it as a non-goal: it is a much larger undertaking discussed for years, and the targeted solution leaves room for future generalization.
Client-side stripping only (status quo) — The KEP says relying on client-side transforms still incurs API server CPU, network, and client GC costs, which is the problem it aims to remove.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes using an `Accept` header parameter (`drop=metadata.managedFields`) to allow clients to opt-out of receiving `metadata.managedFields` in API responses.
This won't be completed in v1.37 due negative performance implications of the current implementation proposal.
I've spoken with @yongruilin and we've agreed this should be dropped from the v1.37 release.
Confirming that KEP #5958 will be dropped from the v1.37 release. Updating the status to `Removed from Milestone` and clearing the milestone.
The server-side gate controls exposure of a new client-controlled capability that has never been run in the kube-apiserver.

summary: KEP-5963 proposes an optional compatibilityGroups field on DRA devices so the scheduler can refuse to co-allocate devices that a driver marks as mutually incompatible (e.g., MIG vs. full-GPU style partitioning). It is implementable at alpha as of 2026-06-15.
rationale: Existing counter-based constraints cannot express "devices in a set are mutually exclusive unless they share a group," so the scheduler can allocate incompatible devices that only fail at preparation time. The KEP adds a per-device group list where devices are compatible only if they share at least one group, and devices without groups are only compatible with other devices without groups. Reviewers pushed for alpha-stage safeguards: ignore devices using the field when the gate is off, and have drivers detect dropped fields and fail rather than publish silently wrong slices.
alternatives: Shared counter with capacity one for mutual exclusion — Such a counter would have to be decremented once for the first device from a compatible set, not once per device, and this cannot be expressed at the moment.

Default of 'not compatible with any group' or regex/wildcard group matching — The author worried that a default other than 'compatible with all devices' would brick existing devices on upgrade until drivers are updated.

Scheduler reads groups back from the ResourceSlice of allocated devices — Reviewers noted a driver may remove the definition of an allocated device while it is in use; the KEP instead copies group info into the allocation result as the source of truth.

evidence.quote: A shared counter with a capacity of one can ensure mutual exclusion, but this cannot be used here: such a counter would have to be decremented once
My worry is that if the default is anything other than "compatible with all devices", this will introduce API breakage.
Other features like consumable capacity therefore copy all relevant information into the allocation result, then use that as source of truth. You should do the same.
At alpha, add a check for the new field if the feature gate is off. If the field is non-empty, ignore the device.
the scheduler >= 1.37 will ignore the devices instead of doing incorrect allocations.

summary: KEP-5966 proposes a new server-streaming RangeStream RPC on the etcd KV service that reuses RangeRequest, paginates internally with adaptive chunk sizing, pins a single MVCC revision, and derives the total count from streamed keys. Status is implementable, stage beta.
rationale: The unary Range RPC buffers the entire response, causing server memory spikes, and paginated Range calls recompute the total count by walking the full index on every page. RangeStream addresses both by chunking results and computing the count once from the running tally. Reviewers agreed that server-side chunking avoids long-running read transactions from single large range requests, and the count was moved to the last chunk to avoid an extra tree scan.
alternatives: Fall back transparently from RangeStream to unary Range when sort order is non-default or the server is old — Reviewers chose to reject non-default sort order with an error and have clients use unary Range, since the contract differs and the server switching silently was judged less sensible.

Have MVCC return up to X bytes per page, deciding page size from expected result size, instead of adaptive chunking — Raised by serathius as an alternative in review; the excerpt does not record a decision against it, and the design kept adaptive chunking.

Reuse the existing Kubernetes-side List interface method with a Stream option instead of a separate ListStream method — Reviewers (jefftree, serathius) argued that reassembling the stream into one response would force bypassing the interface for concurrent chunk decoding, so a non-blocking ListStream was preferred; ahrtr's ListOptions Stream suggestion was adopted only for the etcd client-side design.

evidence.quote: The server performs pagination internally with adaptive chunk sizing and pins to a single MVCC revision for consistency.
The total count is derived from the running tally of streamed keys, eliminating the separate index traversal required by paginated Range.
returning an error and getting the client to use unary Range seems to make more sense.
returning the count on the first chunk will require a full traversal to obtain the chunk. If we return on the last chunk, we can keep a running count and avoid the duplicate traversal.
The batched range requests was band-aid added quickly many years ago to avoid sending large range requests with long running read txns to etcd.

summary: KEP-5975 proposes that API directories contain only the code that differs from the standard pattern, with a trivial storage registration (registry.NewREST with a RESTConfig) and generated or default wiring for codegen, validation, field wiping, generation management, and feature-gated field dropping. Status is provisional (stage stable).
rationale: Every strategy file in pkg/registry/ reimplements the same ~12 methods across 67 files (~12,000 lines), and this has caused costly mistakes. The KEP builds on declarative validation (KEP-4153, KEP-5073) and declarative defaulting (KEP-1929) to drive standard behavior from types.go tags. It keeps backward compatibility: external users must opt in to the new behaviors.
alternatives: Declarative tags for all strategy behavior — Tags break down for complex validation options, cross-field generation tracking, custom warnings, and injected dependencies; the KEP keeps strategy and storage definitions in Go for type safety.

Enabling generators via a per-directory apigroup.yaml-style config file — Not chosen as the KEP text; the author removed references to YAML files after review feedback. Discussion treated it as a separate, related change (kubernetes PR 138657).

Merging the narrower enforcement change in kubernetes PR 138577 — Mentioned by the author as the alternative to this broader change, which would consume more review bandwidth; the sources do not state why it was not taken.
Reflection for generic field wiping — Raised by the author as an alternative to the current generic wiping approach; the sources do not record a decision on it.

evidence.quote: Every strategy file in `pkg/registry/` implements the same ~12 methods: status clearing, generation bumping, validation delegation, and feature-gate field dropping.
All changes will be backwards compatible. External users of API frameworks and code generators will need to opt-in to the new behaviors.
These behaviors should be driven by information already available in the API definition (types.go files) such as declarative validation and feature gate tags.
Existing generator usage is unchanged. All flags/args/tags will continue to be supported.
I've removed the reference to yaml files and responded to all feedback.

summary: KEP-5978 proposed a cluster-scoped ClusterResourceClaimTemplate in Kubernetes so Pods and PodGroups could reference a shared template by name. The KEP was withdrawn and the capability is to be built out-of-tree instead.
rationale: Reviewers questioned whether cluster admins would actually manage ClusterResourceClaimTemplates, since ResourceClaims are normally part of the workload itself. Maintainers judged that a ClusterResourceClaimTemplate only adds value as an admin-level abstraction, and that the in-tree API surface was not justified for 1.37. The group agreed to move the idea to an out-of-tree controller that copies templates into namespaces.
outcome_reason: Withdrawn because the maintainers concluded that the feature is most appropriately done out-of-tree, and they did not want to add the in-tree API surface for 1.37. The sources say "we don't proceed with this KEP for 1.37 (and potentially never)" and that the decision was to "withdraw this KEP".
alternatives: Pod field resolves to a namespaced ResourceClaimTemplate and falls back to a ClusterResourceClaimTemplate of the same name — liggitt said ambiguous resolution is hard to reason about and can cause race conditions, and it changes the meaning of the field for existing clients.

Separate ResourceClaimTemplateRef field with kind (ResourceClaimTemplate or ClusterResourceClaimTemplate) — pohly said having two equivalent ways to reference a template is confusing; he preferred a separate clusterResourceClaimTemplateName field.

Authorize ClusterResourceClaimTemplate usage by checking whether the pod's service account can get the template — pohly said the controller has no credentials of the user who created the reference, and that referencing a cluster template grants no extra privileges.

Separate CRD and controller that generates namespaced ResourceClaimTemplates — Not chosen as the in-tree path; it was instead the basis of the out-of-tree direction the group settled on (a controller copying RCTs from a special namespace).

evidence.quote: I think that's reasonable. @troychiu WDYT? Instead of doing this in-tree, we create a separate controller in k-sigs? We would therefore withdraw this KEP.
I think that makes sense. Maintaining an out-of-tree controller looks good enough. I have marked this KEP as `withdrawn`.
ClusterResourceClaimTemplate makes sense when it will be used as an additional abstraction between cluster admin and users
We decided that it is most appropriately done out-of-tree. For example, a controller that copies RCTs from a special namespace to other namespaces (that's one approach).
ambiguous reference resolution from an object depending on what else exists at a given point in time is pretty hard to reason about

summary: KEP-5996 proposes a kubelet configuration field, DefaultPodSysctls, that applies default sysctls to all Pods, including static Pods. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: The sources do not give a full problem statement; reviewers asked for a concrete example of a sysctl an administrator would need to adjust across all Pods. Reviewers also asked that the KEP exclude per-namespace filtering and that unknown sysctls fail validation, so that typos are caught early. Kubelet validation was aligned with the container runtime, which ignores unnamespaced sysctls.
alternatives: Ignore non-existing sysctls silently — Reviewer sergeykanzhelev said failing fast helps detect configuration issues, and asked for at least a log message rather than silent ignoring.
Check sysctl existence in the kubelet against kernel files — Commenter veraqin said this check might be expensive, and that value type and range can only be validated by the Linux kernel.
Tie DefaultPodSysctls to AllowedUnsafeSysctls — veraqin said DefaultPodSysctls is unrelated to AllowedUnsafeSysctls, which controls what sysctls user workloads may set.

evidence.quote: add non-goal to not include any additional filtering on which Pods those default will apply to. For e.g. we do not want to have per-Pod-namespace sets of sysctls
specify that static pods are also in-scope. Mentioning them explicitly helps to not forget to add tests for them
Yes, container runtime only does namespace validation, and thus Kubelet will also add the same validation.
This is not supported on Windows, should be denied in validation step if set on Windows
`DefaultPodSysctls` is unrelated to `AllowedUnsafeSysctls`. `AllowedUnsafeSysctls` is used for admins to decide what sysctls can be set inside user workloads.

summary: KEP-5999 proposes HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) support for kubelet container probes, currently at implementable/alpha for v1.37. The discussion settled on adding a Protocol field (HTTPProbeProtocol, pointer, with HTTP2 value) to HTTPGetAction rather than a dedicated h2cGet probe type, with no host override and no HTTP/1 fallback.
rationale: Reviewers asked whether h2c should be built into the kubelet rather than handled by exec probes, and whether to extend httpGet or add a new probe type. The lead reviewer (aojea) preferred a pointer Protocol field because it leaves room for HTTP/3 and keeps a smaller API surface, while the dedicated type avoids new validation rules. Maintainers asked that new behavior be additive, so with the gate off the field is ignored, and the probe is identifiable from the pod spec so no new metric label is needed for alpha.
alternatives: Dedicated h2cGet probe type (mirrors the gRPC probe, numeric port only, no host field) — Discussion favored extending httpGet with a Protocol field for a smaller API surface and future HTTP/3 support; the dedicated type needed extra validation rules for host, named ports and scheme. The sources do not record a final formal rejection of this option beyond that preference.
scheme: HTTP2_CLEARTEXT on httpGet — Reviewers asked for a section explaining why it was rejected in favor of a new probe; the sources do not give the detailed reasoning beyond that request.

Separate protocol label on prober_probe_total metric — Reviewer said no new metric label is needed for alpha since there is no fallback and the probe is uniquely identifiable; a later reviewer (haircommander) raised cardinality concerns about the existing metric's labels.
Include host override for h2c probes — Validation rejects host override when protocol is HTTP2, matching gRPC probes that always target the pod IP, to avoid health-checking a different endpoint.

evidence.quote: I'm leaning towards adding `Protocol *HTTPProbeProtocol` , as we may want to have to add http/3 later and this paves the way
i think its good, will add a validation rule to reject host override when protocol is set to HTTP2, same logic as gRPC probes always targeting pod IP.
Given the above, I believe the correct way, and this is how we've always treated new things is to ignore the new field.
if there is never a fallback and the probe can be uniquily identified anyways, I do not see a reason to add a new metric
I am a bit concerned about this metric. I didn't realize it had pod_uid, pod and containers, which means it has very high cardinality.

summary: KEP-6012 proposes a CompositePodGroup API (a Workload-level type for nested groups of PodGroups) for sig-scheduling. Its status is implementable at alpha, from 2026-06-15.
rationale: The KEP models a hierarchy of groups (CompositePodGroup over PodGroups) so the scheduler can treat a multi-layer workload as one scheduling unit. Reviewers questioned whether CompositePodGroup should be a distinct type rather than a PodGroup variant, citing different concepts. Discussion also flagged open issues for later phases, such as heterogeneous multi-layer groups, priorities, and UnschedulableAndUnresolvable semantics, which were deferred to Beta or follow-ups. The source comments do not record an explicit final resolution of the type-distinction question beyond the KEP's implementable status.
alternatives: Reuse PodGroup with a policy that determines the object types it can reference (e.g. HomogeneousSchedulingPolicy) — Reviewer dom4ha argued Pods and PodGroups need different definitions and that the type-based policy claim needed more justification; the sources do not record a final rejection of this option.
Use a dedicated type for groups of not-yet-existing objects (reservations) — Raised by dom4ha as a possible alternative; the sources do not say it was adopted or rejected.

Single CompositePodGroupTemplate instead of a slice in the Workload spec — Raised by mm4tt as a trade-off to document; the sources say the rationale should be documented but do not give the authors' full reasoning.

evidence.quote: The second one (CompositePodGroup) no longer represents a group of pods - it represents a complex structure of potentially nested groups.
In Alpha we can assume that everything within a tree has the same priority. For Beta, we will need to discuss different options
In alpha, we'll be doing a single pass only.
The assumption that we only keep roots in the queue simplifies the logic and mental model significantly, and I'd prefer to stick with it.
It's very well written KEP that is easy to read. The approach looks good to me including the details.

summary: KEP-6030 proposes allowing dynamic resize of memory-backed (tmpfs) emptyDir volumes via the pod /resize subresource, so the volume size can change in place alongside memory requests/limits. Its status is implementable, stage alpha, as of 2026-06-09.
rationale: Memory-backed emptyDir volumes are charged against container and pod memory cgroups, and users want to resize the volume together with memory limits so the volume keeps a fixed share of pod memory. The discussion settled on restricting the feature to memory-backed emptyDir (not PVCs or inline CSI ephemeral volumes) and to cgroup v2, which avoids the coordination problems of general volume expansion. Reviewers (dchen1107 approved and lgtm'd; kannon92 approved with a hold for PRR nits) accepted the design after the shrink-safety and accounting questions were answered.
alternatives: Generic volume expansion for all volume types (PVCs, inline CSI ephemeral volumes) — jsafrane noted kubelet has no knowledge of CSI volume size parameters, and the KEP restricts scope to emptyDir types; msau42 said restricting to emptyDir avoids the concurrency/coordination problem.

Add a top-level VolumeStatus capacity field or a generic per-volume status — tallclair objected to EmptyDir-specific fields at the top level; natasha41575 said a generic capacity field would be confusing, so the status was placed under VolumeStatus.EmptyDir.SizeLimit.

Have the kubelet create an allocatedPod object and coordinate volume and cgroup actuation through it — natasha41575 found it more complicated while keeping strict actuation ordering between cgroups and volume mounts, and was not convinced it was better.
Support cgroup v1 as well — The discussion chose to support only cgroup v2; on cgroup v1 nodes kubelet marks the resize as Infeasible.

evidence.quote: only supporting cgroup v2 for this feature SGTM. I added to the KEP that if kubelet sees this resize request on a node with cgroup v1, it will mark the resize as `Infeasible`.
I'm not proposing that all volume resizes be done via the /resize subresource, but for specifically mem-backed volumes, the volume is considered part of the pod's memory
This kep in particular avoids the concurrency/coordination problem by restricting this to only emptyDir types.
If the volume shrink fails (usage > limit), we abort the transaction before shrinking cgroups.
I'm not sure that we want to 'generically' represent it... We could theoretically add a top-level VolumeStatus.Capacity field

summary: KEP-6035 (Exec session identity propagation, sig-node) is implementable at alpha. It proposes letting the API server inject an audit ID, exposed as an environment variable (KUBERNETES_EXEC_AUDIT_ID), into exec sessions so runtime tools can correlate in-session activity with API audit logs. The KEP was merged with KEP-6090 into a single KEP, per the discussion.
rationale: The discussion says interactive kubectl exec sessions are not visible in audit logs beyond the initial connect event, so a correlation key must reach the runtime layer. Reviewers pushed back on the design: sigtrapd said the audit ID is API-server-set and overrides user input, while others questioned whether env vars (vs. headers or baggage) are the right carrier and whether generic user env vars are safe. Status is implementable at alpha; the record does not show a final approval of the API review, which was still pending.
alternatives: OpenTelemetry baggage rendered into prefixed env vars — Discussion says baggage would still render into prefixed env vars at the process boundary, so the outcome is the same with extra indirection; sergeykanzhelev said it may be better only if generic env vars are removed.

Reject user-supplied KUBERNETES_* env entries via API validation (Option A) — Proposed as a way to resolve the distinguishability concern in the later comment, but the sources do not show it was adopted or rejected; it is described as a follow-on option by sigtrapd.

Rely on existing audit log configuration — Per the latest comment from sigtrapd, this only covers ExecSyncRequest (where the command is visible), not interactive kubectl exec sessions, which are not sent through the API server after upgrade.

API server checks kubelet version before allowing the feature — haircommander said this is not the right move, since past features did not do this; errors surfacing to cluster admins were suggested instead.

evidence.quote: The KEPs #6035 and #6090 Have been merged into one single KEP. I have addressed all the questions that were raised in the previous round of review.
On the smushing concern, the API server enforces a hard override for `KUBERNETES_EXEC_AUDIT_ID` regardless of what the user supplies
Whether this KEP will touch the CRI or not is still a question I don't know the answer to.

summary: KEP-6060 proposes authenticating API server calls to admission webhooks (and related aggregated-server callers) using short-lived service account tokens minted via TokenRequest, bound to an APIService or a webhook configuration. The KEP is marked implementable at alpha stage for v1.37.
rationale: Webhooks currently need to verify callers by calling back to kube-apiserver (TokenReview or SubjectAccessReview), and the design aims to avoid that. The authorization check moves to token issuance, so the webhook only inspects claims in the token. Reviewers pushed for fewer tokens (one per client per webhook, cached and renewed) and for narrowly scoped "attest" permissions. The discussion records the leads' decision to allow bindings to APIService or to either WebhookConfiguration type, with "attest" on "*" required only for webhook-config bindings.
alternatives: Bind tokens to the webhook configuration or Service/CRD instead of an APIService — Reviewer liggitt asked whether this would make more sense, but pmengelbert answered that with webhook configurations as the bound object, kube-apiserver cannot perform the same authorization check without calling back to kube-apiserver. The team kept APIService binding and added webhook-configuration bindings as an option.

Mint a token per webhook invocation or per group/version per webhook — Reviewers objected that it would be too many tokens. The agreed approach is to cache each token until expiry and refresh it then.

Randomize the kube-apiserver service account name — liggitt said built-in service account names are not randomized elsewhere and the idea was more confusing than helpful. ahmedtd and enj raised the open question of a fixed name like system:serviceaccount:kube-system:kube-apiserver, and it was left open.

Use a wildcard APIService as the bound object for kube-apiserver — pmengelbert proposed it first, then the team preferred allowing bindings to a WebhookConfiguration type instead of a wildcard APIService.

evidence.quote: Support 3 types of bindings: - `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` - `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` - `APIService` When either of the webhook configurations is used as the bound object
In order to avoid the webhook talking back to `kube-apiserver` for `TokenReview` or `SubjectAccessReview`. This is all done to prevent aggregated API servers from probing policy information
I think we landed on not needing both feature gates because we can ensure that an old API server will never honor these incorrectly.
The main PR for 1.37 merged last week (before code freeze): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140113 The rest are deferred until 1.38 per discussion with Sig AUTH.

summary: KEP-6063 adds a per-pod PID limit (spec.resources.limits.pids) at Pod level, enforced by the kubelet via the pod cgroup pids.max, behind a new PerPodPIDLimit feature gate. Status is implementable, stage alpha.
rationale: Pods that need more PIDs than the node-wide podPidsLimit (for example a sidecar such as Envoy, or agent pods that should be more constrained) cannot set their own pool today. The KEP extends the Pod-level resources stanza from KEP-2837 to PIDs, with the effective limit being min(podPidsLimit, spec.resources.limits.pids). Requests for PIDs are forbidden, since scheduler-side accounting of dynamic PID usage was judged too complex for this scope.
alternatives: Requests-based PID accounting in the scheduler — Scoped out: "Adding support for requests would mean the scheduler needs to check if the node can accommodate the pod. This gets complicated because the number of PIDs in use at the exact moment the scheduler evaluates the node is highly dynamic."
Container-level PID limits — Decided to start with pod-level: "the decision was to start with pod-level. ... Adding per-container would add complexity for Alpha."

NRI plugin (annotation-based) or PriorityClass-based approaches — Listed as alternatives in the Alternatives section; the sources do not give a detailed reason for rejecting them beyond their being alternatives.
Using nproc in ulimit (KEP-5758) — "since ulimit does not operate at the cgroup level, we decided not to pursue this implementation in KEP-5758."

evidence.quote: This KEP extends that same API to add PID limits This KEP has a dependency on the `PodLevelResources` featuregate which enabled by default now.
So the effective limit is min(podPidsLimit, spec.resources.limits.pid) — the lower value wins.
We scoped this to a kubelet change and therefore restricted it to limits alone, which are enforced via cgroups.
the decision was to start with pod-level. I n cgroupsv2, the PID controller is set at the pod cgroup (pids.max)

Addressed the feedback by integrating Node Declared Features (KEP-5328) into the KEP, including design details, version skew handling, dependency documentation, and unit/e2e test coverage for feature declaration and scheduler filtering.

summary: KEP-6072 standardizes a `numaNode` device attribute for DRA, with a list form (via KEP-5491) and a scalar fallback, plus deviceattribute library helpers. It is implementable at stage stable with no feature gate; drivers choose list or scalar form through their own configuration.

The list form and intersection matching depend on DRAListTypeAttributes (KEP-5491), so the KEP has no gate of its own. Reviewers agreed drivers decide what they publish and Kubernetes stays unaware, so the KEP went directly to stable with no feature gate.
alternatives: Add a DRAStandardNUMANode feature gate with alpha/beta graduation — Reviewer pohly preferred option 1: "DRA drivers decide what they publish, Kubernetes remains unaware." and noted that without a gate nothing would use it, so the gate was dropped.

Runtime dry-run probe to detect whether DRAListTypeAttributes is enabled — pohly said dynamic feature discovery is "too fragile", and the agreed approach is an operator-set listEnabled config with a fatal error on mismatch.

Ship as alpha, with the PRR filled out for alpha — kannon92 argued that without a gate alpha/beta/stable mean nothing; the outcome from Slack was to go directly to stable. johnahull's earlier alpha proposal was superseded.
Use a dedicated maturity-tagged attribute name or a staging registry for experimental attributes — Raised by swatisehgal as a question; the sources do not record a decision adopting it.

KEP is going directly to stable. - PRR is not really relevant here. Feel free to mark NA for areas that you don't think are relevant.

the numaNode helper would take a `listEnabled` input that the operator sets on the driver to match what the cluster has enabled
No `DRAStandardNUMANode` feature gate. Drivers decide what they publish and Kubernetes stays unaware (option 1).

summary: KEP-6080 proposes a `derivedAttributes` field on DRA devices, where each entry is a CEL expression over a device's properties that yields an extra attribute usable in constraints such as matchAttribute. The KEP is currently provisional at alpha stage.
rationale: Standardizing hardware attribute names in DRA is slow, so users cannot constrain on attributes that drivers do not publish under standard names. Derived attributes let users compute such attributes via CEL from existing attributes, with no driver implementation work. Reviewers agreed to keep constraints unchanged and add only the derivedAttributes field, and to keep derived attributes out of CEL device selectors for now.
outcome_reason: The sources do not give a final reason for the provisional status. The history shows the KEP missed the enhancements freeze after the release team was asked for an exception, which the sources record as "evaluating" with the KEP removed from the milestone.
alternatives: Change the constraints section so derived attributes get their own matching semantics — johnbelamaric said 'We should not change the constraints. These should just look like any other attribute to the entire constraints section. The only API addition needed should be the `derivedAttributes` field.'

Use derived attributes inside CELDeviceSelector expressions (device.derivedAttributes map or injecting into device.attributes) — gauravkghildiyal said it was 'intentionally did not include in this KEP' because it 'brings additional complexities, such as how they impact performance by forcing early evaluation'; a different KEP is suggested for that.

Migrate pcieRoot from a scalar to list(string) in place under the same attribute name — gauravkghildiyal argued 'It's gonna be extremely difficult for DRA Driver to directly change pcieRoot from a single element to a list type without breaking users', and proposed a separate pcieRoots attribute instead.

Use a 'Option 2' FQDN-based naming for standard attributes — aojea said Option 2 'will break existing users of the well defined pcieRoot standard attribute'; the discussion favored Option 1 (allow FQDNs) as the recommended approach.

evidence.quote: We should not change the constraints. These should just look like any other attribute to the entire constraints section.
Forcing users to only be able to constraint match on 'standard attributes' is very limiting. The pace of defining 'standard attributes' can never keep up
I'd rather avoid introducing this change without more careful consideration. If this usability experience is needed in the future, a different KEP would be a perfect opportunity
This KEP has filed an exception, the release team is evaluating and will be added back to the milestone after a consensus.

summary: KEP-6089 defines the shared Workload/PodGroup scheduling building-block API types (policy, constraints, disruption, resource claims) under the scheduling API group, with a versioned workloadbuilder helper library that translates them into Workload objects. Status: implementable, alpha.
rationale: Higher-level controllers (Job, JobSet, etc.) need to express scheduling intent for Workload objects without duplicating the types. The discussion settled on granular, purpose-oriented building-block types that APIs embed, with a helper library doing a pass-through translation, so that new fields flow through when libraries are upgraded. Reviewers agreed TopologyConstraint should be shared with PodGroup rather than duplicated, and that validation lives in the library. Naming and default-handling were still being debated in the review thread.
alternatives: Reuse the full PodSpec-like or PodGroup structures directly in every controller API — The discussion noted that reusing existing structures and embedding them elsewhere hit the problems the authors wanted to avoid; a separate sibling structure was chosen for this purpose. The reviewer also said embedding PodSpec everywhere is less appealing than granular building blocks.

Duplicate TopologyConstraint as WorkloadTopologyConstraint — Reviewer wojtek-t argued the topology concept reflects the real world and cannot diverge from PodGroup, so it should be shared; the authors agreed and TopologyConstraint is now shared.

Per-node defaulting via a single DefaultGangMinCount field or a list of callbacks — Discussion considered these but reviewers found them awkward: a Basic and Gang policy at once is semantically odd, and a field proliferation or callback list was debated. No final resolution is recorded in the sources.
Owner-reference-only mechanism for lifecycle delegation — wojtek-t said owner references alone cannot express the three ownership states, so annotations are needed in addition to owner references.

evidence.quote: the `TopologyConstraint` should actually be shared (we shouldn't introduce WorkloadTopologyConstraint here) - because that's a concept that reflects the topology
We introduce entirely new API group with all the share-able APIs, and then the library will be responsible for translating that into the core scheduling primitives.
they are intended to map in a ~pass-through way to creation of Workload objects
So the mechanism isn't OwnerReference-based. It should be based on the annotations that are described below
The status of this enhancement is marked as `At risk for enhancements freeze`.

summary: KEP-6122 proposes a node-level configurable delay before the kubelet actuates a CPU scale-down for exclusive-CPU containers, plus exposing the assigned cpuset via the Downward API so workloads can prepare. The KEP is now implementable at alpha stage, approved by sig-node lead dchen1107 for alpha1 only, with alpha2 (not beta) expected next.
rationale: Scaling down exclusive CPUs takes effect immediately, so workloads have no heads-up to move work off CPUs being removed. The KEP delays the cpuset actuation and exposes the about-to-be-applied cpuset to the workload through the Downward API. Reviewers accepted the design for alpha because it is opt-in and unblocks user feedback, while raising concerns about node-wide impact, Downward API coupling, and restart races that are deferred to alpha2.
alternatives: Releasing CPUs in reverse order of allocation (LIFO) — Rejected in sig-node meeting per the author; the KEP keeps the Original cpuset allocated at container creation so promised CPUs are never removed from the actuated set.

Releasing CPUs based on usage during scale-down — Raised by sig-node as a significant deviation from the current design; discussion recorded in the issue but no rationale for rejection is given in the sources beyond the author's statement that the delay approach was chosen.
Node Declared Features as an opt-out mechanism — Removed from being an opt-out option and added to rejected alternatives, per the KEP update.
Hook-based approach / pod-level API — Suggested by reviewers (ffromani, dchen1107, natasha41575) but deferred to alpha2/beta for evaluation rather than adopted for alpha1.

evidence.quote: Therefore, summing all together I think I can add a provisional LGTM under the *strict* condition that next cycle we get alpha2, not beta
/lgtm for alpha1 to unblock the progress so that we can collect the real inputs from the users.
mitigation in alpha by recommending operators to taint nodes with feature enabled - extension to be investigated in alpha2/beta to set up taints or use Node Declared Features

I am inclined to accept this for alpha and accept the workaround for alpha to unblock the progress and receive the user feedbacks earlier, but strongly suggest we have alpha 2 to think through pod level API.

summary: KEP-6132 proposes a PreQueueingHint extension point in the kube-scheduler: a plugin can pre-filter which unschedulable pods a cluster event could make schedulable, so the scheduler does not run QueueingHints for every unschedulable pod. The KEP is currently implementable at stage alpha.
rationale: The motivating problem is a thundering herd of pods (e.g., thousands of DRA pods created with ResourceClaimTemplates at once) that all get re-evaluated on each claim event. A reviewer's scheduler_perf run showed throughput rising from about 297 to about 711 pods/s with the feature on, which the reviewer called worthwhile. Review raised open concerns: a second pod referencing a generated claim, PodGroup membership lookup, and whether the async ResourceClaim queue should be separate.
outcome_reason: The sources give the status as implementable, stage alpha, but also show the KEP was later marked tracked/no and had a release exception filed on 2026-07-23 with the release team evaluating it. The sources do not state the final outcome of that exception request.
alternatives: Periodic sweep of the unschedulable queue to rescue missed pods — Reviewer noted it causes an unpredictable, potentially long delay for pods such as a second pod sharing a claim, and questioned whether the sweep is meant to go away.

Maintain a pod informer index mapping ResourceClaims to referencing pods — Described as more expensive, but the author adopted an informer-based approach in the KEP update on 2026-06-09 after the reviewer's patch showed it working.

Ship the asynchronous ResourceClaim event queue together with PreQueueingHint — Benchmarking showed no throughput benefit and about 18% less CPU for scheduling; the author said they were open to dropping it, and reviewers asked for it to have a separate feature gate.

evidence.quote: No throughput benefit from the async queue. Profiling shows ~18% reduction in CPU available for scheduling due to worker goroutine overhead.
I think both should have separate feature gates. Then one can be turned off without affecting the other. A single KEP seems sufficient.
This KEP has filed an exception, the release team is evaluating and will be added back to the milestone after a consensus.
We can't break such a usage and cause the second pod to not get scheduled.

summary: KEP-6164 proposes eliminating Kubernetes internal API types by making the internal (hub) type memory-identical to the preferred served version, to remove costly conversions. Status is implementable, stage stable, and the change is treated as unconditionally on with no feature gate.
rationale: Conversion between internal and external API objects allocates new objects on every request, which drives memory spikes during bulk operations such as LIST and relist after apiserver restarts. The author's experiment showed memory-identical types cut allocations sharply (for 1000 pods, 21,005 allocs to 5 allocs). Because the change is internal-only and cannot be feature gated, SIG leads agreed to mark it stable on its first release, with a go/no-go checkpoint within two releases.
alternatives: Fully remove the internal type concept now and use the versioned hub everywhere — Reviewers (liggitt) objected that this would lose the benefit of a decoupled internal type during alpha/beta development. The author then split the work into phases and focused 1.37 on making the internal type memory-identical with the preferred version, leaving the broader question for another day.

Gate the change behind a feature gate and launch as alpha — The author said it is an internal-only change to how Go source is managed and cannot be feature gated; SIG leads chose to mark it stable on the first release, as was done for the gogo dependency KEP.

Type-alias stable versions as the internal version only, instead of changing all types — This was proposed by liggitt as a narrower plan and the author accepted scoping down to it; it is not an alternative the sources reject, but it was folded into the phased plan rather than chosen as a separate path.

evidence.quote: I've split this into two phases where the first one focuses on making the internal type memory identical with the preferred served type.
I've updated this to commit to a go/no-go decision within 2 releases. Either we've migrated some easy cases + pod + CRD or we'll revert the change.
Type aliasing stable versions as the internal version seems reasonable.
This suggests that even *before* we invest in aliases, there is a big performance boost for making the internal types memory-identical with the preferred version.

summary: KEP-6178 (Concurrent Watch Object Decode, sig-api-machinery) is at status implementable, stage beta. It proposes decoding watch objects concurrently; the implementation PR kubernetes/kubernetes#139679 was merged before code freeze, which let the KEP be tracked for code freeze in v1.37.
rationale: The KEP was at risk for enhancements freeze until its readme/PRR PR (kubernetes/enhancements#6179) was resolved, and it was then tracked for enhancements freeze. At code freeze the enhancement was first removed from the v1.37 milestone because implementation PRs were not merge-ready, then re-added after PR #139679 merged with an updated description. The stated benefit is from a Kueue user: the previous behavior caused a boot incident, and benchmarks show about 3.4x more workloads processed.
alternatives: Leave the KEP out of v1.37 after code freeze — The sources show it was re-added to the v1.37 milestone after PR kubernetes/kubernetes#139679 merged with an updated description, so it was not left out.
Track total active decode goroutines as the observability metric — Jefftree preferred a gauge, stating 'I added a gauge for apiserver_watch_decode_inflight' instead of describing goroutines.

Use queue depth or delay as the observability signal for decode — Jefftree said queue delay already exists via logs: 'when decoder is falling behind and crosses a threshold' a block logger records it.

evidence.quote: Pertaining to the concerned PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139679 being merged and with an updated description, this KEP is now marked as `Tracked for code freeze`.
the implementation (code-related) PRs associated with this enhancement are not in the merge-ready state by code-freeze and hence this enhancement is now removed from the v1.37 milestone.
I added a gauge for `apiserver_watch_decode_inflight`. (b) exists already via logs.
the previous behavior caused us an incident as reported here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136950 where Kueue could not boot up.
